1.1: Blessed is the man that doeth not walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in ye seat of the scornefull:
1.2: But his delite is in the Law of the Lord, and in his Law doeth he meditate day and night.
1.3: For he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of waters, that will bring foorth her fruit in due season: whose leaf shall not fade: so whatsoever he shall doe, shall prosper.
1.4: The wicked are not so, but as the chaff, which the wind driveth away.
1.5: Therefore the wicked shall not stand in the iudgement, nor sinners in the assemblie of the righteous.
1.6: For the Lord knoweth the way of the righteous, and the way of the wicked shall perish.

2.1: Why doe the heathen rage, and the people murmur in vain?
2.2: The Kings of the earth band themselves, and the princes are assembled together against the Lord, and against his Christ.
2.3: Let us break their bands, and cast their cordes from us.
2.4: But he that dwelleth in the heaven, shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in derision.
2.5: Then shall hee speak unto them in his wrath, and vex them in his sore displeasure, saying,
2.6: Even I have set my King upon Zion mine holy mountain.
2.7: I will declare the decree: that is, the Lord hath said unto me, Thou art my Sonne: this day have I begotten thee.
2.8: Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the endes of the earth for thy possession.
2.9: Thou shalt krush them with a scepter of yron, and break them in pieces like a potters vessell.
2.10: Be wise now therefore, ye Kings: be learned ye Judges of the earth.
2.11: Serve the Lord in fear, and reioyce in trembling.
2.12: Kiss the sonne, least he be angry, and ye perish in the way, when his wrath shall suddenly burn. blessed are all that trust in him.

3.1: A Psalm of David, when he fled from his sonne Absalom. Lord, how are mine adversaries increased? how many rise against me?
3.2: Many say to my soul, There is no help for him in God. Selah.
3.3: But thou Lord art a buckler for me: my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.
3.4: I did call unto the Lord with my voyce, and he heard me out of his holy mountain. Selah.
3.5: I layed me down and slept, and rose up again: for the Lord susteined me.
3.6: I will not be afrayde for ten thousand of the people, that should beset me round about.
3.7: O Lord, arise: help me, my God: for thou hast smitten all mine enemies upon the cheek bone: thou hast broken the teeth of the wicked.
3.8: Salvation belongeth unto the Lord, and thy blessing is upon thy people. Selah.

4.1: To him that excelleth on Neginoth. A Psalm of David. Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousnes: thou hast set me at libertie, when I was in distress: have mercie upon me and hearken unto my prayer.
4.2: O ye sonnes of men, how long will yee turn my glory into shame, loving vanitie, and seeking lyes? Selah.
4.3: For be ye sure that the Lord hath chosen to himself a godly man: the Lord will hear when I call unto him.
4.4: Tremble, and sinne not: examine your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.
4.5: Offer the sacrifices of righteousnes, and trust in the Lord.
4.6: Many say, Who will shew us any good? but Lord, lift up the light of thy countenance upon us.
4.7: Thou hast given mee more ioye of heart, then they have had, when their wheat and their wine did abound.
4.8: I will lay mee down, and also sleep in peace: for thou, Lord, onely makest me dwell in safetie.

5.1: To him that excelleth upon Nehiloth. A Psalm of David. Hear my wordes, O Lord: vnderstande my meditation.
5.2: Hearken unto the voyce of my crie, my King and my God: for unto thee doe I pray.
5.3: Hear my voyce in the morning, O Lord: for in the morning will I direct me unto thee, and I will wait.
5.4: For thou art not a God that loveth wickednes: neither shall evil dwell with thee.
5.5: The foolish shall not stand in thy sight: for thou hatest all them that work iniquitie.
5.6: Thou shalt destroy them that speak lyes: the Lord will abhorre the bloodie man and deceitful.
5.7: But I wil come into thine house in the multitude of thy mercie: and in thy fear will I worship toward thine holy Temple.
5.8: Lead me, O Lord, in thy righteousnes, because of mine enemies: make thy way plain before my face.
5.9: For no constancie is in their mouth: within, they are very corruption: their throte is an open sepulchre, and they flatter with their tongue.
5.10: Destroy them, O God: let them fall from their counsels: cast them out for the multitude of their iniquities, because they have rebelled against thee.
5.11: And let all them that trust in thee, reioyce and triumph for ever, and cover thou them: and let them, that love thy Name, reioyce in thee.
5.12: For thou Lord wilt bless the righteous, and with fauour wilt compass him, as with a shield.

6.1: To him that excelleth on Neginoth upon the eith tune. A Psalm of David. O lord, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chastise me in thy wrath.
6.2: Have mercie upon me, O Lord, for I am weak: O Lord heal me, for my bones are vexed.
6.3: My soul is also sore troubled: but Lord how long wilt thou delay?
6.4: Return, O Lord: deliver my soul: save me for thy mercies sake.
6.5: For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall prayse thee?
6.6: I fainted in my mourning: I cause my bed every night to swimme, and water my couch with my teares.
6.7: Mine eye is dimmed for despight, and sunk in because of all mine enemies.
6.8: Away from mee all ye workers of iniquitie: for the Lord hath heard the voyce of my weeping.
6.9: The Lord hath heard my petition: the Lord will receive my prayer.
6.10: All mine enemies shall be confounded and sore vexed: they shall be turned back, and put to shame suddenly.

7.1: Shigaion of David, which he sang unto the Lord, concerning the wordes of Chush the sonne of Iemini. O Lord my God, in thee I put my trust: save me from all that persecute me, and deliver me,
7.2: Least he deuoure my soul like a lion, and tear it in pieces, while there is none to help.
7.3: O Lord my God, if I have done this thing, if there be any wickednes in mine handes,
7.4: If I have rewarded evil unto him that had peace with mee, (yea I have delivered him that vexed me without cause)
7.5: Then let the enemie persecute my soul and take it: yea, let him tread my life down upon the earth, and lay mine honour in the dust. Selah.
7.6: Arise, O Lord, in thy wrath, and lift up thy self against the rage of mine enemies, and awake for mee according to the iudgement that thou hast appointed.
7.7: So shall the Congregation of the people compass thee about: for their sakes therefore return on hie.
7.8: The Lord shall judge the people: Judge thou me, O Lord, according to my righteousness, and according to mine innocencie, that is in mee.
7.9: Oh let the malice of the wicked come to an end: but guide thou the just: for the righteous God trieth the hearts and reines.
7.10: My defence is in God, who preserveth the upright in heart.
7.11: God judgeth the righteous, and him that contemneth God every day.
7.12: Except he turn, he hath whet his sword: he hath bent his bow and made it readie.
7.13: Hee hath also prepared him deadly weapons: hee will ordeine his arrowes for them that persecute me.
7.14: Behold, hee shall travail with wickednes: for he hath conceived mischief, but he shall bring foorth a lye.
7.15: Hee hath made a pitte and digged it, and is fallen into the pit that he made.
7.16: His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his crueltie shall fall upon his own pate.
7.17: I wil praise the Lord according to his righteousnes, and will sing praise to the Name of the Lord most high.

8.1: To him that excelleth on Gittith. A Psalm of David. O Lord our Lord, how excellent is thy Name in all the world! which hast set thy glory above the heavens.
8.2: Out of the mouth of babes and suckelings hast thou ordeined strength, because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemie and the avenger.
8.3: When I behold thine heavens, even the workes of thy fingers, the moon and the starres which thou hast ordeined,
8.4: What is man, say I, that thou art mindefull of him? and the sonne of man, that thou visitest him?
8.5: For thou hast made him a little lower then God, and crowned him with glory and worship.
8.6: Thou hast made him to have dominion in the workes of thine hands: thou hast put all things under his feet:
8.7: All sheep and oxen: yea, and the beastes of the field:
8.8: The foules of the ayre, and the fish of the sea, and that which passeth through the paths of the seas.
8.9: O Lord our Lord, how excellent is thy Name in all the world!

9.1: To him that excelleth upon Muth Laben. A Psalm of David. I will praise the Lord with my whole heart: I will speak of all thy marueilous workes.
9.2: I will bee glad, and reioyce in thee: I will sing praise to thy Name, O most High,
9.3: For that mine enemies are turned back: they shall fall, and perish at thy presence.
9.4: For thou hast maintained my right and my cause: thou art set in the throne, and judgest right.
9.5: Thou hast rebuked the heathen: thou hast destroyed the wicked: thou hast put out their name for ever and ever.
9.6: O enemie, destructions are come to a perpetual end, and thou hast destroyed the cities: their memorial is perished with them.
9.7: But the Lord shall sit for ever: hee hath prepared his throne for iudgement.
9.8: For he shall judge the world in righteousnes, and shall judge the people with equitie.
9.9: The Lord also wil be a refuge for the poor, a refuge in due time, even in affliction.
9.10: And they that know thy Name, will trust in thee: for thou, Lord, hast not failed them that seek thee.
9.11: Sing praises to the Lord, which dwelleth in Zion: shew the people his workes.
9.12: For whe he maketh inquisition for blood, hee remembreth it, and forgetteth not the complaint of the poor.
9.13: Have mercie upon mee, O Lord: consider my trouble which I suffer of them that hate mee, thou that liftest me up from the gates of death,
9.14: That I may shew all thy praises within the gates of the daughter of Zion, and reioyce in thy salvation.
9.15: The heathen are sunken down in the pit that they made: in the nette that they hid, is their foot taken.
9.16: The Lord is knowen by executing iudgement: the wicked is snared in the work of his own handes. Higgaion. Selah.
9.17: The wicked shall turn into hell, and all nations that forget God.
9.18: For the poor shall not bee alway forgotten: the hope of the afflicted shall not perish for ever.
9.19: Up Lord: let not man prevail: let the heathen be judged in thy sight.
9.20: Put them in fear, O Lord, that the heathen may know that they are but men. Selah.

10.1: Why standest thou far off, O Lord, and hidest thee in due time, even in affliction?
10.2: The wicked with pride doeth persecute the poor: let them be taken in the craftes that they have imagined.
10.3: For the wicked hath made boast of his own heartes desire, and the couetous blesseth himself: he contemneth the Lord.
10.4: The wicked is so proud that hee seeketh not for God: hee thinketh alwayes, There is no God.
10.5: His wayes alway prosper: thy iudgements are hie above his sight: therefore defieth he all his enemies.
10.6: He saith in his heart, I shall never be moved, nor be in danger.
10.7: His mouth is full of cursing and deceit and fraud: under his tongue is mischief and iniquitie.
10.8: He lieth in wait in the villages: in the secret places doeth hee murder the innocent: his eyes are bent against the poor.
10.9: He lyeth in wait secretly, even as a lyon in his denne: he lyeth in wait to spoyle the poor: he doeth spoyle the poor, when he draweth him into his net.
10.10: He croucheth and boweth: therefore heaps of the poor doe fall by his might.
10.11: He hath said in his heart, God hath forgotten, he hideth away his face, and will never see.
10.12: Arise, O Lord God: lift up thine hand: forget not the poor.
10.13: Wherefore doeth the wicked contemn God? he saith in his heart, Thou wilt not regard.
10.14: Yet thou hast seen it: for thou beholdest mischief and wrong, that thou mayest take it into thine handes: the poor committeth himself unto thee: for thou art the helper of the fatherless.
10.15: Break thou the arm of the wicked and malicious: search his wickednes, and thou shalt find none.
10.16: The Lord is King for ever and ever: the heathen are destroyed foorth of his land.
10.17: Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the poor: thou preparest their heart: thou bendest thine ear to them,
10.18: To judge the fatherless and poor, that earthly man cause to fear no more.

11.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. In the Lord put I my trust: how say yee then to my soul, Flee to your mountain as a bird?
11.2: For loe, the wicked bend their bow, and make readie their arrowes upon the string, that they may secretly shoot at them, which are upright in heart.
11.3: For the foundations are cast down: what hath the righteous done?
11.4: The Lord is in his holy palace: the Lordes throne is in the heaven: his eyes wil consider: his eye lids will try the children of men.
11.5: The Lord will try the righteous: but the wicked and him that loveth iniquitie, doeth his soul hate.
11.6: Upon the wicked he shall rain snares, fire, and brimstone, and stormie tempest: this is the porcion of their cup.
11.7: For the righteous Lord loveth righteousnes: his countenance doeth behold the just.

12.1: To him that excelleth upon the eight tune. A Psalm of David. Help Lord, for there is not a godly man left: for the faithful are fayled from among the children of men.
12.2: They speak deceitfully every one with his neighbour, flattering with their lips, and speak with a double heart.
12.3: The Lord cut off all flattering lippes, and the tongue that speaketh proud things:
12.4: Which have said, With our tongue will we prevail: our lippes are our own: who is Lord over us?
12.5: Now for the oppression of the needy, and for the sighes of the poor, I will up, sayeth the Lord, and will set at libertie him, whom the wicked hath snared.
12.6: The wordes of the Lord are pure wordes, as the silver, tried in a fornace of earth, fined seven fold.
12.7: Thou wilt keep them, O Lord: thou wilt preserve him from this generation for ever.
12.8: The wicked walk on every side: when they are exalted, it is a shame for the sonnes of men.

13.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. How long wilt thou forget me, O Lord, for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
13.2: How long shall I take counsel within my self, having weariness dayly in mine heart? how long shall mine enemie be exalted above me?
13.3: Behold, and hear mee, O Lord my God: lighten mine eyes, that I sleep not in death:
13.4: Lest mine enemie say, I have prevailed against him: and they that afflict me, reioyce when I slide.
13.5: But I trust in thy mercie: mine heart shall reioyce in thy salvation: I will sing to the Lord, because he hath delt louingly with me.

14.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God: they have corrupted, and done an abominable work: there is none that doeth good.
14.2: The Lord looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that would understand, and seek God.
14.3: All are gone out of the way: they are all corrupt: there is none that doeth good, no not one.
14.4: Doe not all the workers of iniquitie know that they eat up my people, as they eat bread? they call not upon the Lord.
14.5: There they shall be taken with fear, because God is in the generation of the just.
14.6: You have made a mock at the counsel of the poor, because the Lord is his trust.
14.7: Oh give salvation unto Israel out of Zion: when the Lord turneth the captiuitie of his people, then Iaakob shall reioyce, and Israel shall be glad.

15.1: A Psalm of David. Lord, who shall dwell in thy Tabernacle? who shall rest in thine holy Mountain?
15.2: He that walketh uprightly and worketh righteousnes, and speaketh the trueth in his heart.
15.3: He that slandereth not with his tongue, nor doeth evil to his neighbour, nor receiveth a false report against his neighbour.
15.4: In whose eyes a vile person is contemned, but he honoureth them that fear the Lord: he that sweareth to his own hinderance and changeth not.
15.5: He that giveth not his money unto vsurie, nor taketh reward against the innocent: hee that doeth these things, shall never be moved.

16.1: Michtam of David. Preserve mee, O God: for in thee doe I trust.
16.2: O my soul, thou hast sayd unto the Lord, Thou art my Lord: my weldoing extendeth not to thee,
16.3: But to the Saints that are in the earth, and to the excellent: all my delite is in them.
16.4: The sorowes of them, that offer to an other god, shall be multiplied: their offerings of blood will I not offer, neither make mention of their names with my lips.
16.5: The Lord is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: thou shalt mainteine my lot.
16.6: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places: yea, I have a fair heritage.
16.7: I wil prayse the Lord, who hath given me counsel: my reines also teach me in the nightes.
16.8: I have set the Lord alwayes before me: for hee is at my right hand: therefore I shall not slide.
16.9: Wherefore mine heart is glad and my tongue reioyceth: my flesh also doeth rest in hope.
16.10: For thou wilt not leave my soul in the grave: neither wilt thou suffer thine holy one to see corruption.
16.11: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is the fulness of joy: and at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.

17.1: The prayer of David. Hear the right, O Lord, consider my cry: hearken unto my prayer of lips vnfained.
17.2: Let my sentence come forth from thy presence, and let thine eyes behold equitie.
17.3: Thou hast prooued and visited mine heart in the night: thou hast tryed me, and foundest nothing: for I was purposed that my mouth should not offend.
17.4: Concerning the workes of men, by the wordes of thy lips I kept mee from the paths of the cruel man.
17.5: Stay my steps in thy paths, that my feet doe not slide.
17.6: I have called upon thee: surely thou wilt hear me, O God: incline thine ear to me, and hearken unto my wordes.
17.7: Shew thy marueilous mercies, thou that art the Sauiour of them that trust in thee, from such as resist thy right hand.
17.8: Keep me as the apple of the eye: hide me under the shadow of thy wings,
17.9: From the wicked that oppress mee, from mine enemies, which compass me round about for my soul.
17.10: They are inclosed in their own fat, and they have spoken proudely with their mouth.
17.11: They have compassed us now in our steps: they have set their eyes to bring down to the ground:
17.12: Like as a lyon that is greedy of pray, and as it were a lyons whelp lurking in secret places.
17.13: Up Lord, disappoint him: cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked with thy sword,
17.14: From men by thine hand, O Lord, from men of the world, who have their portion in this life, whose bellies thou fillest with thine hid treasure: their children have ynough, and leave the rest of their substance for their children.
17.15: But I will behold thy face in righteousnes, and when I awake, I shalbe satisfied with thine image.

18.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David the servant of the Lord, which spake unto the Lord the wordes of this song (in the day that the Lord delivered him for the hand of all this enemies, and form the and of saul) and sayd, I will love thee dearely, O Lord my strength.
18.2: The Lord is my rock, and my fortress, and he that delivereth me, my God and my strength: in him will I trust, my shield, the horn also of my salvation, and my refuge.
18.3: I will call upon the Lord, which is worthie to be praysed: so shall I be safe from mine enemies.
18.4: The sorowes of death compassed me, and the floods of wickednes made me afraid.
18.5: The sorowes of the grave have compassed me about: the snares of death overtook me.
18.6: But in my trouble did I call upon the Lord, and cryed unto my God: he heard my voyce out of his Temple, and my cry did come before him, even into his eares.
18.7: Then the earth trembled, and quaked: the foundations also of the mountaines mooued and shook, because he was angrie.
18.8: Smoke went out at his nostrels, and a consuming fire out of his mouth: coales were kindled thereat.
18.9: He bowed the heavens also and came down, and darkenes was under his feet.
18.10: And he rode upon Cherub and did flie, and he came flying upon the wings of the wind.
18.11: He made darkenes his secret place, and his pavilion round about him, even darkenesse of waters, and cloudes of the ayre.
18.12: At the brightnes of his presence his clouds passed, haylestones and coles of fire.
18.13: The Lord also thundred in the heaven, and the Highest gave his voyce, haylestones and coales of fire.
18.14: Then hee sent out his arrowes and scattred them, and he increased lightnings and destroyed them.
18.15: And the chanels of waters were seen, and the foundations of the world were discovered at thy rebuking, O Lord, at the blasting of the breath of thy nostrels.
18.16: He hath sent down from above and taken mee: hee hath drawen mee out of many waters.
18.17: He hath delivered mee from my strong enemie, and from them which hate me: for they were too strong for me.
18.18: They prevented me in the day of my calamitie: but the Lord was my stay.
18.19: Hee brought mee foorth also into a large place: hee delivered mee because hee fauoured me.
18.20: The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousnes: according to the purenes of mine hands he recompensed me:
18.21: Because I kept the wayes of the Lord, and did not wickedly against my God.
18.22: For all his Lawes were before mee, and I did not cast away his commandements from mee.
18.23: I was upright also with him, and have kept me from my wickednes.
18.24: Therefore the Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness, and according to the purenes of mine hands in his sight.
18.25: With the godly thou wilt shew thy self godly: with the upright man thou wilt shew thy self upright.
18.26: With the pure thou wilt shew thy self pure, and with the froward thou wilt shew thy self froward.
18.27: Thus thou wilt save the poor people, and wilt cast down the proud lookes.
18.28: Surely thou wilt light my candle: the Lord my God wil lighten my darkenes.
18.29: For by thee I have broken through an host, and by my God I have leaped over a wall.
18.30: The way of God is vncorrupt: the word of the Lord is tried in the fire: he is a shield to all that trust in him.
18.31: For who is God besides the Lord? and who is mightie save our God?
18.32: God girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way upright.
18.33: He maketh my feet like hindes feet, and setteth me upon mine high places.
18.34: He teacheth mine hands to fight: so that a bow of brass is broken with mine armes.
18.35: Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation, and thy right hand hath stayed me, and thy loving kindenes hath caused me to increase.
18.36: Thou hast enlarged my steps under mee, and mine heeles have not slid.
18.37: I have pursued mine enemies, and taken them, and have not turned again till I had consumed them.
18.38: I have wounded them, that they were not able to rise: they are fallen under my feet.
18.39: For thou hast girded me with strength to battell: them, that rose against me, thou hast subdued under me.
18.40: And thou hast given me the neckes of mine enemies, that I might destroy them that hate me.
18.41: They cryed but there was none to save them, even unto the Lord, but hee answered them not.
18.42: Then I did beat them small as the dust before the wind: I did tread them flat as the clay in the streetes.
18.43: Thou hast delivered me from the contentions of the people: thou hast made me the head of the heathen: a people, whom I have not knowen, shall serve me.
18.44: As soon as they hear, they shall obey me: the strangers shall be in subiection to me.
18.45: Strangers shall shrinke away, and fear in their priuie chambers.
18.46: Let the Lord live, and blessed be my strength, and the God of my salvation be exalted.
18.47: It is God that giveth me power to avenge me, and subdueth the people under me.
18.48: O my deliverer from mine enemies, even thou hast set mee up from them, that rose against me: thou hast delivered mee from the cruel man.
18.49: Therefore I will prayse thee, O Lord, among the nations, and wil sing unto thy Name.
18.50: Great deliverances giveth hee unto his King, and sheweth mercie to his anoynted, even to David, and to his seed for ever.

19.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament sheweth ye work of his hands.
19.2: Day unto day uttereth the same, and night unto night teacheth knowledge.
19.3: There is no speach nor language, where their voyce is not heard.
19.4: Their line is gone forth through all the earth, and their words into the endes of the world: in them hath he set a tabernacle for the sunne.
19.5: Which cometh forth as a bridegrome out of his chamber, and reioyceth like a mightie man to runne his race.
19.6: His going out is from the end of the heaven, and his compass is unto the endes of ye same, and none is hid from the heat thereof.
19.7: The Law of the Lord is perfite, converting the soul: the testimonie of the Lord is sure, and giveth wisedome unto the simple.
19.8: The statutes of the Lord are right and reioyce the heart: the commandement of the Lord is pure, and giveth light unto the eyes.
19.9: The fear of the Lord is clean, and indureth for ever: the iudgements of the Lord are trueth: they are righteous altogether,
19.10: And more to be desired then gold, yea, then much fine gold: sweeter also then honie and the honie combe.
19.11: Moreover by them is thy servant made circumspect, and in keeping of them there is great reward.
19.12: Who can understand his faultes? clense me from secret fautes.
19.13: Keep thy servant also from presumptuous sinnes: let them not reign over me: so shall I be upright, and made clean from much wickednes.
19.14: Let the wordes of my mouth, and the meditation of mine heart be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, my strength, and my redeemer.

20.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble: the name of ye God of Iaakob defend thee:
20.2: Send thee help from the Sanctuarie, and strengthen thee out of Zion.
20.3: Let him remember all thine offerings, and turn thy burnt offerings into ashes. Selah:
20.4: And graunt thee according to thine heart, and fulfil all thy purpose:
20.5: That we may reioyce in thy salvation, and set up the banner in the Name of our God, when the Lord shall perform all thy petitions.
20.6: Now know I that the Lord will help his anointed, and will hear him from his Sanctuarie, by the mightie help of his right hand.
20.7: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the Name of ye Lord our God.
20.8: They are brought down and fallen, but we are risen, and stand upright.
20.9: Save Lord: let the King hear us in the day that we call.

21.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. The King shall reioyce in thy strength, O Lord: yea how greatly shall he reioyce in thy salvation!
21.2: Thou hast given him his hearts desire, and hast not denyed him the request of his lips. Selah.
21.3: For thou diddest prevent him with liberal blessings, and didest set a crown of pure gold upon his head.
21.4: He asked life of thee, and thou gavest him a long life for ever and ever.
21.5: His glory is great in thy salvation: dignitie and honour hast thou laid upon him.
21.6: For thou hast set him as blessings for ever: thou hast made him glad with the joy of thy countenance.
21.7: Because the King trusteth in the Lord, and in the mercie of the most High, he shall not slide.
21.8: Thine hand shall find out all thine enemies, and thy right hand shall find out them that hate thee.
21.9: Thou shalt make them like a fierie oven in time of thine anger: the Lord shall destroy them in his wrath, and the fire shall deuoure them.
21.10: Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed from the children of men.
21.11: For they intended evil against thee, and imagined mischief, but they shall not prevail.
21.12: Therefore shalt thou put them apart, and the strings of thy bow shalt thou make readie against their faces.
21.13: Be thou exalted, O Lord, in thy strength: so will we sing and prayse thy power.

22.1: To him that excelleth upon Aiieleth Hasshahar. A Psalm of David. My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me, and art so far from mine health, and from the wordes of my roaring?
22.2: O my God, I crie by day, but thou hearest not, and by night, but have no audience.
22.3: But thou art holy, and doest inhabit the prayses of Israel.
22.4: Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didest deliver them.
22.5: They called upon thee, and were delivered: they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.
22.6: But I am a worm, and not a man: a shame of men, and the contempt of the people.
22.7: All they that see me, have me in derision: they make a mowe and nod the head, saying,
22.8: He trusted in the Lord, let him deliver him: let him save him, seeing he loveth him.
22.9: But thou didest draw me out of ye womb: thou gavest me hope, even at my mothers breasts.
22.10: I was cast upon thee, even from ye womb: thou art my God from my mothers belly.
22.11: Be not far from me, because trouble is neere: for there is none to help me.
22.12: Many yong bulles have compassed me: mightie bulles of Bashan have closed me about.
22.13: They gap upon me with their mouthes, as a ramping and roaring lyon.
22.14: I am like water powred out, and all my bones are out of ioynt: mine heart is like wax: it is molten in the middes of my bowels.
22.15: My strength is dryed up like a potsheard, and my tongue cleaveth to my iawes, and thou hast brought me into the dust of death.
22.16: For dogges have compassed me, and the assemblie of the wicked have inclosed me: they perced mine hands and my feet.
22.17: I may tell all my bones: yet they behold, and look upon me.
22.18: They part my garments among them, and cast lottes upon my vesture.
22.19: But be thou not far off, O Lord, my strength: hasten to help me.
22.20: Deliver my soul from the sword: my desolate soul from the power of the dogge.
22.21: Save me from the lyons mouth, and answer me in saving me from the hornes of the vnicornes.
22.22: I wil declare thy Name unto my brethren: in the middes of the Congregation will I praise thee, saying,
22.23: Prayse the Lord, ye that fear him: magnifie ye him, all the seed of Iaakob, and fear ye him, all the seed of Israel.
22.24: For he hath not despised nor abhorred ye affliction of the poor: neither hath he hid his face from him, but when he called unto him, he heard.
22.25: My prayse shalbe of thee in the great Congregation: my vowes will I perfourme before them that fear him.
22.26: The poor shall eat and be satisfied: they that seek after the Lord, shall prayse him: your heart shall live for ever.
22.27: All the endes of the world shall remember themselves, and turn to the Lord: and all the kinreds of the nations shall worship before thee.
22.28: For the kingdom is the Lords, and he ruleth among the nations.
22.29: All they that be fat in the earth, shall eat and worship: all they that go down into the dust, shall bow before him, even he that cannot quicken his own soul.
22.30: Their seed shall serve him: it shalbe counted unto the Lord for a generation.
22.31: They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be borne, because he hath done it.

23.1: A Psalm of David. The Lord is my shepheard, I shall not want.
23.2: He maketh me to rest in green pasture, and leadeth me by the still waters.
23.3: He restoreth my soul, and leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his Names sake.
23.4: Yea, though I should walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me: thy rod and thy staff, they comfort me.
23.5: Thou doest prepare a table before me in the sight of mine adversaries: thou doest anoynt mine head with oyle, and my cuppe runneth over.
23.6: Doubtless kindness and mercie shall follow me all the dayes of my life, and I shall remain a long season in the house of the Lord.

24.1: A Psalm of David. The earth is the Lordes, and all that therein is: the world and they that dwell therein.
24.2: For he hath founded it upon the seas: and established it upon the floods.
24.3: Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord? and who shall stand in his holy place?
24.4: Even he that hath innocent handes, and a pure heart: which hath not lift up his mind unto vanitie, nor sworn deceitfully.
24.5: He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.
24.6: This is the generation of them that seek him, of them that seek thy face, this is Iaakob. Selah.
24.7: Lift up your heads ye gates, and be ye lift up ye everlasting doores, and the King of glory shall come in.
24.8: Who is this King of glorie? the Lord, strong and mightie, even the Lord mightie in battell.
24.9: Lift up your heads, ye gates, and lift up your selves, ye everlasting doores, and the King of glorie shall come in.
24.10: Who is this King of glory? the Lord of hostes, he is the King of glorie. Selah.

25.1: A Psalm of David. Unto thee, O Lord, lift I up my soul.
25.2: My God, I trust in thee: let me not be confounded: let not mine enemies reioyce over mee.
25.3: So all that hope in thee, shall not be ashamed: but let them be confounded, that transgress without cause.
25.4: Shew me thy waies, O Lord, and teach me thy paths.
25.5: Lead me foorth in thy trueth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation: in thee doe I trust all the day.
25.6: Remember, O Lord, thy tender mercies, and thy loving kindness: for they have been for ever.
25.7: Remember not the sinnes of my youth, nor my rebellions, but according to thy kindenesse remember thou me, even for thy goodness sake, O Lord.
25.8: Gracious and righteous is the Lord: therefore will he teach sinners in the way.
25.9: Them that be meek, will hee guide in iudgement, and teach the humble his way.
25.10: All the pathes of the Lord are mercie and trueth unto such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.
25.11: For thy Names sake, O Lord, be merciful unto mine iniquitie, for it is great.
25.12: What man is he that feareth the Lord? him wil he teach the way that hee shall chuse.
25.13: His soul shall dwell at ease, and his seed shall inherit the land.
25.14: The secret of the Lord is reueiled to them, that fear him: and his covenant to give them understanding.
25.15: Mine eyes are ever toward the Lord: for he will bring my feet out of the net.
25.16: Turn thy face unto mee, and have mercie upon me: for I am desolate and poor.
25.17: The sorowes of mine heart are enlarged: draw me out of my troubles.
25.18: Look upon mine affliction and my travel, and forgive all my sinnes.
25.19: Behold mine enemies, for they are manie, and they hate me with cruel hatred.
25.20: Keep my soul, and deliver me: let me not be confounded, for I trust in thee.
25.21: Let mine vprightnes and equitie preserve me: for mine hope is in thee.
25.22: Deliver Israel, O God, out of all his troubles.

26.1: A Psalm of David. Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in mine innocency: my trust hath been also in the Lord: therefore shall I not slide.
26.2: Prove me, O Lord, and trie mee: examine my reines, and mine heart.
26.3: For thy loving kindness is before mine eyes: therefore have I walked in thy trueth.
26.4: I have not hanted with vain persons, neither kept companie with the dissemblers.
26.5: I have hated the assemblie of the evil, and have not companied with the wicked.
26.6: I will wash mine handes in innocencie, O Lord, and compass thine altar,
26.7: That I may declare with the voyce of thankesgiuing, and set foorth all thy wonderous woorkes.
26.8: O Lord, I have loved the habitation of thine house, and the place where thine honour dwelleth.
26.9: Gather not my soul with the sinners, nor my life with the bloodie men:
26.10: In whose handes is wickednes, and their right hand is full of bribes.
26.11: But I will walk in mine innocencie: redeem me therefore, and be merciful unto me.
26.12: My foot standeth in vprightnesse: I will praise thee, O Lord, in the Congregations.

27.1: A Psalm of David. The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear? the Lord is the strength of my life, of whom shall I be afraid?
27.2: When the wicked, even mine enemies and my foes came upon mee to eat up my flesh; they stumbled and fell.
27.3: Though an host pitched against me, mine heart should not be afraid: though war be raised against me, I will trust in this.
27.4: One thing have I desired of the Lord, that I will require, even that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the dayes of my life, to behold the beautie of the Lord, and to visit his Temple.
27.5: For in the time of trouble hee shall hide mee in his Tabernacle: in the secret place of his pavilion shall he hide me, and set me up upon a rock.
27.6: And now shall hee lift up mine head above mine enemies round about mee: therefore wil I offer in his Tabernacle sacrifices of joy: I wil sing and praise the Lord.
27.7: Hearken unto my voyce, O Lord, when I crie: have mercie also upon mee and hear mee.
27.8: When thou saidest, Seek ye my face, mine heart answered unto thee, O Lord, I will seek thy face.
27.9: Hide not therefore thy face from mee, nor cast thy seruat away in displeasure: thou hast been my succour: leave me not, neither forsake mee, O God of my salvation.
27.10: Though my father and my mother should forsake me, yet the Lord will gather me up.
27.11: Teach mee thy way, O Lord, and lead me in a right path, because of mine enemies.
27.12: Give me not unto the lust of mine adversaries: for there are false witnesses risen up against me, and such as speak cruelly.
27.13: I should have fainted, except I had beleeued to see the goodnes of the Lord in the land of the living.
27.14: Hope in the Lord: be strong, and he shall comfort thine heart, and trust in the Lord.

28.1: A Psalm of David. Unto thee, O Lord, doe I crie: O my strength, be not deaf toward mee, lest, if thou answer me not, I be like them that goe down into the pit.
28.2: Hear the voyce of my petitions, when I crie unto thee, when I hold up mine handes toward thine holy Oracle.
28.3: Draw mee not away with the wicked, and with the woorkers of iniquitie: which speak friendly to their neighbours, when malice is in their hearts.
28.4: Reward them according to their deedes, and according to the wickednes of their inventions: recompense them after the woorke of their handes: render them their reward.
28.5: For they regard not the woorkes of the Lord, nor the operation of his handes: therefore break them down, and build them not up.
28.6: Praised be the Lord, for he hath heard the voyce of my petitions.
28.7: The Lord is my strength and my shield: mine heart trusted in him, and I was helped: therfore mine heart shall reioyce, and with my song will I praise him.
28.8: The Lord is their strength, and he is the strength of the deliverances of his anointed.
28.9: Save thy people, and bless thine inheritance: feed them also, and exalt them for ever.

29.1: A Psalm of David. Give unto the Lord, ye sonnes of the mightie: give unto the Lord glorie and strength.
29.2: Give unto the Lord glorie due unto his Name: worship the Lord in the glorious Sanctuarie.
29.3: The voyce of the Lord is upon the waters: the God of glorie maketh it to thunder: the Lord is upon the great waters.
29.4: The voyce of the Lord is mightie: the voyce of the Lord is glorious.
29.5: The voyce of the Lord breaketh the cedars: yea, the Lord breaketh the cedars of Lebanon.
29.6: He maketh them also to leap like a calf: Lebanon also and Shirion like a yong vnicorne.
29.7: The voice of the Lord deuideth the flames of sir.
29.8: The voice of the Lord maketh the wildernes to tremble: the Lord maketh the wildernes of Kadesh to tremble.
29.9: The voice of the Lord maketh the hindes to calve, and discovereth the forests: therefore in his Temple doth every man speak of his glory.
29.10: The Lord sitteth upon the flood, and the Lord doeth remain King for ever.
29.11: The Lord shall give strength unto his people: the Lord shall bless his people with peace.

30.1: A Psalm or song of the dedication of the house of David. I will magnifie thee, O Lord: for thou hast exalted mee, and hast not made my foe to reioyce over me.
30.2: O Lord my God, I cried unto thee, and thou hast restored me.
30.3: O Lord, thou hast brought up my soul out of the grave: thou hast revived me from them that goe down into the pit.
30.4: Sing praises unto the Lord, ye his Saintes, and give thankes before the remembrance of his Holiness.
30.5: For he endureth but a while in his anger: but in his fauour is life: weeping may abide at evening, but joy cometh in the morning.
30.6: And in my prosperitie I sayde, I shall never be moved.
30.7: For thou Lord of thy goodnes hadest made my mountain to stand strong: but thou didest hide thy face, and I was troubled.
30.8: Then cried I unto thee, O Lord, and praied to my Lord.
30.9: What profit is there in my blood, when I go down to the pit? shall the dust give thankes unto thee? or shall it declare thy trueth?
30.10: Hear, O Lord, and have mercy upon me: Lord, be thou mine helper.
30.11: Thou hast turned my mourning into joy: thou hast loosed my sack and girded mee with gladness.
30.12: Therefore shall my tongue praise thee and not cease: O Lord my God, I will give thankes unto thee for ever.

31.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. In thee, O Lord, have I put my trust: let mee never be confounded: deliver me in thy righteousness.
31.2: Bow down thine ear to me: make haste to deliver mee: be unto me a strong rock, and an house of defence to save me.
31.3: For thou art my rock and my fortress: therefore for thy Names sake direct mee and guide me.
31.4: Draw mee out of the nette, that they have layde priuilie for mee: for thou art my strength.
31.5: Into thine hand I commend my spirit: for thou hast redeemed me, O Lord God of trueth.
31.6: I have hated them that give them selves to deceitful vanities: for I trust in the Lord.
31.7: I wil be glad and reioyce in thy mercie: for thou hast seen my trouble: thou hast knowen my soul in adversities,
31.8: And thou hast not shut me up in the hand of the enemie, but hast set my feet at large.
31.9: Have mercie upon mee, O Lord: for I am in trouble: mine eye, my soul and my bellie are consumed with grief.
31.10: For my life is wasted with heaviness, and my yeeres with mourning: my strength faileth for my pain, and my bones are consumed.
31.11: I was a reproch among all mine enemies, but specially among my neighbours: and a fear to mine acquaintance, who seeing me in the street, fled from me.
31.12: I am forgotten, as a dead man out of mind: I am like a broken vessell.
31.13: For I have heard the rayling of great men: fear was on every side, while they conspired together against mee, and consulted to take my life.
31.14: But I trusted in thee, O Lord: I said, Thou art my God.
31.15: My times are in thine hand: deliver mee from the hand of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me.
31.16: Make thy face to shine upon thy servant, and save me through thy mercie.
31.17: Let me not be confounded, O Lord: for I have called upon thee: let the wicked bee put to confusion, and to silence in the grave.
31.18: Let the lying lips be made dumme, which cruelly, proudly and spitefully speak against the righteous.
31.19: How great is thy goodness, which thou hast layde up for them, that fear thee! and done to them, that trust in thee, even before the sonnes of men!
31.20: Thou doest hide them privily in thy presence from the pride of men: thou keepest them secretly in thy Tabernacle from the strife of tongues.
31.21: Blessed be the Lord: for hee hath shewed his marueilous kindenesse toward me in a strong citie.
31.22: Though I said in mine haste, I am cast out of thy sight, yet thou heardest the voyce of my prayer, when I cryed unto thee.
31.23: Love ye the Lord all his Saintes: for the Lord preserveth the faithful, and rewardeth abundantly the proud doer.
31.24: All ye that trust in the Lord, be strong, and he shall establish your heart.

32.1: A Psalm of David to give instruction. Blessed is he whose wickednes is forgiven, and whose sinne is covered.
32.2: Blessed is the man, unto whom the Lord imputeth not iniquitie, and in whose spirit there is no guile.
32.3: When I held my tongue, my bones consumed, or when I roared all the day,
32.4: (For thine hand is heauie upon me, day and night: and my moysture is turned into ye drought of summer. Selah)
32.5: Then I acknowledged my sinne unto thee, neither hid I mine iniquitie: for I thought, I will confess against my self my wickedness unto the Lord, and thou forgavest the punishment of my sinne. Selah.
32.6: Therefore shall every one, that is godly, make his prayer unto thee in a time, when thou mayest be found: surely in the flood of great waters they shall not come neere him.
32.7: Thou art my secret place: thou preservest me from trouble: thou compassest me about with ioyfull deliverance. Selah.
32.8: I will instruct thee, and teach thee in the way that thou shalt goe, and I will guide thee with mine eye.
32.9: Be ye not like an horse, or like a mule, which understand not: whose mouthes thou doest bind with bit and bridle, least they come neere thee.
32.10: Many sorowes shall come to the wicked: but he, that trusteth in the Lord, mercie shall compass him.
32.11: Be glad ye righteous, and reioyce in the Lord, and be ioyfull all ye, that are upright in heart.

33.1: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous: for it becometh upright men to be thankefull.
33.2: Prayse the Lord with harp: sing unto him with viol and instrument of ten strings.
33.3: Sing unto him a new song: sing cheerefully with a loud voyce.
33.4: For the word of the Lord is righteous, and all his workes are faithful.
33.5: He loveth righteousness and iudgement: the earth is full of the goodness of the Lord.
33.6: By the word of the Lord were the heavens made, and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.
33.7: He gathereth the waters of the sea together as upon an heap, and layeth up the depths in his treasures.
33.8: Let all the earth fear the Lord: let al them that dwell in the world, fear him.
33.9: For he spake, and it was done: he commanded, and it stood.
33.10: The Lord breaketh the counsel of the heathen, and bringeth to nought the devices of the people.
33.11: The counsel of the Lord shall stand for ever, and the thoughts of his heart throughout all ages.
33.12: Blessed is that nation, whose God is the Lord: even the people that he hath chosen for his inheritance.
33.13: The Lord looketh down from heaven, and beholdeth all the children of men.
33.14: From the habitation of his dwelling he beholdeth all them that dwell in the earth.
33.15: He facioneth their hearts every one, and understandeth all their workes.
33.16: The King is not saved by the multitude of an host, neither is the mightie man delivered by great strength.
33.17: A horse is a vain help, and shall not deliver any by his great strength.
33.18: Behold, the eye of the Lord is upon them that fear him, and upon them, that trust in his mercie,
33.19: To deliver their soules from death, and to preserve them in famine.
33.20: Our soul waiteth for the Lord: for he is our help and our shield.
33.21: Surely our heart shall reioyce in him, because we trusted in his holy Name.
33.22: Let thy mercie, O Lord, be upon us, as we trust in thee.

34.1: A Psalm of David, when he changed his behauiour before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he departed. I will alway give thankes unto the Lord: his praise shalbe in my mouth continually.
34.2: My soul shall glory in the Lord: the humble shall hear it, and be glad.
34.3: Praise ye the Lord with me, and let us magnifie his Name together.
34.4: I sought the Lord, and he heard me: yea, he delivered me out of all my fear.
34.5: They shall look unto him, and runne to him: and their faces shall not be ashamed, saying,
34.6: This poor man cryed, and the Lord heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.
34.7: The Angel of the Lord pitcheth round about them, that fear him, and delivereth them.
34.8: Taste ye and see, how gratious the Lord is: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.
34.9: Fear the Lord, ye his Saintes: for nothing wanteth to them that fear him.
34.10: The lyons doe lack and suffer hunger, but they, which seek the Lord, shall want nothing that is good.
34.11: Come children, hearken unto me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord.
34.12: What man is he, that desireth life, and loveth long dayes for to see good?
34.13: Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips, that they speak no guile.
34.14: Eschew evil and doe good: seek peace and follow after it.
34.15: The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his eares are open unto their crie.
34.16: But the face of the Lord is against them that doe evil, to cut off their remembrance from the earth.
34.17: The righteous crie, and the Lord heareth them, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.
34.18: The Lord is neere unto them that are of a contrite heart, and will save such as be afflicted in Spirit.
34.19: Great are the troubles of the righteous: but the Lord delivereth him out of them all.
34.20: He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.
34.21: But malice shall slay the wicked: and they that hate the righteous, shall perish.
34.22: The Lord redeemeth the soules of his servants: and none, that trust in him, shall perish.

35.1: A Psalm of David. Plead thou my cause, O Lord, with them that strive with me: fight thou against them, that fight against me.
35.2: Lay hand upon the shield and buckler, and stand up for mine help.
35.3: Bring out also the spear and stop the way against them, that persecute me: say unto my soul, I am thy salvation.
35.4: Let them be confounded and put to shame, that seek after my soul: let them be turned back, and brought to confusion, that imagine mine hurt.
35.5: Let them be as chaff before the wind, and let the Angel of the Lord scatter them.
35.6: Let their way be dark and slipperie: and let the Angel of the Lord persecute them.
35.7: For without cause they have hid the pit and their net for me: without cause have they digged a pit for my soul.
35.8: Let destruction come upon him at vnwares, and let his net, that he hath laid priuilie, take him: let him fall into the same destruction.
35.9: Then my soul shalbe ioyfull in the Lord: it shall reioyce in his salvation.
35.10: All my bones shall say, Lord, who is like unto thee, which deliverest the poor from him, that is too strong for him! yea, the poor and him that is in miserie, from him that spoyleth him!
35.11: Cruel witnesses did rise up: they asked of me things that I knew not.
35.12: They rewarded me evil for good, to have spoyled my soul.
35.13: Yet I, when they were sick, I was clothed with a sack: I humbled my soul with fasting: and my praier was turned upon my bosom.
35.14: I behaved my self as to my friend, or as to my brother: I humbled my self, mourning as one that bewaileth his mother.
35.15: But in mine aduersitie they reioyced, and gathered them selves together: the abiects assembled themselves against me, and knew not: they tare me and ceased not,
35.16: With the false skoffers at bankets, gnashing their teeth against me.
35.17: Lord, how long wilt thou behold this? deliver my soul from their tumult, even my desolate soul from the lions.
35.18: So will I give thee thankes in a great Congregation: I will praise thee among much people.
35.19: Let not them that are mine enemies, vniustly reioyce over mee, neyther let them wink with the eye, that hate mee without a cause.
35.20: For they speak not as friendes: but they imagine deceitful woordes against the quiet of the land.
35.21: And they gaped on mee with their mouthes, saying, Aha, aha, our eye hath seen.
35.22: Thou hast seen it, O Lord: keep not silence: be not far from me, O Lord.
35.23: Arise and wake to my iudgement, even to my cause, my God, and my Lord.
35.24: Judge me, O Lord my God, according to thy righteousness, and let them not reioyce over mee.
35.25: Let them not say in their hearts, O our soul reioyce: neither let them say, We have deuoured him.
35.26: Let them bee confounded, and put to shame together, that reioyce at mine hurt: let them bee clothed with confusion and shame, that lift up themselves against me.
35.27: But let them be joyful and glad, that love my righteousness: yea, let them say alway, Let the Lord be magnified, which loveth the prosperitie of his servant.
35.28: And my tongue shall utter thy righteousness, and thy praise every day.

36.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David, the servant of the Lord. Wickedness sayeth to the wicked man, even in mine heart, that there is no fear of God before his eyes.
36.2: For hee flattereth himself in his own eyes, while his iniquitie is foud worthy to be hated.
36.3: The wordes of his mouth are iniquitie and deceit: hee hath left off to understand and to doe good.
36.4: Hee imagineth mischief upon his bed: he setteth himself upon a way, that is not good, and doeth not abhorre evil.
36.5: Thy mercy, O Lord, reacheth unto the heavens, and thy faithfulness unto the cloudes.
36.6: Thy righteousness is like the mightie moutaines: thy iudgements are like a great deep: thou, Lord, doest save man and beast.
36.7: How excellent is thy mercy, O God! therefore the children of men trust under the shadow of thy wings.
36.8: They shall be satisfied with the fatness of thine house, and thou shalt give them drink out of the river of thy pleasures.
36.9: For with thee is the well of life, and in thy light shall we see light.
36.10: Extend thy loving kindnes unto them that know thee, and thy righteousness unto them that are upright in heart.
36.11: Let not ye foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of ye wicked men move me.
36.12: There they are fallen that work iniquity: they are cast down, and shall not be able to rise.

37.1: A Psalm of David. Fret not thy self because of the wicked men, neither be enuious for the evil doers.
37.2: For they shall soon bee cut down like grass, and shall wither as the green herb.
37.3: Trust thou in the Lord and do good: dwell in the land, and thou shalt be fed assuredly.
37.4: And delite thy self in the Lord, and hee shall give thee thine hearts desire.
37.5: Commit thy way unto the Lord, and trust in him, and he shall bring it to pass.
37.6: And he shall bring foorth thy righteousnes as the light, and thy iudgement as the noon day.
37.7: Wait patiently upon the Lord and hope in him: fret not thy self for him which prospereth in his way: nor for the man that bringeth his enterprises to pass.
37.8: Cease from anger, and leave off wrath: fret not thy self also to doe evil.
37.9: For evil doers shalbe cut off, and they that wait upon the Lord, they shall inherit the land.
37.10: Therefore yet a litle while, and the wicked shall not appear, and thou shalt look after his place, and he shall not be found.
37.11: But meek men shall possess the earth, and shall have their delite in the multitude of peace.
37.12: The wicked practiseth against the just, and gnasheth his teeth against him.
37.13: But the Lord shall laugh him to scorn: for he seeth, that his day is coming.
37.14: The wicked have drawen their sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needie, and to slay such as be of upright conversation.
37.15: But their sword shall enter into their own heart, and their bowes shalbe broken.
37.16: A small thing unto the just man is better, then great riches to the wicked and mightie.
37.17: For the armes of the wicked shall be broken: but the Lord upholdeth the just men.
37.18: The Lord knoweth the dayes of upright men, and their inheritance shall bee perpetual.
37.19: They shall not be confounded in the perilous time, and in the daies of famine they shall have ynough.
37.20: But the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the Lord shall be consumed as the fatte of lambes: even with the smoke shall they consume away.
37.21: The wicked boroweth and payeth not again. but the righteous is merciful, and giveth.
37.22: For such as be blessed of God, shall inherit the land, and they that be cursed of him, shalbe cut off.
37.23: The pathes of man are directed by the Lord: for he loveth his way.
37.24: Though he fall, hee shall not be cast off: for the Lord putteth under his hand.
37.25: I have been yong, and am old: yet I saw never the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.
37.26: But hee is ever merciful and lendeth, and his seed enioyeth the blessing.
37.27: Flee from evil and doe good, and dwell for ever.
37.28: For the Lord loveth iudgement, and forsaketh not his Saintes: they shall be preserved for evermore: but the seed of the wicked shall be cut off.
37.29: The righteous men shall inherit the land, and dwell therein for ever.
37.30: The mouth of the righteous will speak of wisedome, and his tongue will talk of iudgement.
37.31: For the Law of his God is in his heart, and his steppes shall not slide.
37.32: The wicked watcheth the righteous, and seeketh to slay him.
37.33: But the Lord wil not leave him in his hand, nor condemn him, when he is judged.
37.34: Wait thou on the Lord, and keep his way, and he shall exalt thee, that thou shalt inherit the land: when the wicked men shall perish, thou shalt see.
37.35: I have seen the wicked strong, and spreading himself like a green bay tree.
37.36: Yet he passed away, and loe, he was gone, and I sought him, but he could not be found.
37.37: Mark the upright man, and behold the just: for the end of that man is peace.
37.38: But the transgressours shall be destroyed together, and the end of the wicked shall bee cut off.
37.39: But the salvation of the righteous men shalbe of the Lord: he shalbe their strength in the time of trouble.
37.40: For the Lord shall help them, and deliver them: he shall deliver them from the wicked, and shall save them, because they trust in him.

38.1: A Psalm of David for remembrance. O Lord, rebuke mee not in thine anger, neither chastise me in thy wrath.
38.2: For thine arrowes have light upon me, and thine hand lyeth upon me.
38.3: There is nothing sound in my flesh, because of thine anger: neither is there rest in my bones because of my sinne.
38.4: For mine iniquities are gone over mine head, and as a weightie burden they are too heauie for me.
38.5: My woundes are putrified, and corrupt because of my foolishnes.
38.6: I am bowed, and crooked very sore: I goe mourning all the day.
38.7: For my reines are full of burning, and there is nothing sound in my flesh.
38.8: I am weakened and sore broken: I roar for the very grief of mine heart.
38.9: Lord, I powre my whole desire before thee, and my sighing is not hid from thee.
38.10: Mine heart panteth: my strength faileth me, and the light of mine eyes, even they are not mine own.
38.11: My lovers and my friends stand aside from my plague, and my kinsmen stand a far off.
38.12: They also, that seek after my life, lay snares, and they that go about to do me evil, talk wicked things and imagine deceit continually.
38.13: But I as a deaf man heard not, and am as a dumme man, which openeth not his mouth.
38.14: Thus am I as a man, that heareth not, and in whose mouth are no reproofes.
38.15: For on thee, O Lord, do I wait: thou wilt hear me, my Lord, my God.
38.16: For I said, Hear me, least they reioyce over me: for when my foot slippeth, they extol themselves against me.
38.17: Surely I am ready to halt, and my sorow is ever before me.
38.18: When I declare my pain, and am sory for my sinne,
38.19: Then mine enemies are alive and are mightie, and they that hate me wrongfully are many.
38.20: They also, that reward evil for good, are mine adversaries, because I follow goodness.
38.21: Forsake me not, O Lord: be not thou far from me, my God.
38.22: Haste thee to help mee, O my Lord, my salvation.

39.1: To the excellent musician Jeduthun. I thought, I will take heed to my wayes, that I sinne not with my tongue: I will keep my mouth brideled, while the wicked is in my sight.
39.2: I was dumme and spake nothing: I kept silece even from good, and my sorow was more stirred.
39.3: Mine heart was hot within me, and while I was musing, the fire kindeled, and I spake with my tongue, saying,
39.4: Lord, let me know mine end, and the measure of my dayes, what it is: let mee know how long I have to live.
39.5: Behold, thou hast made my dayes as an hand breadth, and mine age as nothing in respect of thee: surely every man in his best state is altogether vanitie. Selah.
39.6: Doubtless man walketh in a shadow, and disquieteth himself in vain: he heapeth up riches, and cannot tell who shall gather them.
39.7: And now Lord, what wait I for? mine hope is even in thee.
39.8: Deliver me from all my transgressions, and make me not a rebuke unto the foolish.
39.9: I should have been dumme, and not have opened my mouth, because thou didest it.
39.10: Take thy plague away from mee: for I am consumed by the stroke of thine hand.
39.11: When thou with rebukes doest chastise man for iniquitie, thou as a moth makest his beautie to consume: surely every man is vanitie. Selah.
39.12: Hear my prayer, O Lord, and hearken unto my cry: keep not silence at my teares, for I am a strager with thee, and a soiourner as all my fathers.
39.13: Stay thine anger from me, that I may recover my strength, before I go hence and be not.

40.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. I Waited paciently for the Lord, and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.
40.2: Hee brought mee also out of the horrible pit, out of the myrie clay, and set my feet upon the rock, and ordered my goings.
40.3: And he hath put in my mouth a new song of praise unto our God: many shall see it and fear, and shall trust in the Lord.
40.4: Blessed is the man that maketh the Lord his trust, and regardeth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lyes.
40.5: O Lord my God, thou hast made thy wonderful workes so many, that none can count in order to thee thy thoughts toward us: I would declare, and speak of them, but they are moe then I am able to express.
40.6: Sacrifice and offering thou didest not desire: (for mine eares hast thou prepared) burnt offring and sinne offering hast thou not required.
40.7: Then said I, Lo, I come: for in the roll of the book it is written of me,
40.8: I desired to doe thy good will, O my God: yea, thy Law is within mine heart.
40.9: I have declared thy righteousness in the great Congregation: loe, I will not refrain my lippes: O Lord, thou knowest.
40.10: I have not hid thy righteousness within mine heart, but I have declared thy trueth and thy salvation: I have not conceiled thy mercy and thy trueth from the great Congregation.
40.11: Withdraw not thou thy tender mercie from mee, O Lord: let thy mercie and thy trueth alway preserve me.
40.12: For innumerable troubles have compassed mee: my sinnes have taken such hold upon me, that I am not able to look up: yea, they are moe in nomber then the heares of mine head: therefore mine heart hath failed me.
40.13: Let it please thee, O Lord, to deliver mee: make haste, O Lord, to help me.
40.14: Let them be confounded and put to shame together, that seek my soul to destroy it: let them be driven backward and put to rebuke, that desire mine hurt.
40.15: Let them be destroyed for a reward of their shame, which say unto me, Aha, aha.
40.16: Let all them, that seek thee, reioyce and be glad in thee: and let them, that love thy salvation, say alway, The Lord be praysed.
40.17: Though I be poor and needie, the Lord thinketh on mee: thou art mine helper and my deliverer: my God, make no tarying.

41.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. Blessed is he that judgeth wisely of the poor: the Lord shall deliver him in ye time of trouble.
41.2: The Lord will keep him, and preserve him alive: he shalbe blessed upon the earth, and thou wilt not deliver him unto the will of his enemies.
41.3: The Lord wil strengthen him upon ye bed of sorow: thou hast turned al his bed in his sicknes.
41.4: Therefore I said, Lord have mercie upon me: heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.
41.5: Mine enemies speak evil of me, saying, When shall he die, and his name perish?
41.6: And if hee come to see mee, hee speaketh lies, but his heart heapeth iniquitie within him, and when he cometh foorth, he telleth it.
41.7: All they that hate me, whisper together against me: even against me do they imagine mine hurt.
41.8: A mischief is light upon him, and he that lyeth, shall no more rise.
41.9: Yea, my familiar friend, whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up the heel against me.
41.10: Therefore, O Lord, have mercy upon mee, and raise me up: so I shall reward them.
41.11: By this I know that thou fauourest me, because mine enemie doth not triumph against me.
41.12: And as for me, thou upholdest me in mine integritie, and doest set me before thy face for ever.
41.13: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel world without end. So be it, even so be it.

42.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm to give instruction, committed to the sonnes of Korah. As the hart brayeth for the rivers of water, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
42.2: My soul thirsteth for God, even for the living God: when shall I come and appear before the presence of God?
42.3: My teares have bin my meat day and night, while they dayly say unto me, Where is thy God?
42.4: When I remembred these things, I powred out my very heart, because I had gone with the multitude, and ledde them into the House of God with the voyce of singing, and prayse, as a multitude that keepeth a feast.
42.5: Why art thou cast down, my soul, and vnquiet within me? wait on God: for I will yet give him thankes for the help of his presence.
42.6: My God, my soul is cast down within me, because I remember thee, from the land of Iorden, and Hermonim, and from the mount Mizar.
42.7: One deep calleth another deep by the noyse of thy water spoutes: all thy waves and thy floods are gone over me.
42.8: The Lord will graunt his loving kindenesse in the day, and in the night shall I sing of him, even a prayer unto the God of my life.
42.9: I wil say unto God, which is my rock, Why hast thou forgotten mee? why goe I mourning, when the enemie oppresseth me?
42.10: My bones are cut asunder, while mine enemies reproch me, saying dayly unto me, Where is thy God?
42.11: Why art thou cast down, my soul? and why art thou disquieted within mee? wait on God: for I wil yet give him thankes: he is my present help, and my God.

43.1: Judge me, O God, and defend my cause against the unmerciful people: deliver mee from the deceitful and wicked man.
43.2: For thou art the God of my strength: why hast thou put me away? why goe I so mourning, when the enemie oppresseth me?
43.3: Send thy light and thy trueth: let them lead mee: let them bring mee unto thine holy Mountain and to thy Tabernacles.
43.4: Then wil I go unto the altar of God, even unto the God of my joy and gladnes: and upon the harp wil I give thanks unto thee, O God, my God.
43.5: Why art thou cast down, my soul? and why art thou disquieted within mee? wait on God: for I will yet give him thankes, he is my present help, and my God.

44.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm to give instruction, committed to the sonnes of Korah. We have heard with our eares, O God: our fathers have told us the workes, that thou hast done in their dayes, in the old time:
44.2: How thou hast driven out the heathen with thine hand, and planted them: how thou hast destroyed the people, and caused them to grow.
44.3: For they inherited not the land by their own sword, neither did their own arm save them: but thy right hand, and thine arm and the light of thy countenance, because thou didest fauour them.
44.4: Thou art my King, O God: send help unto Iaakob.
44.5: Through thee have we thrust back our adversaries: by thy Name have we troden down them that rose up against us.
44.6: For I do not trust in my bow, neither can my sword save me.
44.7: But thou hast saved us from our adversaries, and hast put them to confusion that hate us.
44.8: Therefore will wee praise God continually, and will confess thy Name for ever. Selah.
44.9: But now thou art far off, and puttest us to confusion, and goest not forth with our armies.
44.10: Thou makest us to turn back from the adversary, and they, which hate us, spoil for theselues.
44.11: Thou givest us as sheep to bee eaten, and doest scatter us among the nations.
44.12: Thou sellest thy people without gain, and doest not increase their price.
44.13: Thou makest us a reproche to our neighbours, a iest and a laughing stock to them that are round about us.
44.14: Thou makest us a proverb among the nations, and a nodding of the head among the people.
44.15: My confusion is dayly before me, and the shame of my face hath covered me,
44.16: For the voyce of the slaunderer and rebuker, for the enemie and avenger.
44.17: All this is come upon us, yet doe wee not forget thee, neither deal wee falsly concerning thy covenant.
44.18: Our heart is not turned back: neither our steps gone out of thy paths,
44.19: Albeit thou hast smitten us down into the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death.
44.20: If wee have forgotten the Name of our God, and holden up our hands to a strange god,
44.21: Shall not God search this out? for hee knoweth the secrets of the heart.
44.22: Surely for thy sake are we slain continually, and are counted as sheep for the slaughter.
44.23: Up, why sleepest thou, O Lord? awake, be not far off for ever.
44.24: Wherefore hidest thou thy face? and forgettest our miserie and our affliction?
44.25: For our soul is beaten down unto the dust: our belly cleaveth unto the ground.
44.26: Rise up for our succour, and redeem us for thy mercies sake.

45.1: To him that excelleth on Shoshannim a song of love to give instruction, committed to the sonnes of Korah. Mine heart will utter forth a good matter: I wil intreat in my workes of the King: my tongue is as the pen of a swift writer.
45.2: Thou art fayrer then the children of men: grace is powred in thy lips, because God hath blessed thee for ever.
45.3: Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O most mightie, to wit, thy worship and thy glory,
45.4: And prosper with thy glory: ride upon the word of trueth and of meekenes and of righteousnes: so thy right hand shall teach thee terrible things.
45.5: Thine arrowes are sharp to pearce the heart of the Kings enemies: therefore the people shall fall under thee.
45.6: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the scepter of thy kingdom is a scepter of righteousness.
45.7: Thou lovest righteousnes, and hatest wickedness, because God, even thy God hath anoynted thee with the oyle of gladnes above thy fellowes.
45.8: All thy garments smell of myrrh and aloes, and cassia, when thou comest out of the yuorie palaces, where they have made thee glad.
45.9: Kings daugthers were among thine honorable wives: upon thy right hand did stand the Queen in a vesture of gold of Ophir.
45.10: Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear: forget also thine own people and thy fathers house.
45.11: So shall the King have pleasure in thy beautie: for he is thy Lord, and reverence thou him.
45.12: And the daughter of Tyrus with the rich of the people shall doe homage before thy face with presents.
45.13: The Kings daughter is all glorious within: her clothing is of broydred gold.
45.14: She shalbe brought unto the King in raiment of needle work: the virgins that follow after her, and her companions shall be brought unto thee.
45.15: With joy and gladnes shall they be brought, and shall enter into the Kings palace.
45.16: In stead of thy fathers shall thy children be: thou shalt make them princes through all the earth.
45.17: I will make thy Name to be remembred through all generations: therefore shall the people give thanks unto thee world without end.

46.1: To him that excelleth upon Alamoth a song committed to the sonnes of Korah. God is our hope and strength, and help in troubles, ready to be found.
46.2: Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be moved, and though the mountaines fall into the middes of the sea.
46.3: Though the waters thereof rage and be troubled, and the mountaines shake at the surges of the same. Selah,
46.4: Yet there is a River, whose streames shall make glad the citie of God: even the Sanctuarie of the Tabernacles of the most High.
46.5: God is in the middes of it: therefore shall it not be moved: God shall help it very earely.
46.6: When the nations raged, and the kingdomes were moved, God thundred, and the earth melted.
46.7: The Lord of hostes is with us: the God of Iaakob is our refuge. Selah.
46.8: Come, and behold the workes of the Lord, what desolations he hath made in the earth.
46.9: He maketh wars to cease unto the endes of the world: he breaketh the bow and cutteth the spear, and burneth the chariots with fire.
46.10: Be still and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, and I wil be exalted in the earth.
46.11: The Lord of hostes is with us: the God of Iaakob is our refuge. Selah.

47.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm committed to the sonnes of Korah. All people clap your hands: sing loud unto God with a ioyfull voyce.
47.2: For the Lord is high, and terrible: a great King over all the earth.
47.3: He hath subdued the people under us, and the nations under our feet.
47.4: Hee hath chosen our inheritance for us: even the glory of Iaakob whom he loved. Selah.
47.5: God is gone up with triumph, even the Lord, with the sound of the trumpet.
47.6: Sing prayses to God, sing prayses: sing prayses unto our King, sing prayses.
47.7: For God is the King of all the earth: sing prayses every one that hath understanding.
47.8: God reigneth over the heathen: God sitteth upon his holy throne.
47.9: The princes of the people are gathered unto the people of the God of Abraham: for the shields of the world belong to God: he is greatly to be exalted.

48.1: A song or Psalm committed to the sonnes of Korah. Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praysed, in the Citie of our God, even upon his holy Mountain.
48.2: Mount Zion, lying Northward, is fair in situation: it is the joy of the whole earth, and the Citie of the great King.
48.3: In the palaces thereof God is knowen for a refuge.
48.4: For lo, the Kings were gathered, and went together.
48.5: When they saw it, they marueiled: they were astonied, and suddenly driven back.
48.6: Fear came there upon them, and sorowe, as upon a woman in travail.
48.7: As with an East wind thou breakest the shippes of Tarshish, so were they destroyed.
48.8: As we have heard, so have we seen in the citie of the Lord of hostes, in the Citie of our God: God will stablish it for ever. Selah.
48.9: We wait for thy loving kindnes, O God, in the middes of thy Temple.
48.10: O God, according unto thy Name, so is thy prayse unto the worlds end: thy right hand is full of righteousnes.
48.11: Let mount Zion reioyce, and the daughters of Judah be glad, because of thy iudgements.
48.12: Compass about Zion, and goe round about it, and tell the towres thereof.
48.13: Mark well the wall thereof: behold her towres, that ye may tell your posteritie.
48.14: For this God is our God for ever and ever: he shall be our guide unto the death.

49.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm committed to the sonnes of Korah. Hear this, all ye people: give ear, all ye that dwell in the world,
49.2: As well low as hie, both rich and poor.
49.3: My mouth shall speak of wisdom, and the meditation of mine heart is of knowledge.
49.4: I will incline mine ear to a parable, and utter my grave matter upon the harp.
49.5: Wherefore should I fear in the evil dayes, when iniquitie shall compass me about, as at mine heeles?
49.6: They trust in their goods, and boast them selves in the multitude of their riches.
49.7: Yet a man can by no meanes redeem his brother: he can not give his raunsome to God,
49.8: (So precious is the redemption of their soules, and the continuance for ever)
49.9: That he may live still for ever, and not see the grave.
49.10: For he seeth that wise men die, and also that the ignorant and foolish perish, and leave their riches for others.
49.11: Yet they think, their houses, and their habitations shall continue for ever, even from generation to generation, and call their lands by their names.
49.12: But man shall not continue in honour: he is like the beastes that die.
49.13: This their way uttereth their foolishnes: yet their posteritie delite in their talk. Selah.
49.14: Like sheep they lie in grave: death deuoureth them, and the righteous shall have domination over them in the morning: for their beautie shall consume, when they shall goe from their house to grave.
49.15: But God shall deliver my soul from the power of the grave: for he will receive me. Selah.
49.16: Be not thou afrayd when one is made rich, and when the glory of his house is increased.
49.17: For he shall take nothing away when he dieth, neither shall his pomp descend after him.
49.18: For while he lived, he reioyced himself: and men will prayse thee, when thou makest much of thy self.
49.19: He shall enter into the generation of his fathers, and they shall not live for ever.
49.20: Man is in honour, and understandeth not: he is like to beasts that perish.

50.1: A Psalm of Asaph. The God of Gods, even the Lord hath spoken and called the earth from the rising up of the sunne unto the going down thereof.
50.2: Out of Zion, which is the perfection of beautie, hath God shined.
50.3: Our God shall come and shall not keep silence: a fire shall deuoure before him, and a mightie tempest shall be mooued round about him.
50.4: Hee shall call the heaven above, and the earth to judge his people.
50.5: Gather my Saints together unto me, those that make a covenant with me with sacrifice.
50.6: And the heavens shall declare his righteousnes: for God is judge himself. Selah.
50.7: Hear, O my people, and I wil speak: hear, O Israel, and I wil testifie unto thee: for I am God, even thy God.
50.8: I wil not reprove thee for thy sacrifices, or thy burnt offerings, that have not been continually before me.
50.9: I will take no bullock out of thine house, nor goates out of thy foldes.
50.10: For all the beastes of the forest are mine, and the beastes on a thousand mountaines.
50.11: I know all the foules on the mountaines: and the wild beastes of the field are mine.
50.12: If I bee hungry, I will not tell thee: for the world is mine, and all that therein is.
50.13: Will I eat the flesh of bulles? or drink the blood of goates?
50.14: Offer unto God praise, and pay thy vowes unto the most High,
50.15: And call upon me in the day of trouble: so will I deliver thee, and thou shalt glorifie me.
50.16: But unto the wicked said God, What hast thou to doe to declare mine ordinances, that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth,
50.17: Seeing thou hatest to bee reformed, and hast cast my wordes behind thee?
50.18: For when thou seest a thief, thou runnest with him, and thou art partaker with the adulterers.
50.19: Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and with thy tongue thou forgest deceit.
50.20: Thou sittest, and speakest against thy brother, and slanderest thy mothers sonne.
50.21: These things hast thou done, and I held my tongue: therefore thou thoughtest that I was like thee: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thee.
