50.22: Oh cosider this, ye that forget God, least I tear you in pieces, and there be none that can deliver you.
50.23: He that offereth praise, shall glorifie mee: and to him, that disposeth his way aright, will I shew the salvation of God.

51.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David, when the Prophet Nathan came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba. Have mercie upon me, O God, according to thy loving kindnes: according to the multitude of thy compassions put away mine iniquities.
51.2: Wash me throughly from mine iniquitie, and clense me from my sinne.
51.3: For I know mine iniquities, and my sinne is ever before me.
51.4: Against thee, against thee onely have I sinned, and done evil in thy sight, that thou mayest be just when thou speakest, and pure when thou judgest.
51.5: Behold, I was borne in iniquitie, and in sinne hath my mother conceived me.
51.6: Behold, thou lovest trueth in the inward affections: therefore hast thou taught mee wisedome in the secret of mine heart.
51.7: Purge me with hyssop, and I shalbe clean: wash me, and I shalbe whiter then snow.
51.8: Make me to hear ioye and gladnes, that the bones, which thou hast broken, may reioyce.
51.9: Hide thy face from my sinnes, and put away all mine iniquities.
51.10: Create in mee a clean heart, O God, and renue a right spirit within me.
51.11: Cast mee not away from thy presence, and take not thine holy Spirit from me.
51.12: Restore to me the joy of thy salvation, and stablish me with thy free Spirit.
51.13: Then shall I teach thy wayes unto the wicked, and sinners shalbe converted unto thee.
51.14: Deliver me from blood, O God, which art the God of my salvation, and my tongue shall sing joyfully of thy righteousnes.
51.15: Open thou my lippes, O Lord, and my mouth shall shew foorth thy praise.
51.16: For thou desirest no sacrifice, though I would give it: thou delitest not in burnt offering.
51.17: The sacrifices of God are a contrite spirit: a contrite and a broken heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
51.18: Bee fauourable unto Zion for thy good pleasure: build the walles of Jerusalem.
51.19: Then shalt thou accept ye sacrifices of righteousnes, even the burnt offering and oblation: then shall they offer calves upon thine altar.

52.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David to give instruction. When Doeg the Edomite came and shewed Saul, and said to him, David is come to the house of Abimelech. Why boastest thou thy self in thy wickedness, O man of power? the loving kindenesse of God indureth dayly.
52.2: Thy tongue imagineth mischief, and is like a sharp rasor, that cutteth deceitfully.
52.3: Thou doest love evil more then good, and lies more then to speak the trueth. Selah.
52.4: Thou lovest all wordes that may destroy, O deceitful tongue!
52.5: So shall God destroy thee for ever: he shall take thee and pluck thee out of thy tabernacle, and root thee out of ye land of the living. Selah.
52.6: The righteous also shall see it, and fear, and shall laugh at him, saying,
52.7: Behold the man that took not God for his strength, but trusted unto the multitude of his riches, and put his strength in his malice.
52.8: But I shall bee like a green olive tree in the house of God: for I trusted in the mercie of God for ever and ever.
52.9: I will alway praise thee, for that thou hast done this, and I will hope in thy Name, because it is good before thy Saints.

53.1: To him that excelleth on Mahalath. A Psalm of David to give instruction. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. they have corrupted and done abominable wickednes: there is none that doeth good.
53.2: God looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that would understand, and seek God.
53.3: Every one is gone back: they are altogether corrupt: there is none that doth good, no not one.
53.4: Doe not the workers of iniquitie know that they eat up my people as they eat bread? they call not upon God.
53.5: There they were afraid for fear, where no fear was: for God hath scattered the bones of him that besieged thee: thou hast put them to confusion, because God hath cast them off.
53.6: Oh give salvation unto Israel out of Zion: when God turneth the captiuitie of his people, then Iaakob shall reioyce, and Israel shalbe glad.

54.1: To him that excelleth on Neginoth. A Psalm of David, to give instruction. When the Ziphims came and said unto Saul, Is not David hid among us? Save mee, O God, by thy Name, and by thy power judge me.
54.2: O God, hear my prayer: hearken unto the wordes of my mouth.
54.3: For strangers are risen up against me, and tyrants seek my soul: they have not set God before them. Selah.
54.4: Behold, God is mine helper: the Lord is with them that vpholde my soul.
54.5: He shall reward evil unto mine enemies: Oh cut them off in thy trueth!
54.6: Then I will sacrifice freely unto thee: I wil praise thy Name, O Lord, because it is good.
54.7: For he hath delivered me out of al trouble, and mine eye hath seen my desire upon mine enemies.

55.1: To him that excelleth on Neginoth. A Psalm of David to give instruction. Hear my prayer, O God, and hide not thy self from my supplication.
55.2: Hearken unto me, and answer me: I mourn in my prayer, and make a noyse,
55.3: For the voyce of the enemie, and for the vexation of ye wicked, because they have brought iniquitie upon me, and furiously hate me.
55.4: Mine heart trembleth within mee, and the terrours of death are fallen upon me.
55.5: Fear and trembling are come upon mee, and an horrible fear hath covered me.
55.6: And I said, Oh that I had wings like a dove: then would I flie away and rest.
55.7: Behold, I would take my flight far off, and lodge in the wildernes. Selah.
55.8: Hee would make haste for my deliverance from the stormie wind and tempest.
55.9: Destroy, O Lord, and deuide their tongues: for I have seen crueltie and strife in the citie.
55.10: Day and night they goe about it upon the walles thereof: both iniquitie and mischief are in the middes of it.
55.11: Wickednes is in the middes thereof: deceit and guile depart not from her streetes.
55.12: Surely mine enemie did not defame mee: for I could have borne it: neither did mine aduersarie exalt himself against mee: for I would have hid me from him.
55.13: But it was thou, O man, even my companion, my guide and my familiar:
55.14: Which delited in consulting together, and went into the House of God as companions.
55.15: Let death sense upon them: let them goe down quick into the grave: for wickednes is in their dwellings, even in the middes of them.
55.16: But I will call unto God, and the Lord will save me.
55.17: Evening and morning, and at noon will I pray, and make a noyse, and he wil hear my voice.
55.18: He hath delivered my soul in peace from the battel, that was against me: for many were with me.
55.19: God shall hear and afflict them, even hee that reigneth of old, Selah. because they have no changes, therefore they fear not God.
55.20: Hee layed his hand upon such, as be at peace with him, and he brake his covenant.
55.21: The wordes of his mouth were softer then butter, yet war was in his heart: his words were more gentle then oyle, yet they were swordes.
55.22: Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and hee shall nourish thee: he wil not suffer the righteous to fall for ever.
55.23: And thou, O God, shalt bring them down into the pitte of corruption: the bloudie, and deceitful men shall not live half their dayes: but I will trust in thee.

56.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David on Michtam, concerning the dumme dove in a far countrey, when the Philistims took him in Gath. Be merciful unto me, O God, for man would swallow me up: he fighteth continually and vexeth me.
56.2: Mine enemies would dayly swallow mee up: for many fight against me, O thou most High.
56.3: When I was afrayd, I trusted in thee.
56.4: I will reioyce in God, because of his word, I trust in God, and will not fear what flesh can doe unto me.
56.5: Mine own wordes grieve me dayly: all their thoughtes are against me to doe me hurt.
56.6: They gather together, and keep them selves close: they mark my steps, because they wait for my soul.
56.7: They think they shall escape by iniquitie: O God, cast these people down in thine anger.
56.8: Thou hast counted my wandrings: put my teares into thy bottel: are they not in thy register?
56.9: When I cry, then mine enemies shall turn back: this I know, for God is with me.
56.10: I will reioyce in God because of his word: in the Lord wil I reioyce because of his word.
56.11: In God doe I trust: I will not be afrayd what man can doe unto me.
56.12: Thy vowes are upon me, O God: I will render prayses unto thee.
56.13: For thou hast delivered my soul from death, and also my feet from falling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living.

57.1: To him that excelleth. Destroy not. A Psalm of David on Michtam. When he fled from Saul in the cave. Have mercie upon me, O God, have mercie upon me: for my soul trusteth in thee, and in the shadow of thy wings wil I trust, till these afflictions overpass.
57.2: I will call unto the most high God, even to the God, that performeth his promise toward me.
57.3: He will send from heaven, and save me from the reproof of him that would swallow me. Selah. God wil send his mercy, and his trueth.
57.4: My soul is among lions: I lie among the children of men, that are set on fire: whose teeth are speares and arrowes, and their tongue a sharp sword.
57.5: Exalt thy self, O God, above the heaven, and let thy glory be upon all the earth.
57.6: They have layd a net for my steps: my soul is pressed down: they have digged a pit before me, and are fallen into the mids of it. Selah.
57.7: Mine heart is prepared, O God, mine heart is prepared: I will sing and give prayse.
57.8: Awake my tongue, awake viol and harp: I wil awake early.
57.9: I will prayse thee, O Lord, among the people, and I wil sing unto thee among the nations.
57.10: For thy mercie is great unto the heavens, and thy trueth unto the cloudes.
57.11: Exalt thy self, O God, above the heavens, and let thy glory be upon all the earth.

58.1: To him that excelleth. Destroy not. A Psalm of David on Michtam. Is it true? O Congregation, speak ye justly? O sonnes of men, judge ye uprightly?
58.2: Yea, rather ye imagine mischief in your heart: your hands execute crueltie upon the earth.
58.3: The wicked are strangers from ye womb: even from the belly have they erred, and speak lyes.
58.4: Their poyson is even like the poyson of a serpent: like ye deaf adder that stoppeth his ear.
58.5: Which heareth not the voyce of the inchanter, though he be most expert in charming.
58.6: Break their teeth, O God, in their mouthes: break the iawes of the yong lions, O Lord.
58.7: Let them melt like the waters, let them pass away: when hee shooteth his arrowes, let them be as broken.
58.8: Let them consume like a snayle that melteth, and like the untimely fruit of a woman, that hath not seen the sunne.
58.9: As raw flesh before your pots feel the fire of thornes: so let him cary them away as with a whirlewinde in his wrath.
58.10: The righteous shall reioyce when he seeeth the vengeance: he shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.
58.11: And men shall say, Verily there is fruit for the righteous: doutlesse there is a God that judgeth in the earth.

59.1: To him that excelleth. Destroy not. A Psalm of David on Michtam. When Saul sent and they did watch the house to kill him. O my God, deliver mee from mine enemies: defend me from them that rise up against me.
59.2: Deliver me from the wicked doers, and save me from the bloody men.
59.3: For loe, they have layd wait for my soul: the mightie men are gathered against me, not for mine offence, nor for my sinne, O Lord.
59.4: They runne and prepare themselves without a fault on my part: arise therefore to assist me, and behold.
59.5: Even thou, O Lord God of hostes, O God of Israel awake to visit all the heathen, and be not merciful unto all that transgress maliciously. Selah.
59.6: They goe to and from in the evening: they bark like dogs, and goe about the citie.
59.7: Behold, they brag in their talk, and swords are in their lips: for, Who, say they, doeth hear?
59.8: But thou, O Lord, shalt have them in derision, and thou shalt laugh at all the heathen.
59.9: He is strong: but I will wait upon thee: for God is my defence.
59.10: My merciful God will prevent me: God wil let me see my desire upon mine enemies.
59.11: Slay them not, least my people forget it: but scatter them abroad by thy power, and put them down, O Lord our shield,
59.12: For the sinne of their mouth, and the words of their lips: and let them be taken in their pride, even for their periurie and lies, that they speak.
59.13: Consume them in thy wrath: consume them that they be no more: and let them know that God ruleth in Iaakob, even unto the ends of the world. Selah.
59.14: And in the evening they shall go to and from, and bark like dogs, and go about the citie.
59.15: They shall runne here and there for meat: and surely they shall not be satisfied, though they tary all night.
59.16: But I wil sing of thy power, and will prayse thy mercy in the morning: for thou hast been my defence and refuge in the day of my trouble.
59.17: Unto thee, O my Strength, wil I sing: for God is my defence, and my merciful God.

60.1: To him that excelleth upon Shushan Eduth, or Michtam. A Psalm of David to teach. When he fought against Aram Naharaim, and against Aram Zobah, when Joab returned and slew twelve thousand Edomites in the salt valley. O God, thou hast cast us out, thou hast scattered us, thou hast been angry, turn again unto us.
60.2: Thou hast made the land to tremble, and hast made it to gap: heal the breaches thereof, for it is shaken.
60.3: Thou hast shewed thy people heavy things: thou hast made us to drink the wine of giddines.
60.4: But now thou hast given a banner to them that fear thee, that it may be displayed because of thy trueth. Selah.
60.5: That thy beloved may be delivered, help with thy right hand and hear me.
60.6: God hath spoken in his holines: therefore I will reioyce: I shall deuide Shechem, and measure the valley of Succoth.
60.7: Gilead shalbe mine, and Manasseh shalbe mine: Ephraim also shalbe the strength of mine head: Judah is my lawgiver.
60.8: Moab shalbe my wash pot: over Edom will I cast out my shoe: Palestina shew thy self ioyfull for me.
60.9: Who will lead me into the strong citie? who will bring me unto Edom?
60.10: Wilt not thou, O God, which hadest cast us off, and didest not go forth, O God, with our armies?
60.11: Give us help against trouble: for vain is the help of man.
60.12: Through God we shall doe valiantly: for he shall tread down our enemies.

61.1: To him that excelleth on Neginoth. A Psalm of David. Hear my cry, O God: give ear unto my prayer.
61.2: From the endes of the earth will I cry unto thee: when mine heart is opprest, bring me upon the rock that is higher then I.
61.3: For thou hast been mine hope, and a strong tower against the enemie.
61.4: I will dwell in thy Tabernacle for ever, and my trust shall be under the covering of thy wings. Selah.
61.5: For thou, O God, hast heard my desires: thou hast given an heritage unto those that fear thy Name.
61.6: Thou shalt give the King a long life: his yeeres shalbe as many ages.
61.7: Hee shall dwell before God for ever: prepare mercie and faithfulnes that they may preserve him.
61.8: So will I alway sing prayse unto thy Name in performing dayly my vowes.

62.1: To the excelletn musician Jeduthun. A Psalm of David. Yet my soul keepeth silence unto God: of him cometh my salvation.
62.2: Yet he is my strength and my salvation, and my defence: therefore I shall not much be mooued.
62.3: How long wil ye imagine mischief against a man? ye shalbe all slain: ye shalbe as a bowed wall, or as a wall shaken.
62.4: Yet they consult to cast him down from his dignitie: their delight is in lies, they bless with their mouthes, but curse with their hearts. Selah.
62.5: Yet my soul keep thou silence unto God: for mine hope is in him.
62.6: Yet is hee my strength, and my salvation, and my defence: therefore I shall not be mooued.
62.7: In God is my salvation and my glory, the rock of my strength: in God is my trust.
62.8: Trust in him alway, ye people: powre out your hearts before him, for God is our hope. Selah.
62.9: Yet the children of men are vanitie, the chief men are lies: to lay them upon a balance they are altogether lighter then vanitie.
62.10: Trust not in oppression nor in robberie: be not vain: if riches increase, set not your heart thereon.
62.11: God spake once or twise, I have heard it, that power belongeth unto God,
62.12: And to thee, O Lord, mercie: for thou rewardest every one according to his work.

63.1: A Psalm of David. When he was in the wilderness of Judah. O God, thou art my God, earely will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee: my flesh longeth greatly after thee in a barren and dry land without water.
63.2: Thus I behold thee as in the Sanctuarie, when I behold thy power and thy glorie.
63.3: For thy loving kindness is better then life: therefore my lippes shall prayse thee.
63.4: Thus will I magnifie thee all my life, and lift up mine hands in thy name.
63.5: My soul shalbe satisfied, as with marowe and fatness, and my mouth shall praise thee with ioyfull lippes,
63.6: When I remember thee on my bedde, and when I think upon thee in the night watches.
63.7: Because thou hast been mine helper, therefore under the shadow of thy wings wil I reioyce.
63.8: My soul cleaveth unto thee: for thy right hand upholdeth me.
63.9: Therefore they that seek my soul to destroy it, they shall goe into the lowest partes of the earth.
63.10: They shall cast him down with the edge of the sword, and they shall be a portion for foxes.
63.11: But the King shall reioyce in God, and all that swear by him shall reioyce in him: for the mouth of them that speak lyes, shall be stopped.

64.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. Hear my voyce, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemie.
64.2: Hide me from the conspiracie of the wicked, and from the rage of the workers of iniquitie.
64.3: Which have whette their tongue like a sword, and shot for their arrowes bitter wordes.
64.4: To shoot at the upright in secret: they shoot at him suddenly, and fear not.
64.5: They encourage themselves in a wicked purpose: they commune together to lay snares priuilie, and say, Who shall see them?
64.6: They have sought out iniquities, and have accomplished that which they sought out, even every one his secret thoughtes, and the depth of his heart.
64.7: But God will shoot an arrow at them suddenly: their strokes shalbe at once.
64.8: They shall cause their own tongue to fall upon them: and whosoever shall see them, shall flee away.
64.9: And all men shall see it, and declare the work of God, and they shall understand, what he hath wrought.
64.10: But the righteous shall be glad in the Lord, and trust in him: and all that are upright of heart, shall reioyce.

65.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm or song of David. O God, praise waiteth for thee in Zion, and unto thee shall the vow be perfourmed.
65.2: Because thou hearest the prayer, unto thee shall all flesh come.
65.3: Wicked deedes have prevailed against me: but thou wilt be merciful unto our transgressions.
65.4: Blessed is he, whom thou chusest and causest to come to thee: he shall dwell in thy courtes, and we shall be satisfied with the pleasures of thine House, even of thine holy Temple.
65.5: O God of our salvation, thou wilt answer us with fearefull signes in thy righteousnes, O thou the hope of all the ends of the earth, and of them that are far off in the sea.
65.6: He stablisheth the mountaines by his power: and is girded about with strength.
65.7: He appeaseth the noyse of the seas and the noyse of the waves thereof, and the tumults of the people.
65.8: They also, that dwell in the uttermost parts of the earth, shalbe afraid of thy signes: thou shalt make the East and the West to reioyce.
65.9: Thou visitest the earth, and waterest it: thou makest it very rich: the River of God is full of water: thou preparest them corn: for so thou appointest it.
65.10: Thou waterest abundantly the furrowes thereof: thou causest the rain to descend into the valleies thereof: thou makest it soft with showres, and blessest the bud thereof.
65.11: Thou crownest ye yeere with thy goodness, and thy steppes droppe fatness.
65.12: They drop upon the pastures of the wilderness: and the hils shalbe compassed with gladnes.
65.13: The pastures are clad with sheep: the valleis also shalbe covered with corn: therefore they shout for ioye, and sing.

66.1: To him that excelleth. A song or Psalm. Rejoice in God, all ye inhabitants of the earth.
66.2: Sing forth the glory of his name: make his praise glorious.
66.3: Say unto God, How terrible art thou in thy workes! through the greatness of thy power shall thine enemies be in subiection unto thee.
66.4: All the world shall worship thee, and sing unto thee, even sing of thy Name. Selah.
66.5: Come and behold the workes of God: he is terrible in his doing toward the sonnes of men.
66.6: He hath turned the Sea into drie land: they pass through the river on foot: there did we reioyce in him.
66.7: He ruleth the world with his power: his eyes behold the nations: the rebellious shall not exalt them selves. Selah.
66.8: Prayse our God, ye people, and make the voyce of his prayse to be heard.
66.9: Which holdeth our soules in life, and suffereth not our feet to slippe.
66.10: For thou, O God, hast proved us, thou hast tryed us as silver is tryed.
66.11: Thou hast brought us into the snare, and layed a strait chain upon our loynes.
66.12: Thou hast caused men to ryde over our heads: we went into fire and into water, but thou broughtest us out into a welthie place.
66.13: I will go into thine House with burnt offrings, and will pay thee my vowes,
66.14: Which my lippes have promised, and my mouth hath spoken in mine affliction.
66.15: I will offer unto thee the burnt offerings of fat rammes with incense: I will prepare bullocks and goates. Selah.
66.16: Come and hearken, all ye that fear God, and I will tell you what he hath done to my soul.
66.17: I called unto him with my mouth, and he was exalted with my tongue.
66.18: If I regard wickedness in mine heart, the Lord will not hear me.
66.19: But God hath heard me, and considered the voyce of my prayer.
66.20: Praysed be God, which hath not put back my prayer, nor his mercie from me.

67.1: To him that excelleth on Neginoth. A Psalm or song. God be merciful unto us, and bless us, and cause his face to shine among us. Selah.
67.2: That they may know thy way upon earth, and thy saving health among all nations.
67.3: Let the people prayse thee, O God: let all the people prayse thee.
67.4: Let the people be glad and reioyce: for thou shalt judge the people righteously, and govern the nations upon the earth. Selah.
67.5: Let the people prayse thee, O God: let all the people prayse thee.
67.6: Then shall the earth bring foorth her increase, and God, even our God shall bless us.
67.7: God shall bless us, and all the endes of the earth shall fear him.

68.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm or song of David. God will arise, and his enemies shalbe scattered: they also that hate him, shall flee before him.
68.2: As the smoke vanisheth, so shalt thou drive them away: and as wax melteth before the fire, so shall the wicked perish at the presence of God.
68.3: But the righteous shalbe glad, and reioyce before God: yea, they shall leap for ioye.
68.4: Sing unto God, and sing prayses unto his name: exalt him that rideth upon the heavens, in his Name Jah, and reioyce before him.
68.5: He is a Father of the fatherless, and a Judge of the widowes, even God in his holy habitation.
68.6: God maketh the solitarie to dwell in families, and delivereth them that were prisoners in stocks: but the rebellious shall dwell in a dry land.
68.7: O God, when thou wentest forth before thy people: when thou wentest through the wilderness, (Selah)
68.8: The earth shook, and the heavens dropped at the presence of this God: even Sinai was moved at the presence of God, even the God of Israel.
68.9: Thou, O God, sendest a gracious rain upon thine inheritance, and thou didest refresh it when it was wearie.
68.10: Thy Congregation dwelled therein: for thou, O God, hast of thy goodness prepared it for the poor.
68.11: The Lord gave matter to the women to tell of the great armie.
68.12: Kings of the armies did flee: they did flee, and she that remained in the house, deuided the spoyle.
68.13: Though ye have lien among pots, yet shall ye be as the winges of a dove that is covered with silver, and whose fethers are like yelowe gold.
68.14: When the Almightie scattered Kings in it, it was white as the snow in Zalmon.
68.15: The mountain of God is like the mountain of Bashan: it is an high Mountain, as mount Bashan.
68.16: Why leap ye, ye high mountaines? as for this Mountain, God deliteth to dwell in it: yea, the Lord will dwell in it for ever.
68.17: The charets of God are twentie thousand thousand Angels, and the Lord is among them, as in the Sanctuarie of Sinai.
68.18: Thou art gone up on high: thou hast led captiuitie captive, and received giftes for men: yea, even the rebellious hast thou led, that the Lord God might dwell there.
68.19: Praysed be the Lord, even the God of our salvation, which ladeth us dayly with benefites. Selah.
68.20: This is our God, even the God that saveth us: and to the Lord God belong the issues of death.
68.21: Surely God will wound the head of his enemies, and the hearie pate of him that walketh in his sinnes.
68.22: The Lord hath sayde, I will bring my people again from Bashan: I will bring them again from the depths of the Sea:
68.23: That thy foot may bee dipped in blood, and the tongue of thy dogges in the blood of the enemies, even in it.
68.24: They have seen, O God, thy goings, the goings of my God, and my King, which art in the Sanctuarie.
68.25: The singers went before, the players of instruments after: in the middes were the maides playing with timbrels.
68.26: Praise yee God in the assemblies, and the Lord, ye that are of the fountain of Israel.
68.27: There was litle Beniamin with their ruler, and the princes of Judah with their assemblie, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.
68.28: Thy God hath appointed thy strength: stablish, O God, that, which thou hast wrought in us,
68.29: Out of thy Temple upon Jerusalem: and Kings shall bring presents unto thee.
68.30: Destroy the company of the spearemen, and multitude of the mightie bulles with the calves of the people, that tread under feet pieces of silver: scatter the people that delite in war.
68.31: Then shall the princes come out of Egypt: Ethiopia shall hast to stretch her hands unto God.
68.32: Sing unto God, O yee kingdomes of the earth: sing praise unto the Lord, (Selah)
68.33: To him that rideth upon ye most high heavens, which were from the beginning: behold, he will send out by his voice a mightie sound.
68.34: Ascribe the power to God: for his maiestie is upon Israel, and his strength is in the cloudes.
68.35: O God, thou art terrible out of thine holie places: the God of Israel is hee that giveth strength and power unto the people: praised be God.

69.1: To him that excelleth upon Shoshannim. A Psalm of David. Save mee, O God: for the waters are entred even to my soul.
69.2: I stick fast in the deep myre, where no staie is: I am come into deep waters, and the streames runne over me.
69.3: I am wearie of crying: my throte is drie: mine eyes fail, whiles I wait for my God.
69.4: They that hate mee without a cause, are moe then the heares of mine head: they that would destroy mee, and are mine enemies falsly, are mightie, so that I restored that which I took not.
69.5: O God, thou knowest my foolishness, and my fautes are not hid from thee.
69.6: Let not them that trust in thee, O Lord God of hostes, be ashamed for me: let not those that seek thee, be confounded through mee, O God of Israel.
69.7: For thy sake have I suffred reproof: shame hath covered my face.
69.8: I am become a stranger unto my brethren, even an aliant unto my mothers sonnes.
69.9: For the zeal of thine house hath eaten mee, and the rebukes of them that rebuked thee, are fallen upon me.
69.10: I wept and my soul fasted, but that was to my reproof.
69.11: I put on a sack also: and I became a proverb unto them.
69.12: They that sat in the gate, spake of mee, and the drunkards sang of me.
69.13: But Lord, I make my praier unto thee in an acceptable time, even in the multitude of thy mercie: O God, hear me in the trueth of thy salvation.
69.14: Deliver mee out of the myre, that I sink not: let me be delivered from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.
69.15: Let not the water flood drown mee, neither let the deep swallow me up: and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.
69.16: Hear me, O Lord, for thy loving kindnes is good: turn unto me according to ye multitude of thy tender mercies.
69.17: And hide not thy face from thy servant, for I am in trouble: make haste and hear me.
69.18: Draw neere unto my soul and redeem it: deliver me because of mine enemies.
69.19: Thou hast knowen my reproof and my shame, and my dishonour: all mine adversaries are before thee.
69.20: Rebuke hath broken mine heart, and I am full of heaviness, and I looked for some to have pitie on me, but there was none: and for comforters, but I found none.
69.21: For they gave me gall in my meat, and in my thirst they gave me vineger to drink.
69.22: Let their table be a snare before them, and their prosperitie their ruin.
69.23: Let their eyes be blinded that they see not: and make their loynes alway to tremble.
69.24: Powre out thine anger upon them, and let thy wrathful displeasure take them.
69.25: Let their habitation be void, and let none dwell in their tents.
69.26: For they persecute him, whom thou hast smitten: and they add unto the sorrow of them, whom thou hast wounded.
69.27: Laie iniquitie upon their iniquitie, and let them not come into thy righteousness.
69.28: Let them be put out of the book of life, neither let them be written with the righteous.
69.29: When I am poor and in heaviness, thine help, O God, shall exalt me.
69.30: I will praise the Name of God with a song, and magnifie him with thankesgiuing.
69.31: This also shall please the Lord better then a yong bullock, that hath hornes and hoofes.
69.32: The humble shall see this, and they that seek God, shalbe glad, and your heart shall live.
69.33: For the Lord heareth the poor, and despiseth not his prisoners.
69.34: Let heaven and earth praise him: the seas and all that moveth in them.
69.35: For God will save Zion, and build the cities of Judah, that men may dwell there and have it in possession.
69.36: The seed also of his servants shall inherit it: and they that love his name, shall dwel therein.

70.1: To him excelleth. A Psalm of David to put in remembrance. O God, haste thee to deliver mee: make haste to help me, O Lord.
70.2: Let them be confounded and put to shame, that seek my soul: let them bee turned backewarde and put to rebuke, that desire mine hurt.
70.3: Let them be turned back for a reward of their shame, which said, Aha, aha.
70.4: But let all those that seek thee, be ioyfull and glad in thee, and let all that love thy salvation, say alwaies, God be praised.
70.5: Now I am poor and needie: O God, make haste to me: thou art mine helper, and my deliverer: O Lord, make no tarying.

71.1: In thee, O Lord, I trust: let me never be ashamed.
71.2: Rescue mee and deliver me in thy righteousnes: incline thine ear unto me and save me.
71.3: Be thou my strong rock, whereunto I may alway resort: thou hast given commandement to save me: for thou art my rock, and my fortress.
71.4: Deliver mee, O my God, out of the hand of the wicked: out of the hand of the evil and cruel man.
71.5: For thou art mine hope, O Lord God, even my trust from my youth.
71.6: Upon thee have I been stayed from the womb: thou art he that took me out of my mothers bowels: my praise shalbe alwaies of thee.
71.7: I am become as it were a monster unto many: but thou art my sure trust.
71.8: Let my mouth be filled with thy praise, and with thy glory every day.
71.9: Cast mee not off in the time of age: forsake me not when my strength faileth.
71.10: For mine enemies speak of mee, and they that lay wait for my soul, take their counsel together,
71.11: Saying, God hath forsaken him: pursue and take him, for there is none to deliver him.
71.12: Goe not far from me, O God: my God, haste thee to help me.
71.13: Let them be confounded and consumed that are against my soul: let them be covered with reproof and confusion, that seek mine hurt.
71.14: But I will wait continually, and will praise thee more and more.
71.15: My mouth shall daily rehearse thy righteousness, and thy salvation: for I know not the nomber.
71.16: I will goe forward in the strength of the Lord God, and will make mention of thy righteousness, even of thine onely.
71.17: O God, thou hast taught me from my youth even until now: therefore will I tell of thy wonderous workes,
71.18: Yea, even unto mine old age and graie head, O God: forsake me not, until I have declared thine arm unto this generation, and thy power to all them, that shall come.
71.19: And thy righteousnes, O God, I wil exalt on high: for thou hast done great thinges: O God, who is like unto thee!
71.20: Which hast shewed me great troubles and adversities, but thou wilt return, and revive me, and wilt come again, and take mee up from the depth of the earth.
71.21: Thou wilt increase mine honour, and return and comfort me.
71.22: Therefore will I praise thee for thy faithfulness, O God, upon instrument and viol: unto thee will I sing upon the harp, O Holy one of Israel.
71.23: My lippes will reioyce when I sing unto thee, and my soul, which thou hast delivered.
71.24: My tongue also shall talk of thy righteousness daily: for they are confounded and brought unto shame, that seek mine hurt.

72.1: A Psalm of Salomon. Give thy iudgements to the King, O God, and thy righteousness to the Kings sonne.
72.2: Then shall he judge thy people in righteousness, and thy poor with equitie.
72.3: The mountaines and the hilles shall bring peace to the people by justice.
72.4: He shall judge the poor of the people: he shall save the children of the needie, and shall subdue the oppressor.
72.5: They shall fear thee as long as the sunne and moon endureth, from generatio to generation.
72.6: He shall come down like the rayne upon the mowen grass, and as the showres that water the earth.
72.7: In his dayes shall the righteous florish, and abundance of peace shalbe so long as the moon endureth.
72.8: His dominion shall be also from sea to sea, and from the River unto the endes of the land.
72.9: They that dwell in ye wildernes, shall kneel before him, and his enemies shall lick the dust.
72.10: The Kings of Tarshish and of the yles shall bring presents: the Kings of Sheba and Seba shall bring giftes.
72.11: Yea, all Kings shall worship him: all nations shall serve him.
72.12: For he shall deliver the poor when he cryeth: the needie also, and him that hath no helper.
72.13: He shalbe merciful to the poor and needie, and shall preserve the soules of the poor.
72.14: He shall redeem their soules from deceit and violence, and dear shall their blood be in his sight.
72.15: Yea, he shall live, and unto him shall they give of the gold of Sheba: they shall also pray for him continually, and dayly bless him.
72.16: An handful of corn shall be sowen in the earth, even in the toppe of the mountaines, and the fruit thereof shall shake like the trees of Lebanon: and the children shall florish out of the citie like the grass of the earth.
72.17: His name shall be for ever: his name shall indure as long as the sunne: all nations shall bless him, and be blessed in him.
72.18: Blessed be the Lord God, even the God of Israel, which onely doeth wonderous things.
72.19: And blessed be his glorious Name for ever: and let all the earth be filled with his glorie. So be it, even so be it. HERE END THE prayers of David, the sonne of Ishai.

73.1: A Psalm committed to Asaph. Yet God is good to Israel: even, to the pure in heart.
73.2: As for me, my feet were almost gone: my steps had well neere slipt.
73.3: For I feared at the foolish, when I saw the prosperitie of the wicked.
73.4: For there are no bandes in their death, but they are lustie and strong.
73.5: They are not in trouble as other men, neither are they plagued with other men.
73.6: Therefore pride is as a chayne unto them, and crueltie covereth them as a garment.
73.7: Their eyes stand out for fatness: they have more then heart can wish.
73.8: They are licentious, and speak wickedly of their oppression: they talk presumptuously.
73.9: They set their mouth against heaven, and their tongue walketh through the earth.
73.10: Therefore his people turn hither: for waters of a full cup are wrung out to them.
73.11: And they say, How doeth God know it? or is there knowledge in the most High?
73.12: Lo, these are the wicked, yet prosper they alway, and increase in riches.
73.13: Certainely I have clensed mine heart in vain, and washed mine hands in innocencie.
73.14: For dayly have I been punished, and chastened every morning.
73.15: If I say, I will judge thus, behold the generation of thy children: I have trespassed.
73.16: Then thought I to know this, but it was too painefull for me,
73.17: Until I went into the Sanctuarie of God: then vnderstoode I their end.
73.18: Surely thou hast set them in slipperie places, and castest them down into desolation.
73.19: How suddenly are they destroyed, perished and horribly consumed,
73.20: As a dream when one awaketh! O Lord, when thou raisest us up, thou shalt make their image despised.
73.21: Certainely mine heart was vexed, and I was pricked in my reines:
73.22: So foolish was I and ignorant: I was a beast before thee.
73.23: Yet I was alway with thee: thou hast holden me by my right hand.
73.24: Thou wilt guide me by thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.
73.25: Whom have I in heaven but thee? and I have desired none in the earth with thee.
73.26: My flesh fayleth and mine heart also: but God is the strength of mine heart, and my portion for ever.
73.27: For loe, they that withdraw themselves from thee, shall perish: thou destroyest all them that goe a whoring from thee.
73.28: As for me, it is good for me to draw neere to God: therefore I have put my trust in the Lord God, that I may declare all thy workes.

74.1: A Psalm to give instruction, committed to Asaph. O God, why hast thou put us away for ever? why is thy wrath kindled against the sheep of thy pasture?
74.2: Think upon thy Congregation, which thou hast possessed of old, and on the rod of thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed, and on this mount Zion, wherein thou hast dwelt.
74.3: Lift up thy strokes, that thou mayest for ever destroy every enemie that doeth evil to the Sanctuarie.
74.4: Thine adversaries roar in the middes of thy Congregation, and set up their banners for signes.
74.5: He that lifted the axes upon the thick trees, was renowmed, as one, that brought a thing to perfection:
74.6: But now they break down the carved work thereof with axes and hammers.
74.7: They have cast thy Sanctuarie into the fire, and rased it to the ground, and have defiled the dwelling place of thy Name.
74.8: They said in their hearts, Let us destroy them altogether: they have burnt all the Synagogues of God in the land.
74.9: We see not our signes: there is not one Prophet more, nor any with us that knoweth how long.
74.10: O God, how long shall the aduersarie reproche thee? shall the enemie blaspheme thy Name for ever?
74.11: Why withdrawest thou thine hand, even thy right hand? draw it out of thy bosom, and consume them.
74.12: Even God is my King of old, working salvation in the middes of the earth.
74.13: Thou didest deuide the sea by thy power: thou brakest the heads of the dragons in the waters.
74.14: Thou brakest the head of Liuiathan in pieces, and gavest him to be meat for the people in wilderness.
74.15: Thou brakest up the fountain and river: thou dryedst up mightie rivers.
74.16: The day is thine, and the night is thine: thou hast prepared the light and the sunne.
74.17: Thou hast set all the borders of the earth: thou hast made summer and winter.
74.18: Remember this, that the enemie hath reproched the Lord, and the foolish people hath blasphemed thy Name.
74.19: Give not the soul of thy turtle dove unto the beast, and forget not the Congregation of thy poor for ever.
74.20: Consider thy covenant: for the dark places of the earth are full of the habitations of the cruel.
74.21: Oh let not the oppressed return ashamed, but let the poor and needie prayse thy Name.
74.22: Arise, O God: mainteine thine own cause: remember thy dayly reproche by the foolish man.
74.23: Forget not the voyce of thine enemies: for the tumult of them, that rise against thee, ascendeth continually.

75.1: To him that excelleth. Destroy not. A Psalm or song committed toAsaph. We will prayse thee, O God, we will prayse thee, for thy Name is neere: therefore they will declare thy wonderous workes.
75.2: When I shall take a convenient time, I will judge righteously.
75.3: The earth and all the inhabitantes thereof are dissolved: but I will establish the pillars of it. Selah.
75.4: I said unto the foolish, Be not so foolish, and to the wicked, Lift not up the horn.
75.5: Lift not up your horn on high, neither speak with a stiff neck.
75.6: For to come to preferment is neither from the East, nor from the West, nor from the South,
75.7: But God is the judge: he maketh low and he maketh hie.
75.8: For in the hand of the Lord is a cup, and the wine is red: it is full mixt, and he powreth out of the same: surely all the wicked of the earth shall wring out and drink the dregges thereof.
75.9: But I will declare for ever, and sing prayses unto the God of Iaakob.
75.10: All the hornes of the wicked also will I break: but the hornes of the righteous shalbe exalted.

76.1: To him that excelleth on Neginoth. A Psalm or song committed to Asaph. God is knowen in Judah: his Name is great in Israel.
76.2: For in Shalem is his Tabernacle, and his dwelling in Zion.
76.3: There brake he the arrowes of the bow, the shield and the sword and the battell. Selah.
76.4: Thou art more bright and puissant, then the mountaines of pray.
76.5: The stout hearted are spoyled: they have slept their sleep, and all the men of strength have not found their hands.
76.6: At thy rebuke, O God of Iaakob, both the chariot and horse are cast a sleep.
76.7: Thou, even thou art to be feared: and who shall stand in thy sight, when thou art angrie!
76.8: Thou didest cause thy iudgement to bee heard from heaven: therefore the earth feared and was still,
76.9: When thou, O God, arose to iudgement, to help all the meek of the earth. Selah.
76.10: Surely the rage of man shall turn to thy praise: the remnant of the rage shalt thou restrayne.
76.11: Vow and perform unto the Lord your God, all ye that be round about him: let them bring presents unto him that ought to be feared.
76.12: He shall cut off the spirit of princes: he is terrible to the Kings of the earth.

77.1: For the excellent musician Jeduthun. A Psalm committed to Asaph. My voyce came to God, when I cryed: my voyce came to God, and he heard me.
77.2: In the day of my trouble I sought ye Lord: my sore ranne and ceased not in the night: my soul refused comfort.
77.3: I did think upon God, and was troubled: I praied, and my spirit was full of anguish. Selah.
77.4: Thou keepest mine eyes waking: I was astonied and could not speak.
77.5: Then I considered the daies of old, and the yeeres of ancient time.
77.6: I called to remembrance my song in the night: I communed with mine own heart, and my spirit searched diligently.
77.7: Will the Lord absent him self for ever? and will he shew no more fauour?
77.8: Is his mercie clean gone for ever? doeth his promise fail for evermore?
77.9: Hath God forgotten to be merciful? hath he shut up his teder mercies in displeasure? Selah.
77.10: And I sayde, This is my death: yet I remembred the yeeres of the right hand of the most High.
77.11: I remembred the workes of the Lord: certainely I remembred thy wonders of old.
77.12: I did also meditate all thy woorkes, and did devise of thine actes, saying,
77.13: Thy way, O God, is in the Sanctuarie: who is so great a God as our God!
77.14: Thou art ye God that doest wonders: thou hast declared thy power among the people.
77.15: Thou hast redeemed thy people with thine arm, even the sonnes of Iaakob and Joseph. Selah.
77.16: The waters saw thee, O God: the waters saw thee, and were afraid: yea, the depths trembled.
77.17: The cloudes powred out water: the heavens gave a sound: yea, thine arrowes went abroad.
77.18: The voyce of thy thunder was round about: the lightnings lightened the world: the earth trembled and shook.
77.19: Thy way is in the Sea, and thy paths in the great waters, and thy footesteps are not knowen.
77.20: Thou diddest lead thy people like sheep by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

78.1: A Psalm to give instruction committed to Asaph. Hear my doctrine, O my people: incline your eares unto the wordes of my mouth.
78.2: I will open my mouth in a parable: I will declare high sentences of old.
78.3: Which we have heard and knowen, and our fathers have told us.
78.4: Wee will not hide them from their children but to the generation to come we wil shew the praises of the Lord his power also, and his wonderful woorkes that he hath done:
78.5: How he established a testimonie in Iaakob, and ordeined a Law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should teach their children:
78.6: That the posteritie might know it, and the children, which should be borne, should stand up, and declare it to their children:
78.7: That they might set their hope on God, and not forget the workes of God but keep his commandements:
78.8: And not to bee as their fathers, a disobedient and rebellious generation: a generation that set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not faithful unto God.
78.9: The children of Ephraim being armed and shooting with the bow, turned back in the day of battell.
78.10: They kept not the covenant of God, but refused to walk in his Law,
78.11: And forgat his Actes, and his wonderful woorkes that he had shewed them.
78.12: Hee did marueilous thinges in the sight of their fathers in the land of Egypt: even in the field of Zoan.
78.13: He deuided the Sea, and led them through: he made also the waters to stand as an heap.
78.14: In the day time also hee led them with a cloud, and all the night with a light of fire.
78.15: He clave the rockes in the wildernes, and gave them drink as of the great depths.
78.16: He brought floods also out of the stonie rock; so that hee made the waters to descend like the rivers.
78.17: Yet they sinned stil against him, and provoked the Highest in the wilderness,
78.18: And tempted God in their heartes in requiring meat for their lust.
78.19: They spake against God also, saying, Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?
78.20: Behold, he smote the rock, that the water gushed out, and the streames overflowed: can hee give bread also? or prepare flesh for his people?
78.21: Therefore the Lord heard and was angrie, and the fire was kindled in Iaakob, and also wrath came upon Israel,
78.22: Because they beleeued not in God, and trusted not in his help.
78.23: Yet he had comanded the clouds above, and had opened the doores of heaven,
78.24: And had rained down MAN upon them for to eat, and had given them of the wheat of heaven.
78.25: Man did eat the bread of Angels: hee sent them meat ynough.
78.26: He caused the Eastwinde to pass in the heaven, and through his power he brought in the Southwinde.
78.27: Hee rained flesh also upon them as dust, and feathered fowl as the sand of the sea.
78.28: And hee made it fall in the middes of their camp even round about their habitations.
78.29: So they did eat and were well filled: for he gave them their desire.
78.30: They were not turned from their lust, but the meat was yet in their mouthes,
78.31: When the wrath of God came even upon them, and slew the strongest of them, and smote down the chosen men in Israel.
78.32: For all this, they sinned stil, and beleeued not his wonderous woorkes.
78.33: Therefore their daies did hee consume in vanitie, and their yeeres hastily.
78.34: And when hee slew them, they sought him and they returned, and sought God earely.
78.35: And they remembred that God was their strength, and the most high God their redeemer.
78.36: But they flattered him with their mouth, and dissembled with him with their tongue.
78.37: For their heart was not upright with him: neither were they faithful in his covenant.
78.38: Yet he being merciful forgave their iniquitie, and destroied them not, but oft times called back his anger, and did not stirre up all his wrath.
78.39: For he remembered that they were flesh: yea, a wind that passeth and cometh not again.
78.40: How oft did they provoke him in the wildernes? and grieve him in the desert?
78.41: Yea, they returned, and tempted God, and limited the Holie one of Israel.
78.42: They remembered not his hand, nor the day when he delivered them from the enemie,
78.43: Nor him that set his signes in Egypt, and his wonders in the field of Zoan,
78.44: And turned their rivers into blood, and their floods, that they could not drink.
78.45: Hee sent a swarm of flies among them, which deuoured them, and frogs, which destroyed them.
78.46: He gave also their fruites unto the caterpiller, and their labour unto the grassehopper.
78.47: He destroied their vines with hail, and their wild figge trees with the hailestone.
78.48: He gave their cattell also to the hail, and their flockes to the thunderboltes.
78.49: Hee cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, indignation and wrath, and vexation by the sending out of evil Angels.
78.50: He made a way to his anger: he spared not their soul from death, but gave their life to the pestilence,
78.51: And smote al the firstborn in Egypt, even the beginning of their strength in the tabernacles of Ham.
78.52: But hee made his people to goe out like sheep, and led them in the wildernes like a flock.
78.53: Yea, he caried them out safely, and they feared not, and the Sea covered their enemies.
78.54: And he brought them unto the borders of his Sanctuarie: even to this Mountain, which his right hand purchased.
78.55: He cast out the heath also before them, and caused them to fall to the lot of his inheritance, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tabernacles.
78.56: Yet they tempted, and provoked the most high God, and kept not his testimonies,
78.57: But turned back and delt falsely like their fathers: they turned like a deceitful bow.
78.58: And they provoked him to anger with their high places, and mooued him to wrath with their graven images.
78.59: God heard this and was wroth, and greatly abhorred Israel,
78.60: So that hee forsook the habitation of Shilo, even the Tabernacle where hee dwelt among men,
78.61: And delivered his power into captiuitie, and his beautie into the enemies hand.
78.62: And hee gave up his people to the sword, and was angrie with his inheritance.
78.63: The fire deuoured their chosen men, and their maides were not praised.
78.64: Their Priestes fell by the sword, and their widowes lamented not.
78.65: But the Lord awaked as one out of sleep, and as a strong man that after his wine crieth out,
78.66: And smote his enemies in the hinder parts, and put them to a perpetual shame.
78.67: Yet he refused the tabernacle of Joseph, and chose not the tribe of Ephraim:
78.68: But chose the tribe of Judah, and mount Zion which he loved.
78.69: And he built his Sanctuarie as an high palace, like the earth, which he stablished for ever.
78.70: He chose David also his servant, and took him from the shepefolds.
78.71: Even from behind the ewes with yong brought he him to feed his people in Iaakob, and his inheritance in Israel.
78.72: So he fed them according to the simplicitie of his heart, and guided them by the discretion of his hands.

79.1: A Psalm committed to Asaph. O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance: thine holy Temple have they defiled, and made Jerusalem heapes of stones.
79.2: The dead bodies of thy seruats have they given to be meat unto foules of ye heaven: and the flesh of thy Saintes unto the beastes of the earth.
79.3: Their blood have they shead like waters round about Jerusalem, and there was none to burie them.
79.4: Wee are a reproche to our neighbours, even a scorn and derision unto them that are round about us.
79.5: Lord, how long wilt thou be angrie, for ever? shall thy gelousie burn like fire?
79.6: Powre out thy wrath upon the heathen that have not knowen thee, and upon the kingdomes that have not called upon thy Name.
79.7: For they have deuoured Iaakob and made his dwelling place desolate.
79.8: Remember not against us the former iniquities, but make haste and let thy tender mercies prevent us: for we are in great miserie.
79.9: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glorie of thy Name, and deliver us, and be merciful unto our sinnes for thy Names sake.
79.10: Wherefore should the heathen say, Where is their God? let him be knowen among the heathen in our sight by the vengeance of the blood of thy servants that is shed.
79.11: Let the sighing of the prisoners come before thee: according to thy mightie arm preserve the children of death,
79.12: And render to our neighbours seven fold into their bosom their reproche, wherewith they have reproched thee, O Lord.
79.13: So wee thy people, and sheep of thy pasture shall praise thee for ever: and from generation to generation we will set foorth thy praise.

80.1: To him that excelleth on Shoshannim Eduth. A Psalm committed to Asaph. Hear, O thou Shepheard of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like sheep: shew thy brightnes, thou that sittest between the Cherubims.
80.2: Before Ephraim and Beniamin and Manasseh stirre up thy strength, and come to help us.
80.3: Turn us again, O God, and cause thy face to shine that we may be saved.
80.4: O Lord God of hostes, how long wilt thou be angrie against the prayer of thy people?
80.5: Thou hast fedde them with the bread of teares, and given them teares to drink with great measure.
80.6: Thou hast made us a strife unto our neighbours, and our enemies laugh at us among themselves.
80.7: Turn us again, O God of hostes: cause thy face to shine, and we shalbe saved.
80.8: Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the heathen, and planted it.
80.9: Thou madest roume for it, and didest cause it to take root, and it filled the land.
80.10: The mountaines were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughes thereof were like the goodly cedars.
80.11: She stretched out her branches unto the Sea, and her boughes unto the River.
80.12: Why hast thou then broken down her hedges, so that all they, which pass by the way, have plucked her?
80.13: The wild bore out of the wood hath destroyed it, and the wild beastes of the field have eaten it up.
80.14: Return we beseech thee, O God of hostes: look down from heaven and behold and visit this vine,
80.15: And the vineyard, that thy right hand hath planted, and the young vine, which thou madest strong for thy self.
80.16: It is burnt with fire and cut down: and they perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.
80.17: Let thine hand be upon the man of thy right hand, and upon the sonne of man, whom thou madest strong for thine own self.
80.18: So will not we goe back from thee: revive thou us, and we shall call upon thy Name.
80.19: Turn us again, O Lord God of hostes: cause thy face to shine and we shalbe saved.

81.1: To him that excelleth upon Gittith. A Psalm committed to Asaph. Sing joyfully unto God our strength: sing loud unto the God of Iaakob.
81.2: Take the song and bring forth the timbrel, the pleasant harp with the viol.
81.3: Blow the trumpet in the new moon, even in the time appointed, at our feast day.
81.4: For this is a statute for Israel, and a Law of the God of Iaakob.
81.5: Hee set this in Joseph for a testimonie, when hee came out of the land of Egypt, where I heard a language, that I vnderstoode not.
81.6: I have withdrawen his shoulder from the burden, and his handes have left the pots.
81.7: Thou calledst in affliction and I delivered thee, and answered thee in the secret of the thunder: I prooued thee at the waters of Meribah. Selah.
81.8: Hear, O my people, and I wil protest unto thee: O Israel, if thou wilt hearken unto me,
81.9: Let there bee no strange god in thee, neither worship thou any strange god.
81.10: For I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt: open thy mouth wide and I will fill it.
81.11: But my people would not hear my voyce, and Israel would none of me.
81.12: So I gave them up unto the hardness of their heart, and they have walked in their own cousels.
81.13: Oh that my people had hearkened unto me, and Israel had walked in my wayes.
81.14: I would soon have humbled their enemies, and turned mine hand against their adversaries.
81.15: The haters of the Lord should have been subiect unto him, and their time should have endured for ever.
81.16: And God would have fedde them with the fatte of wheat, and with honie out of the rock would I have sufficed thee.

82.1: A Psalm committed to Aspah. God standeth in the assemblie of gods: hee judgeth among gods.
82.2: How long wil ye judge vniustly, and accept the persons of the wicked? Selah.
82.3: Doe right to the poor and fatherless: doe justice to the poor and needie.
82.4: Deliver the poor and needie: save them from the hand of the wicked.
82.5: They know not and understand nothing: they walk in darkenes, albeit all the foundations of the earth be mooued.
82.6: I have said, Ye are gods, and ye all are children of the most High.
82.7: But ye shall die as a man, and yee princes, shall fall like others.
82.8: O God, arise, therefore judge thou the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.

83.1: A song, or Psalm committed to Asaph. Keep not thou silence, O God: bee not still, and cease not, O God.
83.2: For lo, thine enemies make a tumult: and they that hate thee, have lifted up the head.
83.3: They have taken craftie counsel against thy people, and have consulted against thy secret ones.
83.4: They have said, Come and let us cut them off from being a nation: and let the name of Israel be no more in remembrance.
83.5: For they have consulted together in heart, and have made a league against thee:
83.6: The tabernacles of Edom, and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Agarims:
83.7: Gebal and Ammon, and Amalech, the Philistims with the inhabitants of Tyrus:
83.8: Asshur also is ioyned with them: they have been an arm to the children of Lot. Selah.
83.9: Doe thou to them as unto the Midianites: as to Sisera and as to Jabin at the river of Kishon.
83.10: They perished at En-dor, and were dung for the earth.
83.11: Make them, even their princes like Oreb and like Zeeb: yea, all their princes like Zebah and like Zalmuna.
83.12: Which have said, Let us take for our possession the habitations of God.
83.13: O my God, make them like unto a wheel, and as the stubble before the wind.
83.14: As the fire burneth the forest, and as the flame setteth the mountaines on fire:
83.15: So persecute them with thy tempest, and make them afraid with thy storm.
83.16: Fill their faces with shame, that they may seek thy Name, O Lord.
83.17: Let them be confounded and troubled for ever: yea, let them be put to shame and perish,
83.18: That they may know that thou, which art called Jehovah, art alone, even the most High over all the earth.

84.1: To him that excelleth upon Gittith. A Psalm committed to the sonnes of Korah. O Lord of hostes, how amiable are thy Tabernacles!
84.2: My soul longeth, yea, and fainteth for the courtes of the Lord: for mine heart and my flesh reioyce in the living God.
84.3: Yea, the sparrow hath found her an house, and the swallow a nest for her, where she may lay her yong: even by thine altars, O Lord of hostes, my King and my God.
84.4: Blessed are they that dwell in thine house: they will ever praise thee. Selah.
84.5: Blessed is the man, whose strength is in thee, and in whose heart are thy wayes.
84.6: They going through the vale of Baca, make welles therein: the rain also covereth the pooles.
84.7: They goe from strength to strength, till every one appear before God in Zion.
84.8: O Lord God of hostes, hear my prayer: hearken, O God of Iaakob. Selah.
84.9: Behold, O God, our shield, and look upon the face of thine Anointed.
84.10: For a day in thy courtes is better then a thousand other where: I had rather be a door keeper in the House of my God, then to dwell in the Tabernacles of wickedness.
84.11: For the Lord God is the sunne and shield unto us: the Lord will give grace and glory, and no good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.
84.12: O Lord of hostes, blessed is the man that trusteth in thee.

85.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm committed to the sonnes of Korah. Lord, thou hast been fauourable unto thy land: thou hast brought again the captiuitie of Iaakob.
85.2: Thou hast forgiven the iniquitie of thy people, and covered all their sinnes. Selah.
85.3: Thou hast withdrawen all thine anger, and hast turned back from the fiercenes of thy wrath.
85.4: Turn us, O God of our salvation, and release thine anger toward us.
85.5: Wilt thou be angry with us for ever? and wilt thou prolong thy wrath from one generation to another?
85.6: Wilt thou not turn again and quicken us, that thy people may reioyce in thee?
85.7: Shew us thy mercie, O Lord, and graunt us thy salvation.
85.8: I will hearken what the Lord God will say: for he will speak peace unto his people, and to his Saintes, that they turn not again to follie.
85.9: Surely his salvation is neere to them that fear him, that glory may dwell in our land.
85.10: Mercie and trueth shall meet: righteousnes and peace shall kiss one another.
85.11: Trueth shall bud out of the earth, and righteousnes shall look down from heaven.
85.12: Yea, the Lord shall give good things, and our land shall give her increase.
85.13: Righteousness shall go before him, and shall set her steps in the way.

86.1: A prayer of David. Incline thine ear, O Lord, and hear me: for I am poor and needy.
86.2: Preserve thou my soul, for I am merciful: my God, save thou thy servant, that trusteth in thee.
86.3: Be merciful unto me, O Lord: for I crie upon thee continually.
86.4: Reioyce the soul of thy servant: for unto thee, O Lord, doe I lift up my soul.
86.5: For thou, Lord, art good and merciful, and of great kindenes unto all them, that call upon thee.
86.6: Give ear, Lord, unto my prayer, and hearken to the voyce of my supplication.
86.7: In the day of my trouble I will call upon thee: for thou hearest me.
86.8: Among the gods there is none like thee, O Lord, and there is none that can doe like thy workes.
86.9: All nations, whom thou hast made, shall come and worship before thee, O Lord, and shall glorifie thy Name.
86.10: For thou art great and doest wonderous things: thou art God alone.
86.11: Teach me thy way, O Lord, and I will walk in thy trueth: knit mine heart unto thee, that I may fear thy Name.
86.12: I wil prayse thee, O Lord my God, with all mine heart: yea, I wil glorifie thy Name for ever.
86.13: For great is thy mercie toward me, and thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest grave.
86.14: O God, the proud are risen against me, and the assemblies of violent men have sought my soul, and have not set thee before them.
86.15: But thou, O Lord, art a pitiful God and merciful, slow to anger and great in kindenes and trueth.
86.16: Turn unto me, and have mercy upon me: give thy strength unto thy servant, and save the sonne of thine handmayd.
86.17: Shew a token of thy goodnes toward me, that they which hate me, may see it, and be ashamed, because thou, O Lord, hast holpen me and comforted me.

87.1: A Psalm or song committed to the sonnes of Korah. God layde his foundations among the holy mountaines.
87.2: The Lord loveth the gates of Zion above all the habitations of Iaakob.
87.3: Glorious things are spoken of thee, O citie of God. Selah.
87.4: I will make mention of Rahab and Babel among them that know me: behold Palestina and Tyrus with Ethiopia, There is he borne.
87.5: And of Zion it shall be sayde, Many are borne in her: and he, even the most High shall stablish her.
87.6: The Lord shall count, when hee writeth the people, He was borne there. Selah.
87.7: Aswell the singers as the players on instruments shall prayse thee: all my springs are in thee.

88.1: A song or Psalm of Heman the Ezrahite to give instruction, committed to the sonnes of Korah for him that excelleth upon Malath Leannoth. O Lord God of my salvation, I cry day and night before thee.
88.2: Let my prayer enter into thy presence: incline thine ear unto my cry.
88.3: For my soul is filled with evils, and my life draweth neere to the grave.
88.4: I am counted among them that go down unto the pit, and am as a man without strength:
88.5: Free among the dead, like the slain lying in the grave, whom thou remembrest no more, and they are cut off from thine hand.
88.6: Thou hast layde me in the lowest pit, in darkenes, and in the deep.
88.7: Thine indignation lyeth upon me, and thou hast vexed me with all thy waves. Selah.
88.8: Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me, and made mee to be abhorred of them: I am shut up, and cannot get foorth.
88.9: Mine eye is sorowfull through mine affliction: Lord, I call dayly upon thee: I stretch out mine hands unto thee.
88.10: Wilt thou shew a miracle to the dead? or shall the dead rise and prayse thee? Selah.
88.11: Shall thy loving kindenes be declared in the grave? or thy faithfulnes in destruction?
88.12: Shall thy wonderous workes be knowen in the dark? and thy righteousnes in the land of obliuion?
88.13: But unto thee have I cryed, O Lord, and early shall my prayer come before thee.
88.14: Lord, why doest thou reiect my soul, and hidest thy face from me?
88.15: I am afflicted and at the point of death: from my youth I suffer thy terrours, doubting of my life.
88.16: Thine indignations goe over me, and thy fear hath cut me off.
88.17: They came round about me dayly like water, and compassed me together.
88.18: My lovers and friends hast thou put away from me, and mine acquaintance hid themselves.

89.1: A Psalm to give instruction, of Ethan the Ezrahite. I will sing the mercies of the Lord for ever: with my mouth will I declare thy trueth from generation to generation.
89.2: For I said, Mercie shalbe set up for ever: thy trueth shalt thou stablish in ye very heavens.
89.3: I have made a covenant with my chosen: I have sworn to David my servant,
89.4: Thy seed will I stablish for ever, and set up thy throne from generation to generation. Selah.
89.5: O Lord, even the heavens shall prayse thy wonderous work: yea, thy trueth in the Congregation of the Saints.
89.6: For who is equal to the Lord in the heaven? and who is like the Lord among the sonnes of the gods?
89.7: God is very terrible in the assemblie of the Saints, and to be reverenced above all, that are about him.
89.8: O Lord God of hostes, who is like unto thee, which art a mightie Lord, and thy trueth is about thee?
89.9: Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them.
89.10: Thou hast beaten down Rahab as a man slain: thou hast scattered thine enemies with thy mightie arm.
89.11: The heavens are thine, the earth also is thine: thou hast layde the foundation of the world, and all that therein is.
89.12: Thou hast created the North and the South: Tabor and Hermon shall reioyce in thy Name.
89.13: Thou hast a mightie arm: strong is thine hand, and high is thy right hand.
89.14: Righteousness and equitie are the stablishment of thy throne: mercy and trueth goe before thy face.
89.15: Blessed is the people, that can reioyce in thee: they shall walk in the light of thy countenance, O Lord.
89.16: They shall reioyce continually in thy Name, and in thy righteousnes shall they exalt them selves.
89.17: For thou art the glory of their strength, and by thy fauour our hornes shall be exalted.
89.18: For our shield apperteineth to the Lord, and our King to the holy one of Israel.
89.19: Thou spakest then in a vision unto thine Holy one, and saydest, I have layde help upon one that is mightie: I have exalted one chosen out of the people.
89.20: I have found David my servant: with mine holy oyle have I anoynted him.
89.21: Therefore mine hand shall be established with him, and mine arm shall strengthen him.
89.22: The enemie shall not oppress him, neither shall the wicked hurt him.
89.23: But I will destroy his foes before his face, and plague them that hate him.
89.24: My trueth also and my mercie shall be with him, and in my Name shall his horn be exalted.
89.25: I will set his hand also in the sea, and his right hand in the floods.
89.26: He shall cry unto mee, Thou art my Father, my God and the rock of my salvation.
89.27: Also I wil make him my first borne, higher then the Kings of the earth.
89.28: My mercie will I keep for him for evermore, and my covenant shall stand fast with him.
89.29: His seed also will I make to endure for ever, and his throne as the dayes of heaven.
89.30: But if his children forsake my Law, and walk not in my iudgements:
89.31: If they break my statutes, and keep not my commandements:
89.32: Then will I visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquitie with strokes.
89.33: Yet my loving kindness will I not take from him, neither will I falsifie my trueth.
89.34: My covenant wil I not break, nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips.
89.35: I have sworn once by mine holines, that I will not fayle David, saying,
89.36: His seed shall endure for ever, and his throne shalbe as the sunne before me.
89.37: He shalbe established for evermore as the moon, and as a faythfull witnes in the heaven. Selah.
89.38: But thou hast reiected and abhorred, thou hast been angry with thine Anoynted.
89.39: Thou hast broken the covenant of thy servant, and profaned his crown, casting it on the ground.
89.40: Thou hast broken down all his walles: thou hast layd his fortresses in ruin.
89.41: All that goe by the way, spoyle him: he is a rebuke unto his neighbours.
89.42: Thou hast set up the right hand of his enemies, and made all his adversaries to reioyce.
89.43: Thou hast also turned the edge of his sword, and hast not made him to stand in the battell.
89.44: Thou hast caused his dignitie to decay, and cast his throne to the ground.
89.45: The dayes of his youth hast thou shortned, and covered him with shame. Selah.
89.46: Lord, how long wilt thou hide thy self, for ever? shall thy wrath burn like fire?
89.47: Remember of what time I am: wherefore shouldest thou create in vain all the children of men?
89.48: What man liveth, and shall not see death? shall hee deliver his soul from the hand of the grave? Selah.
89.49: Lord, where are thy former mercies, which thou swarest unto David in thy trueth?
89.50: Remember, O Lord, the rebuke of thy servants, which I bear in my bosom of all the mightie people.
89.51: For thine enemies have reproched thee, O Lord, because they have reproched the footesteps of thine Anointed.
89.52: Praised be the Lord for evermore. So be it, even so be it.

90.1: A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, thou hast been our habitation from generation to generation.
90.2: Before the mountaines were made, and before thou hadst formed the earth, and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting thou art our God.
90.3: Thou turnest man to destruction: again thou sayest, Return, ye sonnes of Adam.
90.4: For a thousand yeeres in thy sight are as yesterday when it is past, and as a watch in the night.
90.5: Thou hast overflowed them: they are as a sleep: in the morning he groweth like the grass:
90.6: In the morning it florisheth and groweth, but in the evening it is cut down and withereth.
90.7: For we are consumed by thine anger, and by thy wrath are we troubled.
90.8: Thou hast set our iniquities before thee, and our secret sinnes in the light of thy countenance.
90.9: For all our dayes are past in thine anger: we have spent our yeeres as a thought.
90.10: The time of our life is threescore yeeres and ten, and if they be of strength, fourescore yeeres: yet their strength is but labour and sorowe: for it is cut off quickly, and we flee away.
90.11: Who knoweth the power of thy wrath? for according to thy fear is thine anger.
90.12: Teach us so to nomber our dayes, that we may apply our heartes unto wisdom.
90.13: Return (O Lord, how long?) and be pacified toward thy servants.
90.14: Fill us with thy mercie in the morning: so shall we reioyce and be glad all our dayes.
90.15: Comfort us according to the dayes that thou hast afflicted us, and according to the yeeres that we have seen evil.
90.16: Let thy work bee seen toward thy servants, and thy glory upon their children.
90.17: And let the beautie of the Lord our God be upon us, and direct thou the work of our hands upon us, even direct the work of our handes.

91.1: Who so dwelleth in the secret of the most High, shall abide in the shadow of the Almightie.
91.2: I will say unto the Lord, O mine hope, and my fortress: he is my God, in him will I trust.
91.3: Surely he will deliver thee from the snare of the hunter, and from the noysome pestilence.
91.4: Hee will cover thee under his winges, and thou shalt be sure under his feathers: his trueth shall be thy shield and buckler.
91.5: Thou shalt not be afraid of the fear of the night, nor of the arrow that flyeth by day:
91.6: Nor of the pestilence that walketh in the darkenesse: nor of the plague that destroyeth at noon day.
91.7: A thousand shall fall at thy side, and tenne thousand at thy right hand, but it shall not come neere thee.
91.8: Doubtless with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.
91.9: For thou hast said, The Lord is mine hope: thou hast set the most High for thy refuge.
91.10: There shall none evil come unto thee, neither shall any plague come neere thy tabernacle.
91.11: For hee shall give his Angels charge over thee to keep thee in all thy wayes.
91.12: They shall bear thee in their handes, that thou hurt not thy foot against a stone.
91.13: Thou shalt walk upon the lyon and asp: the yong lyon and the dragon shalt thou tread under feet.
91.14: Because he hath loved me, therefore will I deliver him: I will exalt him because hee hath knowen my Name.
91.15: He shall call upon me, and I wil hear him: I will be with him in trouble: I will deliver him, and glorifie him.
91.16: With long life wil I satisfie him, and shew him my salvation.

92.1: A Psalm or song for the Sabbath day. It is a good thing to praise the Lord, and to sing unto thy Name, O most High,
92.2: To declare thy loving kindenesse in the morning, and thy trueth in the night,
92.3: Upon an instrument of tenne strings, and upon the viol with the song upon the harp.
92.4: For thou, Lord, hast made mee glad by thy workes, and I wil reioyce in the workes of thine handes.
92.5: O Lord, how glorious are thy workes! and thy thoughtes are very deep.
92.6: An unwise man knoweth it not, and a fool doeth not understand this,
92.7: (When the wicked grow as the grass, and all the workers of wickedness doe flourish) that they shall be destroyed for ever.
92.8: But thou, O Lord, art most High for evermore.
92.9: For loe, thine enemies, O Lord: for loe, thine enemies shall perish: all the workers of iniquitie shall be destroyed.
92.10: But thou shalt exalt mine horn, like the vnicornes, and I shalbe anoynted with fresh oyle.
92.11: Mine eye also shall see my desire against mine enemies: and mine eares shall hear my wish against the wicked, that rise up against me.
92.12: The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree, and shall grow like a Cedar in Lebanon.
92.13: Such as bee planted in the house of the Lord, shall flourish in the courtes of our God.
92.14: They shall still bring foorth fruit in their age: they shall be fat and flourishing,
92.15: To declare that the Lord my rock is righteous, and that none iniquitie is in him.

93.1: The Lord reigneth, and is clothed with maiestie: the Lord is clothed, and girded with power: the world also shall be established, that it cannot be mooued.
93.2: Thy throne is established of old: thou art from everlasting.
93.3: The floodes have lifted up, O Lord: the floodes have lifted up their voyce: the floods lift up their waves.
93.4: The waves of ye sea are marueilous through the noyse of many waters, yet the Lord on High is more mightie.
93.5: Thy testimonies are very sure: holiness becometh thine House, O Lord, for ever.

94.1: O Lord God the avenger, O God the avenger, shew thy self clearely.
94.2: Exalt thy self, O Judge of the world, and render a reward to the proud.
94.3: Lord how long shall the wicked, how long shall the wicked triumph?
94.4: They prate and speak fiercely: all the workers of iniquitie vaunt themselves.
94.5: They smite down thy people, O Lord, and trouble thine heritage.
94.6: They slay the widow and the stranger, and murder the fatherless.
94.7: Yet they say, The Lord shall not see: neither will the God of Iaakob regard it.
94.8: Vnderstande ye unwise among the people: and ye fooles, when will ye be wise?
94.9: Hee that planted the ear, shall hee not hear? or he that formed the eye, shall he not see?
94.10: Or he that chastiseth the nations, shall he not correct? hee that teacheth man knowledge, shall he not know?
94.11: The Lord knoweth the thoughtes of man, that they are vanitie.
94.12: Blessed is the man, whom thou chastisest, O Lord, and teachest him in thy Law,
94.13: That thou mayest give him rest from the dayes of evil, whiles the pitte is digged for the wicked.
94.14: Surely the Lord will not fail his people, neither will he forsake his inheritance.
94.15: For iudgement shall return to justice, and all the upright in heart shall follow after it.
94.16: Who will rise up with me against the wicked? or who will take my part against the workers of iniquitie?
94.17: If the Lord had not holpen me, my soul had almost dwelt in silence.
94.18: When I said, My foot slideth, thy mercy, O Lord, stayed me.
94.19: In the multitude of my thoughts in mine heart, thy comfortes have reioyced my soul.
94.20: Hath the throne of iniquitie fellowship with thee, which forgeth wrong for a Law?
94.21: They gather them together against the soul of the righteous, and condemn the innocent blood.
94.22: But the Lord is my refuge, and my God is the rock of mine hope.
94.23: And hee will recompence them their wickednes, and destroy them in their own malice: yea, the Lord our God shall destroy them.

95.1: Come, let us reioyce unto the Lord: let us sing aloud unto the rock of our salvation.
95.2: Let us come before his face with praise: let us sing loud unto him with Psalmes.
95.3: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods.
95.4: In whose hand are the deep places of the earth, and the heightes of the mountaines are his:
95.5: To whom the Sea belongeth: for hee made it, and his handes formed the dry land.
95.6: Come, let us worship and fall down, and kneel before the Lord our maker.
95.7: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand: to day, if ye will hear his voyce,
