95.8: Harden not your heart, as in Meribah, and as in the day of Massah in the wilderness.
95.9: Where your fathers tempted me, proved me, though they had seen my work.
95.10: Fourtie yeeres have I contended with this generation, and said, They are a people that ere in heart, for they have not knowen my wayes.
95.11: Wherefore I sware in my wrath, saying, Surely they shall not enter into my rest.

96.1: Sing unto the Lord a new song: sing unto the Lord, all the earth.
96.2: Sing unto the Lord, and prayse his Name: declare his salvation from day to day.
96.3: Declare his glory among all nations, and his wonders among all people.
96.4: For the Lord is great and much to be praysed: he is to be feared above all gods.
96.5: For all the gods of the people are idoles: but the Lord made the heavens.
96.6: Strength and glory are before him: power and beautie are in his Sanctuarie.
96.7: Give unto the Lord, ye families of the people: give unto the Lord glory and power.
96.8: Give unto the Lord the glory of his Name: bring an offering, and enter into his courtes.
96.9: Worship the Lord in the glorious Sanctuarie: tremble before him all the earth.
96.10: Say among the nations, The Lord reigneth: surely the world shalbe stable, and not move, and he shall judge the people in righteousness.
96.11: Let the heavens reioyce, and let the earth be glad: let the sea roar, and all that therein is.
96.12: Let the field be ioyfull, and all that is in it: let all the trees of the wood then reioyce
96.13: Before the Lord: for he cometh, for he cometh to judge the earth: he wil judge the world with righteousnes, and the people in his trueth.

97.1: The Lord reigneth: let the earth reioyce: let the multitude of the yles be glad.
97.2: Cloudes and darkenes are round about him: righteousness and iudgement are the foundation of his throne.
97.3: There shall goe a fire before him, and burn up his enemies round about.
97.4: His lightnings gave light unto the world: the earth saw it and was afraid.
97.5: The mountaines melted like wax at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the Lord of the whole earth.
97.6: The heavens declare his righteousnes, and all the people see his glory.
97.7: Confounded be all they that serve graven images, and that glory in idoles: worship him all ye gods.
97.8: Zion heard of it, and was glad: and the daughters of Judah reioyced, because of thy iudgements, O Lord.
97.9: For thou, Lord, art most High above all the earth: thou art much exalted above all gods.
97.10: Ye that love the Lord, hate evil: he preserveth the soules of his Saints: hee will deliver them from the hand of the wicked.
97.11: Light is sowen for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.
97.12: Reioyce ye righteous in the Lord, and give thankes for his holy remembrance.

98.1: A Psalm. Sing unto the Lord a new song: for hee hath done marueilous things: his right hand, and his holy arm have gotten him the victorie.
98.2: The Lord declared his salvation: his righteousnes hath he reueiled in the sight of ye nations.
98.3: He hath remembred his mercy and his trueth toward the house of Israel: all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
98.4: All the earth, sing ye loud unto the Lord: crie out and reioyce, and sing prayses.
98.5: Sing prayse to the Lord upon the harp, even upon the harp with a singing voyce.
98.6: With shalmes and sound of trumpets sing loud before the Lord the King.
98.7: Let the sea roar, and all that therein is, the world, and they that dwell therein.
98.8: Let the floods clap their hands, and let the mountaines reioyce together
98.9: Before the Lord: for he is come to judge the earth: with righteousness shall hee judge the world, and the people with equitie.

99.1: The Lord reigneth, let the people tremble: he sitteth between the Cherubims, let the earth be moved.
99.2: The Lord is great in Zion, and he is high above all the people.
99.3: They shall prayse thy great and fearefull Name (for it is holy)
99.4: And the Kings power, that loveth iudgement: for thou hast prepared equitie: thou hast executed iudgement and justice in Iaakob.
99.5: Exalt the Lord our God, and fall down before his footestoole: for he is holy.
99.6: Moses and Aaron were among his Priests, and Samuel among such as call upon his Name: these called upon the Lord, and he heard them.
99.7: Hee spake unto them in the cloudie pillar: they kept his testimonies, and the Law that he gave them.
99.8: Thou heardest them, O Lord our God: thou wast a fauourable God unto them, though thou didst take vengeance for their inventions.
99.9: Exalt the Lord our God, and fall down before his holy Mountain: for the Lord our God is holy.

100.1: A Psalm of Praise. Sing ye loud unto the Lord, all the earth.
100.2: Serve the Lord with gladnes: come before him with ioyfulnes.
100.3: Know ye that even the Lord is God: hee hath made us, and not we our selves: we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.
100.4: Enter into his gates with prayse, and into his courts with reioycing: prayse him and bless his Name.
100.5: For the Lord is good: his mercy is everlasting, and his trueth is from generation to generation.

101.1: A Psalm of David. I will sing mercie and iudgement: unto thee, O Lord, will I sing.
101.2: I will doe wisely in the perfite way, till thou comest to me: I will walk in the vprightnes of mine heart in the middes of mine house.
101.3: I wil set no wicked thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that fall away: it shall not cleave unto me.
101.4: A froward heart shall depart from me: I will know none evil.
101.5: Him that privily slandereth his neighbour, wil I destroy: him that hath a proud look and hie heart, I cannot suffer.
101.6: Mine eyes shalbe unto the faithful of the land, that they may dwell with me: he that walketh in a perfite way, he shall serve me.
101.7: There shall no deceitful person dwell within mine house: he that telleth lyes, shall not remain in my sight.
101.8: Betimes will I destroy all the wicked of the land, that I may cut off all the workers of iniquitie from the Citie of the Lord.

102.1: A prayer of the afflicted, when he shall be in distress, and pour forth his meditation before the Lord. O Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come unto thee.
102.2: Hide not thy face from me in the time of my trouble: incline thine eares unto me: when I call, make haste to hear me.
102.3: For my dayes are consumed like smoke, and my bones are burnt like an herthe.
102.4: Mine heart is smitten and withereth like grass, because I forgat to eat my bread.
102.5: For the voyce of my groning my bones doe cleave to my skinne.
102.6: I am like a pelican of the wilderness: I am like an owl of the deserts.
102.7: I watch and am as a sparrow alone upon the house top.
102.8: Mine enemies revile me dayly, and they that rage against me, have sworn against me.
102.9: Surely I have eaten ashes as bread, and mingled my drink with weeping,
102.10: Because of thine indignation and thy wrath: for thou hast heaved me up, and cast me down.
102.11: My dayes are like a shadow that fadeth, and I am withered like grass.
102.12: But thou, O Lord, doest remain for ever, and thy remembrance from generation to generation.
102.13: Thou wilt arise and have mercy upon Zion: for the time to have mercie thereon, for the appointed time is come.
102.14: For thy servants delite in the stones thereof, and have pitie on the dust thereof.
102.15: Then the heathen shall fear the Name of the Lord, and all the Kings of the earth thy glory,
102.16: When the Lord shall build up Zion, and shall appear in his glory,
102.17: And shall turn unto the prayer of the desolate, and not despise their prayer.
102.18: This shall be written for the generation to come: and the people, which shalbe created, shall prayse the Lord.
102.19: For he hath looked down from the height of his Sanctuarie: out of the heaven did the Lord behold the earth,
102.20: That he might hear the mourning of the prisoner, and deliver the children of death:
102.21: That they may declare the Name of the Lord in Zion, and his prayse in Jerusalem,
102.22: When the people shalbe gathered together, and the kingdomes to serve the Lord.
102.23: He abated my strength in the way, and shortened my dayes.
102.24: And I sayd, O my God, take me not away in the middes of my dayes: thy yeeres endure from generation to generation.
102.25: Thou hast aforetime layde the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of thine hands.
102.26: They shall perish, but thou shalt endure: even they all shall wax old as doeth a garment: as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed.
102.27: But thou art the same, and thy yeeres shall not fayle.
102.28: The children of thy servants shall continue, and their seed shall stand fast in thy sight.

103.1: A Psalm of David. My soul, prayse thou the Lord, and all that is within me, prayse his holy Name.
103.2: My soul, prayse thou the Lord, and forget not all his benefites.
103.3: Which forgiveth all thine iniquitie, and healeth all thine infirmities.
103.4: Which redeemeth thy life from the grave, and crowneth thee with mercy and compassions.
103.5: Which satisfieth thy mouth with good things: and thy youth is renued like the eagles.
103.6: The Lord executeth righteousnes and iudgement to all that are oppressed.
103.7: He made his wayes knowen unto Moses, and his workes unto the children of Israel.
103.8: The Lord is full of compassion and mercie, slow to anger and of great kindness.
103.9: He will not alway chide, neither keep his anger for ever.
103.10: He hath not dealt with us after our sinnes, nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.
103.11: For as high as the heaven is above ye earth, so great is his mercie toward them that fear him.
103.12: As far as the East is from the West: so far hath he remooued our sinnes from us.
103.13: As a father hath compassion on his children, so hath the Lord compassion on them that fear him.
103.14: For he knoweth whereof we be made: he remembreth that we are but dust.
103.15: The dayes of man are as grass: as a flowre of the field, so florisheth he.
103.16: For the wind goeth over it, and it is gone, and the place thereof shall know it no more.
103.17: But the loving kindness of the Lord endureth for ever and ever upon them that fear him, and his righteousnes upon childrens children,
103.18: Unto them that keep his covenant, and think upon his commandements to doe them.
103.19: The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven, and his Kingdom ruleth over all.
103.20: Prayse the Lord, ye his Angels, that excel in strength, that doe his commandement in obeying the voyce of his word.
103.21: Prayse the Lord, all ye his hostes, ye his servants that doe his pleasure.
103.22: Prayse the Lord, all ye his workes, in all places of his dominion: my soul, prayse thou the Lord.

104.1: My soul, prayse thou the Lord: O Lord my God, thou art exceeding great, thou art clothed with glorie and honour.
104.2: Which covereth himself with light as with a garment, and spreadeth the heavens like a curtain.
104.3: Which layeth the beames of his chambers in the waters, and maketh the cloudes his chariot, and walketh upon the wings of the wind.
104.4: Which maketh his spirits his messengers, and a flaming fire his ministers.
104.5: He set the earth upon her foundations, so that it shall never move.
104.6: Thou coveredst it with the deep as with a garment: the waters would stand above the mountaines.
104.7: But at thy rebuke they flee: at the voyce of thy thunder they haste away.
104.8: And the mountaines ascend, and the valleis descend to the place which thou hast established for them.
104.9: But thou hast set them a bound, which they shall not pass: they shall not return to cover the earth.
104.10: He sendeth the springs into the valleis, which runne between the mountaines.
104.11: They shall give drink to all the beasts of the field, and the wild asses shall quench their thirst.
104.12: By these springs shall the foules of the heaven dwell, and sing among the branches.
104.13: He watereth the mountaines from his chambers, and the earth is filled with the fruit of thy workes.
104.14: He causeth grass to grow for the cattell, and herb for the use of man, that he may bring forth bread out of the earth,
104.15: And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oyle to make the face to shine, and bread that strengtheneth mans heart.
104.16: The high trees are satisfied, even the cedars of Lebanon, which he hath planted,
104.17: That ye birdes may make their nestes there: the stork dwelleth in the fire trees.
104.18: The high mountaines are for the goates: the rockes are a refuge for the conies.
104.19: He appoynted the moon for certain seasons: the sunne knoweth his going down.
104.20: Thou makest darkenesse, and it is night, wherein all the beastes of the forest creep forth.
104.21: The lions roar after their pray, and seek their meat at God.
104.22: When the sunne riseth, they retire, and couch in their dennes.
104.23: Then goeth man forth to his work, and to his labour until the evening.
104.24: O Lord, how manifold are thy workes! in wisdom hast thou made them all: the earth is full of thy riches.
104.25: So is this sea great and wide: for therein are things creeping innumerable, both small beastes and great.
104.26: There goe the shippes, yea, that Liuiathan, whom thou hast made to play therein.
104.27: All these wait upon thee, that thou maiest give them food in due season.
104.28: Thou givest it to them, and they gather it: thou openest thine hand, and they are filled with good things.
104.29: But if thou hide thy face, they are troubled: if thou take away their breath, they dye and return to their dust.
104.30: Again if thou send forth thy spirit, they are created, and thou renuest the face of the earth.
104.31: Glory be to the Lord for ever: let the Lord reioyce in his workes.
104.32: He looketh on the earth and it trembleth: he toucheth the mountaines, and they smoke.
104.33: I will sing unto the Lord all my life: I will prayse my God, while I live.
104.34: Let my wordes be acceptable unto him: I will reioyce in the Lord.
104.35: Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth, and the wicked till there be no more: O my soul, prayse thou the Lord. Prayse ye the Lord.

105.1: Praise the Lord, and call upon his Name: declare his workes among the people.
105.2: Sing unto him, sing prayse unto him, and talk of all his wonderous workes.
105.3: Reioyce in his holy Name: let the heart of them that seek the Lord, reioyce.
105.4: Seek the Lord and his strength: seek his face continually.
105.5: Remember his marueilous woorkes, that he hath done, his wonders and the iudgements of his mouth,
105.6: Ye seed of Abraham his servant, ye children of Iaakob, which are his elect.
105.7: He is the Lord our God: his iudgements are through all the earth.
105.8: He hath alway remembred his covenant and promise, that he made to a thousand generations,
105.9: Even that which he made with Abraham, and his othe unto Izhak:
105.10: And since hath confirmed it to Iaakob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant,
105.11: Saying, Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance.
105.12: Albeit they were few in nomber, yea, very few, and strangers in the land,
105.13: And walked about from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people,
105.14: Yet suffered he no man to doe them wrong, but reprooued Kings for their sakes, saying,
105.15: Touch not mine anointed, and doe my Prophets no harm.
105.16: Moreover, he called a famine upon ye land, and utterly brake the staff of bread.
105.17: But he sent a man before them: Joseph was sold for a slave.
105.18: They held his feet in the stockes, and he was laid in yrons,
105.19: Until his appointed time came, and the counsel of the Lord had tryed him.
105.20: The King sent and loosed him: even the Ruler of the people delivered him.
105.21: He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance,
105.22: That he should bind his princes unto his will, and teach his Ancients wisedome.
105.23: Then Israel came to Egypt, and Iaakob was a stranger in the land of Ham.
105.24: And he increased his people exceedingly, and made them stronger then their oppressours.
105.25: He turned their heart to hate his people, and to deal craftily with his servants.
105.26: Then sent he Moses his servant, and Aaron whom he had chosen.
105.27: They shewed among them the message of his signes, and wonders in the land of Ham.
105.28: He sent darkenesse, and made it dark: and they were not disobedient unto his commission.
105.29: He turned their waters into blood, and slew their fish.
105.30: Their land brought foorth frogs, even in their Kings chambers.
105.31: He spake, and there came swarmes of flies and lice in all their quarters.
105.32: He gave them hail for rain, and flames of fire in their land.
105.33: He smote their vines also and their figge trees, and brake down the trees in their coastes.
105.34: He spake, and the grashoppers came, and caterpillers innumerable,
105.35: And did eat up all the grass in their land, and deuoured the fruit of their ground.
105.36: He smote also all the first borne in their land, even the beginning of all their strength.
105.37: He brought them forth also with silver and gold, and there was none feeble among their tribes.
105.38: Egypt was glad at their departing: for the fear of them had fallen upon them.
105.39: He spred a cloud to be a covering, and fire to give light in the night.
105.40: They asked, and he brought quailes, and he filled them with the bread of heaven.
105.41: He opened the rock, and the waters flowed out, and ranne in the dry places like a river.
105.42: For he remembred his holy promise to Abraham his servant,
105.43: And he brought forth his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness,
105.44: And gave them the lands of the heathen, and they took the labours of the people in possession,
105.45: That they might keep his statutes, and observe his Lawes. Prayse ye the Lord.

106.1: Praise ye the Lord. Praise ye the Lord because he is good, for his mercie endureth for ever.
106.2: Who can express the noble actes of the Lord, or shew forth all his prayse?
106.3: Blessed are they that keep iudgement, and doe righteousness at all times.
106.4: Remember me, O Lord, with the fauour of thy people: visit me with thy salvation,
106.5: That I may see the felicitie of thy chosen, and reioyce in the joy of thy people, and glorie with thine inheritance.
106.6: We have sinned with our fathers: we have committed iniquitie, and done wickedly.
106.7: Our fathers vnderstoode not thy wonders in Egypt, neither remembred they the multitude of thy mercies, but rebelled at the Sea, even at the red sea.
106.8: Nevertheless he saved them for his Names sake, that he might make his power to be knowen.
106.9: And he rebuked the red Sea, and it was dryed up, and he led them in the deep, as in the wilderness.
106.10: And he saved them from ye adversaries hand, and delivered them from ye hand of the enemie.
106.11: And the waters covered their oppressours: not one of them was left.
106.12: Then beleeued they his wordes, and sang prayse unto him.
106.13: But incontinently they forgat his workes: they wayted not for his counsel,
106.14: But lusted with concupiscence in the wildernes, and tempted God in the desert.
106.15: Then he gave them their desire: but he sent leanness into their soul.
106.16: They envied Moses also in the tentes, and Aaron the holy one of the Lord.
106.17: Therefore the earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the companie of Abiram.
106.18: And the fire was kindled in their assembly: the flame burnt up the wicked.
106.19: They made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped the molten image.
106.20: Thus they turned their glory into the similitude of a bullock, that eateth grass.
106.21: They forgat God their Sauiour, which had done great things in Egypt,
106.22: Wonderous woorkes in the land of Ham, and fearefull things by the red Sea.
106.23: Therefore he minded to destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stand in the breach before him to turn away his wrath, least he should destroy them.
106.24: Also they contemned that pleasant land, and beleeued not his word,
106.25: But murmured in their tentes, and hearkened not unto the voice of the Lord.
106.26: Therefore hee lifted up his hand against them, to destroy them in the wilderness,
106.27: And to destroy their seed among the nations, and to scatter them throughout the countries.
106.28: They ioyned themselves also unto Baalpeor, and did eat the offrings of the dead.
106.29: Thus they provoked him unto anger with their own inventions, and the plague brake in upon them.
106.30: But Phinehas stood up, and executed iudgement, and the plague was staied.
106.31: And it was imputed unto him for righteousnes from generation to generation for ever.
106.32: They angred him also at the waters of Meribah, so that Moses was punished for their sakes,
106.33: Because they vexed his spirit, so that hee spake vnaduisedly with his lippes.
106.34: Neither destroied they the people, as the Lord had commanded them,
106.35: But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their workes,
106.36: And served their idoles, which were their ruin.
106.37: Yea, they offered their sonnes, and their daughters unto devils,
106.38: And shed innocent blood, even the blood of their sonnes, and of their daughters, whom they offred unto the idoles of Canaan, and the land was defiled with blood.
106.39: Thus were they steined with their own woorkes, and went a whoring with their own inventions.
106.40: Therefore was the wrath of the Lord kindled against his people, and he abhorred his own inheritance.
106.41: And hee gave them into the hand of the heathen: and they that hated them, were lordes over them.
106.42: Their enemies also oppressed them, and they were humbled under their hand.
106.43: Many a time did hee deliver them, but they provoked him by their counsels: therefore they were brought down by their iniquitie.
106.44: Yet hee saw when they were in affliction, and he heard their crie.
106.45: And he remembred his covenant toward them and repented according to the multitude of his mercies,
106.46: And gave them fauour in the sight of all them that lead them captives.
106.47: Save us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the heathen, that we may praise thine holy Name, and glorie in thy praise.
106.48: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel for ever and ever, and let all the people say, So be it. Praise yee the Lord.

107.1: Praise the Lord, because he is good: for his mercie endureth for ever.
107.2: Let them, which have been redeemed of the Lord, shew how he hath delivered them from the hand of the oppressour,
107.3: And gathered them out of the lands, from the East and from the West, from the North and from the South.
107.4: When they wandered in the desert and wilderness out of the waie, and found no citie to dwell in,
107.5: Both hungrie and thirstie, their soul fainted in them.
107.6: Then they cried unto the Lord in their trouble, and he delivered them from their distress,
107.7: And led them forth by the right way, that they might goe to a citie of habitation.
107.8: Let them therefore confess before ye Lord his loving kindness, and his wonderful woorkes before the sonnes of men.
107.9: For he satisfied the thirstie soul, and filled the hungrie soul with goodness.
107.10: They that dwell in darkenesse and in the shadow of death, being bound in miserie and yron,
107.11: Because they rebelled against the wordes of the Lord, and despised the counsel of the most High,
107.12: When he humbled their heart with heauines, then they fell down and there was no helper.
107.13: Then they cried unto the Lord in their trouble, and he delivered them from their distress.
107.14: He brought them out of darkenes, and out of the shadow of death, and brake their bandes asunder.
107.15: Let them therefore cofesse before the Lord his loving kindness, and his wonderful woorkes before the sonnes of men.
107.16: For hee hath broken the gates of brass, and brast the barres of yron asunder.
107.17: Fooles by reason of their transgression, and because of their iniquities are afflicted.
107.18: Their soul abhorreth al meat, and they are brought to deaths door.
107.19: Then they crie unto the Lord in their trouble, and he delivereth them from their distress.
107.20: He sendeth his word and healeth them, and delivereth them from their graves.
107.21: Let them therefore cofesse before the Lord his loving kindness, and his wonderful workes before the sonnes of men,
107.22: And let them offer sacrifices of praise, and declare his workes with reioycing.
107.23: They that goe down to the sea in ships, and occupie by the great waters,
107.24: They see the woorkes of the Lord, and his wonders in the deep.
107.25: For he commaundeth and raiseth the stormie wind, and it lifteth up the waves thereof.
107.26: They mount up to the heaven, and descend to ye deep, so that their soul melteth for trouble.
107.27: They are tossed to and from, and stagger like a drunken man, and all their cunning is gone.
107.28: Then they crie unto the Lord in their trouble, and he bringeth them out of their distress.
107.29: He turneth the storm to calm, so that the waves thereof are still.
107.30: When they are quieted, they are glad, and hee bringeth them unto the haven, where they would be.
107.31: Let them therfore confess before the Lord his loving kindness, and his wonderful woorkes before the sonnes of men.
107.32: And let them exalt him in the Congregation of the people, and praise him in the assembly of the Elders.
107.33: He turneth the floodes into a wilderness, and the springs of waters into drinesse,
107.34: And a fruitful land into barrennes for the wickednes of them that dwell therein.
107.35: Again hee turneth the wilderness into pooles of water, and the drie land into water springs.
107.36: And there he placeth the hungrie, and they build a citie to dwell in,
107.37: And sow the fieldes, and plant vineyardes, which bring foorth fruitful increase.
107.38: For he blesseth them, and they multiplie exceedingly, and he diminisheth not their cattell.
107.39: Again men are diminished, and brought low by oppression, evil and sorowe.
107.40: He powreth contempt upon princes, and causeth them to ere in desert places out of the way.
107.41: Yet he raiseth up the poor out of miserie, and maketh him families like a flock of sheep.
107.42: The righteous shall see it, and reioyce, and all iniquitie shall stoppe her mouth.
107.43: Who is wise that hee may observe these things? for they shall understand the loving kindness of the Lord.

108.1: A song or Psalm of David. O God, mine heart is prepared, so is my tongue: I will sing and give praise.
108.2: Awake viol and harp: I will awake early.
108.3: I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people, and I wil sing unto thee among the nations.
108.4: For thy mercy is great above the heavens, and thy trueth unto the clouds.
108.5: Exalt thy self, O God, above the heavens, and let thy glorie be upon all the earth,
108.6: That thy beloved may be delivered: help with thy right hand and hear me.
108.7: God hath spoken in his holiness: therefore I will reioyce, I shall deuide Shechem and measure the valley of Succoth.
108.8: Gilead shalbe mine, and Manasseh shalbe mine: Ephraim also shalbe the strength of mine head: Juda is my lawgiver.
108.9: Moab shalbe my washpot: over Edom wil I cast out my shoe: upon Palestina wil I triumph.
108.10: Who will lead mee into the strong citie? who will bring me unto Edom?
108.11: Wilt not thou, O God, which haddest forsaken us, and diddest not goe foorth, O God, with our armies?
108.12: Give us help against trouble: for vain is the help of man.
108.13: Through God we shall doe valiantly: for he shall tread down our enemies.

109.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. Hold not thy tongue, O God of my praise.
109.2: For the mouth of the wicked, and the mouth full of deceit are opened upon me: they have spoken to me with a lying tongue.
109.3: They compassed me about also with words of hatred, and fought against me without a cause.
109.4: For my friendship they were mine adversaries, but I gave my self to praier.
109.5: And they have rewarded me evil for good, and hatred for my friendship.
109.6: Set thou the wicked over him, and let the aduersarie stand at his right hand.
109.7: Whe he shalbe judged, let him be condemned, and let his praier be turned into sinne.
109.8: Let his daies be few, and let another take his charge.
109.9: Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.
109.10: Let his children be vagabonds and beg and seek bread, coming out of their places destroyed.
109.11: Let the extortioner catch al that he hath, and let the strangers spoil his labour.
109.12: Let there be none to extend mercie unto him: neither let there be any to shew mercie upon his fatherless children.
109.13: Let his posteritie be destroied, and in the generation following let their name be put out.
109.14: Let the iniquitie of his fathers bee had in remembrance with the Lord: and let not the sinne of his mother be done away.
109.15: But let them alway be before the Lord, that he may cut off their memorial from ye earth.
109.16: Because he remembred not to shew mercie, but persecuted the afflicted and poor man, and the sorowfull hearted to slay him.
109.17: As he loved cursing, so shall it come unto him, and as he loved not blessing, so shall it be far from him.
109.18: As he clothed himself with cursing like a rayment, so shall it come into his bowels like water, and like oyle into his bones.
109.19: Let it be unto him as a garment to cover him, and for a girdle, wherewith he shalbe alway girded.
109.20: Let this be the reward of mine aduersarie from the Lord, and of them, that speak evil against my soul.
109.21: But thou, O Lord my God, deal with me according unto thy Name: deliver me, (for thy mercie is good)
109.22: Because I am poor and needie, and mine heart is wounded within me.
109.23: I depart like the shadow that declineth, and am shaken off as the grashopper.
109.24: My knees are weak through fasting, and my flesh hath lost all fatnes.
109.25: I became also a rebuke unto them: they that looked upon me, shaked their heads.
109.26: Help me, O Lord my God: save me according to thy mercie.
109.27: And they shall know, that this is thine hand, and that thou, Lord, hast done it.
109.28: Though they curse, yet thou wilt bless: they shall arise and be confounded, but thy servant shall reioyce.
109.29: Let mine adversaries be clothed with shame, and let them cover themselves with their confusion, as with a cloke.
109.30: I will give thankes unto the Lord greatly with my mouth and praise him among ye multitude.
109.31: For he will stand at the right hand of the poor, to save him from them that would condemn his soul.

110.1: A Psalm of David. The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footestoole.
110.2: The Lord shall send the rod of thy power out of Zion: be thou ruler in the middes of thine enemies.
110.3: Thy people shall come willingly at the time of assembling thine armie in holy beautie: the youth of thy womb shalbe as the morning dew.
110.4: The Lord sware and wil not repent, Thou art a Priest for ever after ye order of Melchi-zedek.
110.5: The Lord, that is at thy right hand, shall wound Kings in the day of his wrath.
110.6: He shalbe judge among the heathen: he shall fill all with dead bodies, and smite the head over great countreis.
110.7: He shall drink of the brook in the way: therefore shall he lift up his head.

111.1: Praise ye the Lord. I will prayse the Lord with my whole heart in the assemblie and Congregation of the just.
111.2: The workes of the Lord are great, and ought to be sought out of al them that love them.
111.3: His work is beautiful and glorious, and his righteousness endureth for ever.
111.4: He hath made his wonderful workes to be had in remembrance: the Lord is merciful and full of compassion.
111.5: He hath given a portion unto them that fear him: he wil ever be mindful of his covenant.
111.6: He hath shewed to his people the power of his workes in giving unto them the heritage of the heathen.
111.7: The workes of his handes are trueth and iudgement: all his statutes are true.
111.8: They are stablished for ever and ever, and are done in trueth and equitie.
111.9: He sent redemption unto his people: he hath commanded his covenant for ever: holy and fearefull is his Name.
111.10: The beginning of wisedome is the fear of the Lord: all they that observe them, have good understanding: his praise endureth for ever.

112.1: Praise ye the Lord. Blessed is the man, that feareth the Lord, and deliteth greatly in his commandements.
112.2: His seed shall be mightie upon earth: the generation of the righteous shall be blessed.
112.3: Riches and treasures shalbe in his house, and his righteousness endureth for ever.
112.4: Unto the righteous ariseth light in darkenes: he is merciful and full of copassion and righteous.
112.5: A good man is merciful and lendeth, and will measure his affaires by iudgement.
112.6: Surely he shall never be moved: but the righteous shalbe had in everlasting remembrance.
112.7: He will not be afraid of evil tidings: for his heart is fixed, and beleeueth in the Lord.
112.8: His heart is stablished: therefore he will not fear, until he see his desire upon his enemies.
112.9: He hath distributed and given to ye poor: his righteousness remaineth for ever: his horn shalbe exalted with glory.
112.10: The wicked shall see it and be angrie: he shall gnash with his teeth, and consume away: the desire of the wicked shall perish.

113.1: Praise ye the Lord. Praise, O ye servants of the Lord, prayse the Name of the Lord.
113.2: Blessed be the Name of the Lord from hencefoorth and for ever.
113.3: The Lordes Name is praysed from the rising of ye sunne, unto ye going down of the same.
113.4: The Lord is high above all nations, and his glorie above the heavens.
113.5: Who is like unto the Lord our God, that hath his dwelling on high!
113.6: Who abaseth himself to behold things in the heaven and in the earth!
113.7: He raiseth the needie out of the dust, and lifteth up the poor out of the dung,
113.8: That he may set him with the princes, even with the princes of his people.
113.9: He maketh the barren woman to dwell with a familie, and a ioyfull mother of children. Prayse ye the Lord.

114.1: When Israel went out of Egypt, and the house of Iaakob from the barbarous people,
114.2: Judah was his sanctification, and Israel his dominion.
114.3: The Sea saw it and fled: Iorden was turned back.
114.4: The mountaines leaped like rams, and the hils as lambes.
114.5: What ailed thee, O Sea, that thou fleddest? O Iorden, why wast thou turned back?
114.6: Ye mountaines, why leaped ye like rams, and ye hils as lambes?
114.7: The earth trembled at the presence of the Lord, at the presence of the God of Iaakob,
114.8: Which turneth the rock into waterpooles, and the flint into a fountain of water.

115.1: Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto thy Name give the glorie, for thy loving mercie and for thy truethes sake.
115.2: Wherefore shall the heathen say, Where is now their God?
115.3: But our God is in heaven: he doeth what so ever he will.
115.4: Their idoles are silver and gold, even the work of mens hands.
115.5: They have a mouth and speak not: they have eyes and see not.
115.6: They have eares and hear not: they have noses and smell not.
115.7: They have handes and touch not: they have feet and walk not: neither make they a sound with their throte.
115.8: They that make them are like unto them: so are all that trust in them.
115.9: O Israel, trust thou in the Lord: for he is their help and their shield.
115.10: O house of Aaron, trust ye in the Lord: for he is their help and their shield.
115.11: Ye that fear the Lord, trust in the Lord: for he is their helper and their shield.
115.12: The Lord hath been mindful of us: he will bless, he will bless the house of Israel, he will bless the house of Aaron.
115.13: He will bless them that fear the Lord, both small and great.
115.14: The Lord will increase his graces toward you, even toward you and toward your children.
115.15: Ye are blessed of the Lord, which made the heaven and the earth.
115.16: The heavens, even the heavens are the Lordes: but he hath given the earth to the sonnes of men.
115.17: The dead prayse not the Lord, neither any that goe down into the place of silence.
115.18: But we will prayse the Lord from henceforth and for ever. Prayse ye the Lord.

116.1: I love the Lord, because he hath heard my voyce and my prayers.
116.2: For he hath inclined his ear unto me, whe I did call upon him in my dayes.
116.3: When the snares of death copassed me, and the griefes of the grave caught me: when I found trouble and sorowe.
116.4: Then I called upon the Name of the Lord, saying, I beseech thee, O Lord, deliver my soul.
116.5: The Lord is merciful and righteous, and our God is full of compassion.
116.6: The Lord preserveth the simple: I was in miserie and he saved me.
116.7: Return unto thy rest, O my soul: for the Lord hath been beneficiall unto thee,
116.8: Because thou hast delivered my soul from death, mine eyes from teares, and my feet from falling.
116.9: I shall walk before the Lord in the land of the living.
116.10: I beleeued, therefore did I speak: for I was sore troubled.
116.11: I said in my fear, All men are lyers.
116.12: What shall I render unto the Lord for all his benefites toward me?
116.13: I will take the cup of salvation, and call upon the Name of the Lord.
116.14: I will pay my vowes unto the Lord, even now in the presence of all his people.
116.15: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his Saintes.
116.16: Behold, Lord: for I am thy servant, I am thy servant, and the sonne of thine handmaid: thou hast broken my bondes.
116.17: I will offer to thee a sacrifice of prayse, and will call upon the Name of the Lord.
116.18: I will pay my vowes unto the Lord, even now in the presence of all his people,
116.19: In the courtes of ye Lords house, even in the middes of thee, O Jerusalem. Praise ye the Lord.

117.1: All nations, praise ye the Lord: all ye people, praise him.
117.2: For his loving kindnes is great toward us, and the trueth of the Lord endureth for ever. Praise yee the Lord.

118.1: Praise yee the Lord, because he is good: for his mercie endureth for ever.
118.2: Let Israel now say, That his mercy endureth for ever.
118.3: Let the house of Aaron now say, That his mercy endureth for ever.
118.4: Let them, that fear the Lord, now say, That his mercie endureth for ever.
118.5: I called upon the Lord in trouble, and the Lord heard me, and set me at large.
118.6: The Lord is with mee: therefore I will not fear what man can doe unto me.
118.7: The Lord is with mee among them that help me: therefore shall I see my desire upon mine enemies.
118.8: It is better to trust in the Lord, then to have confidence in man.
118.9: It is better to trust in the Lord, then to have confidence in princes.
118.10: All nations have compassed me: but in the Name of the Lord shall I destroy them.
118.11: They have compassed mee, yea, they have compassed mee: but in the Name of the Lord I shall destroy them.
118.12: They came about mee like bees, but they were quenched as a fire of thornes: for in the Name of the Lord I shall destroy them.
118.13: Thou hast thrust sore at me, that I might fall: but the Lord hath holpen me.
118.14: The Lord is my strength and song: for he hath been my deliverance.
118.15: The voice of joy and deliverance shall be in the tabernacles of the righteous, saying, The right hand of the Lord hath done valiantly.
118.16: The right hand of the Lord is exalted: the right hand of the Lord hath done valiantly.
118.17: I shall not die, but live, and declare the woorkes of the Lord.
118.18: The Lord hath chastened me sore, but he hath not delivered me to death.
118.19: Open ye unto me the gates of righteousnes, that I may goe into them, and praise the Lord.
118.20: This is the gate of the Lord: the righteous shall enter into it.
118.21: I will praise thee: for thou hast heard mee, and hast been my deliverance.
118.22: The stone, which the builders refused, is the head of the corner.
118.23: This was the Lordes doing, and it is marueilous in our eyes.
118.24: This is the day, which the Lord hath made: let us reioyce and be glad in it.
118.25: O Lord, I praie thee, save now: O Lord, I praie thee now give prosperitie.
118.26: Blessed be he, that cometh in the Name of the Lord: wee have blessed you out of the house of the Lord.
118.27: The Lord is mightie, and hath given us light: bind the sacrifice with cordes unto the hornes of the altar.
118.28: Thou art my God, and I will praise thee, even my God: therefore I will exalt thee.
118.29: Praise ye the Lord, because he is good: for his mercie endureth for ever.

119.1: ALEPH. Blessed are those that are upright in their way, and walk in the Law of the Lord.
119.2: Blessed are they that keep his testimonies, and seek him with their whole heart.
119.3: Surely they woorke none iniquitie, but walk in his waies.
119.4: Thou hast commanded to keep thy precepts diligently.
119.5: Oh that my waies were directed to keep thy statutes!
119.6: Then should I not be confounded, when I have respect unto all thy commandements.
119.7: I will praise thee with an upright heart, when I shall learn the iudgements of thy righteousness.
119.8: I will keep thy statutes: forsake mee not ouerlong.
119.9: BETH. Wherewith shall a yong man redresse his waie? in taking heed thereto according to thy woorde.
119.10: With my whole heart have I sought thee: let me not wander from thy commandements.
119.11: I have hid thy promise in mine heart, that I might not sinne against thee.
119.12: Blessed art thou, O Lord: teach mee thy statutes.
119.13: With my lippes have I declared all the iudgements of thy mouth.
119.14: I have had as great delight in the way of thy testimonies, as in all riches.
119.15: I will meditate in thy precepts, and consider thy waies.
119.16: I will delite in thy statutes, and I will not forget thy word.
119.17: GIMEL. Be beneficiall unto thy servant, that I may live and keep thy woorde.
119.18: Open mine eies, that I may see the wonders of thy Law.
119.19: I am a stranger upon earth: hide not thy commandements from me.
119.20: Mine heart breaketh for the desire to thy iudgements alway.
119.21: Thou hast destroied the proud: cursed are they that doe ere from thy commandements.
119.22: Remove from mee shame and contempt: for I have kept thy testimonies.
119.23: Princes also did sit, and speak against me: but thy servant did meditate in thy statutes.
119.24: Also thy testimonies are my delite, and my counsellers.
119.25: DALETH. My soul cleaveth to the dust: quicken me according to thy word.
119.26: I have declared my waies, and thou heardest me: teach me thy statutes.
119.27: Make me to understand ye way of thy precepts, and I will meditate in thy wondrous workes.
119.28: My soul melteth for heaviness: raise mee up according unto thy word.
119.29: Take from mee the way of lying, and graunt me graciously thy Law.
119.30: I have chosen the way of trueth, and thy iudgements have I laied before me.
119.31: I have cleaved to thy testimonies, O Lord: confound me not.
119.32: I will runne the way of thy commandements, when thou shalt enlarge mine heart.
119.33: HE. Teach mee, O Lord, the way of thy statutes, and I will keep it unto the end.
119.34: Give mee understanding, and I will keep thy Law: yea, I wil keep it with my whole heart.
119.35: Direct mee in the path of thy commandements: for therein is my delite.
119.36: Incline mine heart unto thy testimonies, and not to couetousnesse.
119.37: Turn away mine eies from regarding vanitie, and quicken me in thy way.
119.38: Stablish thy promise to thy seruaunt, because he feareth thee.
119.39: Take away my rebuke that I fear: for thy iudgements are good.
119.40: Behold, I desire thy commandements: quicken me in thy righteousness,
119.41: VAV. And let thy loving kindness come unto me, O Lord, and thy salvation according to thy promise.
119.42: So shall I make answer unto my blasphemers: for I trust in thy woorde.
119.43: And take not the woorde of trueth utterly out of my mouth: for I wait for thy iudgements.
119.44: So shall I alway keep thy Law for ever and ever.
119.45: And I will walk at libertie: for I seek thy precepts.
119.46: I will speak also of thy testimonies before Kings, and will not be ashamed.
119.47: And my delite shalbe in thy commandements, which I have loved.
119.48: Mine handes also will I lift up unto thy commandements, which I have loved, and I will meditate in thy statutes.
119.49: ZAIN. Remember the promise made to thy servant, wherein thou hast caused me to trust.
119.50: It is my comfort in my trouble: for thy promise hath quickened me.
119.51: The proud have had me exceedingly in derision: yet have I not declined from thy Law.
119.52: I remembred thy iudgements of old, O Lord, and have been comforted.
119.53: Fear is come upon mee for the wicked, that forsake thy Law.
119.54: Thy statutes have been my songes in the house of my pilgrimage.
119.55: I have remembred thy Name, O Lord, in the night, and have kept thy Law.
119.56: This I had because I kept thy precepts.
119.57: CHETH. O Lord, that art my portion, I have determined to keep thy wordes.
119.58: I made my supplication in thy presence with my whole heart: be merciful unto me according to thy promise.
119.59: I have considered my waies, and turned my feet into thy testimonies.
119.60: I made haste and delaied not to keep thy commandements.
119.61: The bandes of the wicked have robbed me: but I have not forgotten thy Law.
119.62: At midnight will I rise to give thanks unto thee, because of thy righteous iudgements.
119.63: I am companion of all them that fear thee, and keep thy precepts.
119.64: The earth, O Lord, is full of thy mercie: teach me thy statutes.
119.65: TETH. O Lord, thou hast delt graciously with thy servant according unto thy woorde.
119.66: Teach me good iudgement and knowledge: for I have beleeued thy commandements.
119.67: Before I was afflicted, I went astray: but now I keep thy woorde.
119.68: Thou art good and gracious: teach me thy statutes.
119.69: The proud have imagined a lie against me: but I wil keep thy precepts with my whole heart.
119.70: Their heart is fatte as grease: but my delite is in thy Law.
119.71: It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I may learn thy statutes.
119.72: The Law of thy mouth is better unto me, then thousands of gold and silver.
119.73: Jod. Thine hands have made me and fashioned me: give mee understanding therefore, that I may learn thy commandements.
119.74: So they that fear thee, seeing mee shall reioyce, because I have trusted in thy word.
119.75: I know, O Lord, that thy iudgements are right, and that thou hast afflicted me justly.
119.76: I pray thee that thy mercie may comfort me according to thy promise unto thy servant.
119.77: Let thy tender mercies come unto me, that I may live: for thy Law is my delite.
119.78: Let the proud be ashamed: for they have dealt wickedly and falsely with me: but I meditate in thy precepts.
119.79: Let such as fear thee turn unto me, and they that know thy testimonies.
119.80: Let mine heart bee upright in thy statutes, that I be not ashamed.
119.81: CAPH. My soul fainteth for thy salvation: yet I wait for thy word.
119.82: Mine eyes fail for thy promise, saying, when wilt thou comfort me?
119.83: For I am like a bottell in the smoke: yet doe I not forget thy statutes.
119.84: How many are the dayes of thy servant? When wilt thou execute iudgement on them that persecute me?
119.85: The proud have digged pittes for mee, which is not after thy Law.
119.86: All thy commandements are true: they persecute me falsely: help me.
119.87: They had almost consumed me upon the earth: but I forsook not thy precepts.
119.88: Quicken me according to thy loving kindnes: so shall I keep the testimony of thy mouth.
119.89: LAMED. O Lord, thy word endureth for ever in heaven.
119.90: Thy trueth is from generation to generation: thou hast layed the foundation of the earth, and it abideth.
119.91: They continue even to this day by thine ordinances: for all are thy servants.
119.92: Except thy Law had been my delite, I should now have perished in mine affliction.
119.93: I wil never forget thy precepts: for by them thou hast quickened me.
119.94: I am thine, save me: for I have sought thy precepts.
119.95: The wicked have waited for me to destroy me: but I will consider thy testimonies.
119.96: I have seen an end of all perfection: but thy commandement is exceeding large.
119.97: MEM. Oh how love I thy Law! it is my meditation continually.
119.98: By thy commandements thou hast made mee wiser then mine enemies: for they are ever with mee.
119.99: I have had more vnderstading then all my teachers: for thy testimonies are my meditation.
119.100: I vnderstoode more then the ancient, because I kept thy precepts.
119.101: I have refrained my feet from every evil way, that I might keep thy word.
119.102: I have not declined from thy iudgements: for thou didest teach me.
119.103: How sweet are thy promises unto my mouth! yea, more then hony unto my mouth.
119.104: By thy precepts I have gotten understanding: therefore I hate all the wayes of falshoode.
119.105: NUN. Thy word is a lanterne unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
119.106: I have sworn and will perform it, that I will keep thy righteous iudgements.
119.107: I am very sore afflicted: O Lord, quicken me according to thy word.
119.108: O Lord, I beseech thee accept the free offerings of my mouth, and teach mee thy iudgements.
119.109: My soul is continually in mine hand: yet doe I not forget thy Law.
119.110: The wicked have layed a snare for mee: but I swarued not from thy precepts.
119.111: Thy testimonies have I taken as an heritage for ever: for they are the joy of mine heart.
119.112: I have applied mine heart to fulfil thy statutes alway, even unto the end.
119.113: SAMECH. I hate vain inventions: but thy Law doe I love.
119.114: Thou art my refuge and shield, and I trust in thy word.
119.115: Away from mee, yee wicked: for I will keep the commandements of my God.
119.116: Stablish me according to thy promise, that I may live, and disappoint me not of mine hope.
119.117: Stay thou mee, and I shall be safe, and I will delite continually in thy statutes.
119.118: Thou hast troden down all them that depart from thy statutes: for their deceit is vain.
119.119: Thou hast taken away all ye wicked of the earth like dross: therefore I love thy testimonies.
119.120: My flesh trembleth for fear of thee, and I am afraid of thy iudgements.
119.121: AIN. I have executed iudgement and justice: leave me not to mine oppressours.
119.122: Answer for thy servant in that, which is good, and let not the proud oppress me.
119.123: Mine eyes have failed in waiting for thy salvation, and for thy just promise.
119.124: Deal with thy servant according to thy mercie, and teach me thy statutes.
119.125: I am thy servant: graunt mee therefore understanding, that I may know thy testimonies.
119.126: It is time for thee Lord to work: for they have destroyed thy Law.
119.127: Therefore love I thy commandements above gold, yea, above most fine gold.
119.128: Therefore I esteem all thy precepts most just, and hate all false wayes.
119.129: PE. Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore doeth my soul keep them.
119.130: The entrance into thy wordes sheweth light, and giveth understanding to the simple.
119.131: I opened my mouth and panted, because I loved thy commandements.
119.132: Look upon mee and bee merciful unto me, as thou usest to doe unto those that love thy Name.
119.133: Direct my steppes in thy word, and let none iniquitie have dominion over me.
119.134: Deliver mee from the oppression of men, and I will keep thy precepts.
119.135: Shew the light of thy countenance upon thy servant, and teach me thy statutes.
119.136: Mine eyes gush out with rivers of water, because they keep not thy Law.
119.137: TSADDI. Righteous art thou, O Lord, and just are thy iudgements.
119.138: Thou hast commanded justice by thy testimonies and trueth especially.
119.139: My zeal hath even consumed mee, because mine enemies have forgotten thy wordes.
119.140: Thy word is prooued most pure, and thy servant loveth it.
119.141: I am small and despised: yet do I not forget thy precepts.
119.142: Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousnes, and thy Law is trueth.
119.143: Trouble and anguish are come upon me: yet are thy commandements my delite.
119.144: The righteousnes of thy testimonies is everlasting: graunt me understanding, and I shall live.
119.145: KOPH. I have cried with my whole heart: hear me, O Lord, and I will keep thy statutes.
119.146: I called upon thee: save mee, and I will keep thy testimonies.
119.147: I prevented the morning light, and cried: for I waited on thy word.
119.148: Mine eyes prevent the night watches to meditate in thy word.
119.149: Hear my voyce according to thy loving kindenesse: O Lord, quicken me according to thy iudgement.
119.150: They draw neere, that follow after malice, and are far from thy Law.
119.151: Thou art neere, O Lord: for all thy commandements are true.
119.152: I have knowen long since by thy testimonies, that thou hast established them for ever.
119.153: RESH. Behold mine affliction, and deliver mee: for I have not forgotten thy Law.
119.154: Plead my cause, and deliver me: quicken me according unto thy word.
119.155: Salvation is far from the wicked, because they seek not thy statutes.
119.156: Great are thy tender mercies, O Lord: quicken me according to thy iudgements.
119.157: My persecutours and mine oppressours are many: yet doe I not swarue from thy testimonies.
119.158: I saw the transgressours and was grieved, because they kept not thy word.
119.159: Consider, O Lord, how I love thy preceptes: quicken mee according to thy loving kindenesse.
119.160: The beginning of thy word is trueth, and all the iudgements of thy righteousness endure for ever.
119.161: SCHIN. Princes have persecuted mee without cause, but mine heart stood in awe of thy wordes.
119.162: I reioyce at thy word, as one that findeth a great spoyle.
119.163: I hate falshoode and abhorre it, but thy Law doe I love.
119.164: Seven times a day doe I praise thee, because of thy righteous iudgements.
119.165: They that love thy Law, shall have great prosperitie, and they shall have none hurt.
119.166: Lord, I have trusted in thy salvation, and have done thy commandements.
119.167: My soul hath kept thy testimonies: for I love them exceedingly.
119.168: I have kept thy precepts and thy testimonies: for all my wayes are before thee.
119.169: Tau. Let my complaint come before thee, O Lord, and give me understanding, according unto thy word.
119.170: Let my supplication come before thee, and deliver me according to thy promise.
119.171: My lippes shall speak praise, when thou hast taught me thy statutes.
119.172: My tongue shall intreat of thy word: for all thy commandements are righteous.
119.173: Let thine hand help me: for I have chosen thy precepts.
119.174: I have longed for thy salvation, O Lord, and thy Law is my delite.
119.175: Let my soul live, and it shall praise thee, and thy iudgements shall help me.
119.176: I have gone astray like a lost sheep: seek thy servant, for I doe not forget thy commandements.

120.1: A song of degrees. I called unto the Lord in my trouble, and hee heard me.
120.2: Deliver my soul, O Lord, from lying lippes, and from a deceitful tongue.
120.3: What doeth thy deceitful tongue bring unto thee? or what doeth it auaile thee?
120.4: It is as the sharp arrowes of a mightie man, and as the coales of juniper.
120.5: Woe is to me that I remain in Meschech, and dwell in the tentes of Kedar.
120.6: My soul hath too long dwelt with him that hateth peace.
120.7: I seek peace, and when I speak thereof, they are bent to war.

121.1: A song of degrees. I will lift mine eyes unto the mountaines, from whence mine help shall come.
121.2: Mine help cometh from the Lord, which hath made the heaven and the earth.
121.3: He wil not suffer thy foot to slippe: for he that keepeth thee, will not slumber.
121.4: Behold, he that keepeth Israel, wil neither slumber nor sleep.
121.5: The Lord is thy keeper: the Lord is thy shadow at thy right hand.
121.6: The sunne shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night.
121.7: The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall keep thy soul.
121.8: The Lord shall preserve thy going out, and thy coming in from henceforth and for ever.

122.1: A song of degrees, or Psalm of David. I rejoiced, when they sayd to me, We wil go into the house of the Lord.
122.2: Our feet shall stand in thy gates, O Jerusalem.
122.3: Jerusalem is builded as a citie, that is compact together in it self:
122.4: Whereunto the Tribes, even the Tribes of the Lord go up according to the testimonie to Israel, to prayse the Name of the Lord.
122.5: For there are thrones set for iudgement, even the thrones of the house of David.
122.6: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: let them prosper that love thee.
122.7: Peace be within thy walles, and prosperitie within thy palaces.
122.8: For my brethren and neighbours sakes I will wish thee now prosperitie.
122.9: Because of the House of the Lord our God, I will procure thy wealth.

123.1: A song of degrees. I lift up mine eyes to thee, that dwellest in the heavens.
123.2: Behold, as the eyes of servants look unto the hand of their masters, and as the eyes of a mayden unto the hand of her mistres: so our eyes wait upon the Lord our God until he have mercie upon us.
123.3: Have mercie upon us, O Lord, have mercie upon us: for we have suffered too much contempt.
123.4: Our soul is filled too full of ye mocking of the wealthy, and of the despitefulnes of the proud.

124.1: A song of degrees, or Psalm of David. If the Lord had not been on our side, (may Israel now say)
124.2: If the Lord had not been on our side, when men rose up against us,
124.3: They had then swallowed us up quick, when their wrath was kindled against us.
124.4: Then the waters had drowned us, and the stream had gone over our soul:
124.5: Then had the swelling waters gone over our soul.
124.6: Praysed be the Lord, which hath not given us as a pray unto their teeth.
124.7: Our soul is escaped, even as a bird out of the snare of the foulers: the snare is broken, and we are delivered.
124.8: Our help is in the Name of the Lord, which hath made heaven and earth.

125.1: A song of degrees. They that trust in the Lord, shalbe as mount Zion, which can not be remooued, but remaineth for ever.
125.2: As the mountaines are about Jerusalem: so is the Lord about his people from henceforth and for ever.
125.3: For the rod of the wicked shall not rest on the lot of the righteous, least the righteous put forth their hand unto wickednes.
125.4: Doe well, O Lord, unto those that be good and true in their hearts.
125.5: But these that turn aside by their crooked wayes, them shall the Lord lead with the workers of iniquitie: but peace shalbe upon Israel.

126.1: A song of degrees, or Psalm of David. When ye Lord brought again the captiuitie of Zion, we were like them that dream.
126.2: Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with ioye: then sayd they among the heathen, The Lord hath done great things for them.
126.3: The Lord hath done great things for us, whereof we reioyce.
126.4: O Lord, bring again our captiuitie, as the rivers in the South.
126.5: They that sow in teares, shall reap in joy.
126.6: They went weeping and caried precious seed: but they shall return with ioye and bring their sheaves.

127.1: A song of degrees, or Psalm of Salomon. Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the citie, the keeper watcheth in vain.
127.2: It is in vain for you to rise earely, and to lie down late, and eat the bread of sorow: but he wil surely give rest to his beloved.
127.3: Behold, children are the inheritance of the Lord, and the fruit of the womb his reward.
127.4: As are the arrowes in the hand of ye strong man: so are the children of youth.
127.5: Blessed is the man, that hath his quiuer full of them: for they shall not be ashamed, when they speak with their enemies in the gate.

128.1: A song of degrees. Blessed is every one that feareth the Lord and walketh in his wayes.
128.2: When thou eatest the labours of thine hands, thou shalt be blessed, and it shall be well with thee.
128.3: Thy wife shalbe as the fruitful vine on the sides of thine house, and thy children like the olive plantes round about thy table.
128.4: Lo, surely thus shall the man be blessed, that feareth the Lord.
128.5: The Lord out of Zion shall bless thee, and thou shalt see the wealth of Jerusalem all the dayes of thy life.
128.6: Yea, thou shalt see thy childrens children, and peace upon Israel.

129.1: A song of degrees. They have often times afflicted me from my youth (may Israel now say)
129.2: They have often times afflicted me from my youth: but they could not prevail against me.
129.3: The plowers plowed upon my back, and made long furrowes.
129.4: But the righteous Lord hath cut the cordes of the wicked.
129.5: They that hate Zion, shalbe all ashamed and turned backward.
129.6: They shalbe as the grass on the house tops, which withereth afore it cometh forth.
129.7: Whereof the mower filleth not his hand, neither the glainer his lap:
129.8: Neither they, which go by, say, The blessing of the Lord be upon you, or, We bless you in the Name of the Lord.

130.1: A song of degrees. Out of the deep places have I called unto thee, O Lord.
130.2: Lord, hear my voyce: let thine eares attend to the voyce of my prayers.
130.3: If thou, O Lord, straightly markest iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand?
130.4: But mercie is with thee, that thou mayest be feared.
130.5: I have waited on the Lord: my soul hath waited, and I have trusted in his word.
130.6: My soul waiteth on the Lord more then the morning watch watcheth for the morning.
130.7: Let Israel wait on the Lord: for with the Lord is mercie, and with him is great redemption.
130.8: And he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.

131.1: A song of degrees or Psalm of David. Lord, mine heart is not hautie, neither are mine eyes loftie, neither have I walked in great matters and hid from me.
131.2: Surely I have behaved my self, like one wained from his mother, and kept silence: I am in my self as one that is wained.
131.3: Let Israel wait on the Lord from hencefoorth and for ever.

132.1: A song of degrees. Lord, remember David with all his affliction.
132.2: Who sware unto the Lord, and vowed unto the mightie God of Iaakob, saying,
132.3: I will not enter into the tabernacle of mine house, nor come upon my pallet or bed,
132.4: Nor suffer mine eyes to sleep, nor mine eye lids to slumber,
132.5: Until I find out a place for the Lord, an habitation for the mightie God of Iaakob.
132.6: Lo, we heard of it in Ephrathah, and found it in the fieldes of the forest.
132.7: We will enter into his Tabernacles, and worship before his footestoole.
132.8: Arise, O Lord, to come into thy rest, thou, and the Ark of thy strength.
132.9: Let thy Priests be clothed with righteousness, and let thy Saints reioyce.
132.10: For thy servant Dauids sake refuse not the face of thine Anointed.
132.11: The Lord hath sworn in trueth unto David, and he wil not shrinke from it, saying, Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.
132.12: If thy sonnes keep my covenant, and my testimonies, that I shall teach them, their sonnes also shall sit upon thy throne for ever.
132.13: For the Lord hath chosen Zion, and loved to dwell in it, saying,
132.14: This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell, for I have a delite therein.
132.15: I will surely bless her vitailes, and will satisfie her poor with bread,
132.16: And will clothe her Priests with salvation, and her Saints shall shout for ioye.
132.17: There will I make the horn of David to bud: for I have ordeined a light for mine Anoynted.
132.18: His enemies will I clothe with shame, but on him his crown shall florish.

133.1: A song of degrees or Psalm of David. Behold, how good and how comely a thing it is, brethren to dwell even together.
133.2: It is like to the precious oyntment upon the head, that runneth down upon the beard, even unto Aarons beard, which went down on the border of his garments:
133.3: And as the dew of Hermon, which falleth upon the mountaines of Zion: for there the Lord appointed the blessing and life for ever.

134.1: A song of degrees. Behold, praise ye the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord, ye that by night stand in the house of the Lord.
134.2: Lift up your hands to the Sanctuarie, and praise the Lord.
134.3: The Lord, that hath made heaven and earth, bless thee out of Zion.

135.1: Praise ye the Lord. Praise the Name of the Lord: ye servants of the Lord, praise him.
135.2: Ye that stand in the House of the Lord, and in the courtes of the House of our God,
135.3: Praise ye the Lord: for the Lord is good: sing praises unto his Name: for it is a comely thing.
135.4: For the Lord hath chosen Iaakob to himself, and Israel for his chief treasure.
135.5: For I know that the Lord is great, and that our Lord is above all gods.
135.6: Whatsoever pleased the Lord, that did hee in heaven and in earth, in the sea, and in all the depths.
135.7: He bringeth up the cloudes from the ends of the earth, and maketh the lightnings with ye rain: he draweth foorth the wind out of his treasures.
135.8: He smote the first borne of Egypt both of man and beast.
135.9: He hath sent tokens and wonders into the middes of thee, O Egypt, upon Pharaoh, and upon all his servants.
135.10: He smote many nations, and slew mightie Kings:
135.11: As Sihon King of the Amorites, and Og King of Bashan, and all the kingdomes of Canaan:
135.12: And gave their land for an inheritance, even an inheritance unto Israel his people.
135.13: Thy Name, O Lord, endureth for ever: O Lord, thy remembrance is from generation to generation.
135.14: For the Lord will judge his people, and be pacified towardes his servants.
135.15: The idoles of the heathen are silver and gold, even the work of mens handes.
135.16: They have a mouth, and speak not: they have eyes and see not.
135.17: They have eares and hear not, neither is there any breath in their mouth.
135.18: They that make them, are like unto them: so are all that trust in them.
135.19: Praise the Lord, ye house of Israel: praise the Lord, ye house of Aaron.
135.20: Praise the Lord, ye house of Levi: ye that fear the Lord, praise the Lord.
135.21: Praised bee the Lord out of Zion, which dwelleth in Jerusalem. Praise ye the Lord.

136.1: Praise ye the Lord, because he is good: for his mercie endureth for ever.
136.2: Praise ye the God of gods: for his mercie endureth for ever.
136.3: Praise ye the Lord of lordes: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.4: Which onely doeth great wonders: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.5: Which by his wisedome made the heavens: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.6: Which hath stretched out the earth upon the waters: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.7: Which made great lightes: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.8: As the sunne to rule the day: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.9: The moon and the starres to govern the night: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.10: Which smote Egypt with their first borne, (for his mercie endureth for ever)
136.11: And brought out Israel from among them (for his mercie endureth for ever)
136.12: With a mightie hand and stretched out arm: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.13: Which deuided the red Sea in two partes: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.14: And made Israel to pass through the mids of it: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.15: And overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the red Sea: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.16: Which led his people through the wildernes: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.17: Which smote great Kings: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.18: And slew mightie Kings: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.19: As Sihon King of the Amorites: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.20: And Og the King of Bashan: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.21: And gave their land for an heritage: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.22: Even an heritage unto Israel his servant: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.23: Which remembred us in our base estate: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.24: And hath rescued us from our oppressours: for his mercie endureth for ever:
136.25: Which giveth food to all flesh: for his mercie endureth for ever.
136.26: Praise ye the God of heaven: for his mercie endureth for ever.

137.1: By the rivers of Babel we sat, and there wee wept, when we remembred Zion.
137.2: Wee hanged our harpes upon the willowes in the middes thereof.
137.3: Then they that ledde us captives, required of us songs and mirth, when wee had hanged up our harpes, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.
137.4: How shall we sing, said we, a song of the Lord in a strange land?
137.5: If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget to play.
137.6: If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth: yea, if I preferre not Jerusalem to my chief joy.
137.7: Remember the children of Edom, O Lord, in the day of Jerusalem, which said, Rase it, rase it to the foundation thereof.
137.8: O daughter of Babel, worthy to be destroyed, blessed shall he be that rewardeth thee, as thou hast served us.
137.9: Blessed shall he be that taketh and dasheth thy children against the stones.

138.1: A Psalm of David. I will praise thee with my whole heart: even before the gods will I praise thee.
138.2: I will worship toward thine holy Temple and praise thy Name, because of thy loving kindenesse and for thy trueth: for thou hast magnified thy Name above all things by thy word.
138.3: When I called, then thou heardest me, and hast encreased strength in my soul.
138.4: All the Kings of the earth shall praise thee, O Lord: for they have heard the wordes of thy mouth.
138.5: And they shall sing of the wayes of the Lord, because the glory of the Lord is great.
138.6: For the Lord is high: yet he beholdeth the lowly, but the proud he knoweth afarre off.
138.7: Though I walk in the middes of trouble, yet wilt thou revive me: thou wilt stretch foorth thine hand upon the wrath of mine enemies, and thy right hand shall save me.
138.8: The Lord will perform his work toward me: O Lord, thy mercie endureth for ever: forsake not the workes of thine handes.

139.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. O Lord, thou hast tried me and knowen me.
139.2: Thou knowest my sitting and my rising: thou understandest my thought afarre off.
139.3: Thou compassest my pathes, and my lying down, and art accustomed to all my wayes.
139.4: For there is not a word in my tongue, but loe, thou knowest it wholy, O Lord.
139.5: Thou holdest mee strait behind and before, and layest thine hand upon me.
139.6: Thy knowledge is too wonderful for mee: it is so high that I cannot attain unto it.
139.7: Whither shall I goe from thy Spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?
139.8: If I ascend into heaven, thou art there: if I lye down in hell, thou art there.
139.9: Let mee take the winges of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea:
139.10: Yet thither shall thine hand lead me, and thy right hand hold me.
139.11: If I say, Yet the darkenes shall hide me, even the night shalbe light about me.
139.12: Yea, the darkenes hideth not from thee: but the night shineth as the day: the darkenes and light are both alike.
139.13: For thou hast possessed my reines: thou hast covered me in my mothers womb.
139.14: I will praise thee, for I am fearefully and wonderously made: marueilous are thy workes, and my soul knoweth it well.
139.15: My bones are not hid from thee, though I was made in a secret place, and facioned beneath in the earth.
139.16: Thine eyes did see me, when I was without form: for in thy book were all things written, which in continuance were facioned, when there was none of them before.
139.17: How dear therefore are thy thoughtes unto me, O God! how great is ye summe of them!
139.18: If I should count them, they are moe then the sand: when I wake, I am still with thee.
139.19: Oh that thou wouldest slay, O God, the wicked and bloody men, to whom I say, Depart ye from mee:
139.20: Which speak wickedly of thee, and being thine enemies are lifted up in vain.
139.21: Doe not I hate them, O Lord, that hate thee? and doe not I earnestly contend with those that rise up against thee?
139.22: I hate them with an vnfained hatred, as they were mine utter enemies.
139.23: Try mee, O God, and know mine heart: prooue me and know my thoughtes,
139.24: And consider if there be any way of wickednes in me, and lead me in the way for ever.

140.1: To him that excelleth. A Psalm of David. Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the cruel man:
140.2: Which imagine evil things in their heart, and make war continually.
140.3: They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent: adders poyson is under their lips. Selah.
140.4: Keep mee, O Lord, from the handes of the wicked: preserve mee from the cruel man, which purposeth to cause my steppes to slide.
140.5: The proud have layde a snare for me, and spred a nette with cordes in my pathway, and set grennes for me. Selah.
140.6: Therefore I said unto the Lord, Thou art my God: hear, O Lord, the voyce of my prayers.
140.7: O Lord God the strength of my salvation, thou hast covered mine head in the day of battel.
140.8: Let not the wicked have his desire, O Lord: perform not his wicked thought, least they be proud. Selah.
140.9: As for the chief of them, that compass me about, let the mischief of their own lippes come upon them.
140.10: Let coles fal upon them: let him cast them into the fire, and into the deep pits, that they rise not.
140.11: For the backbiter shall not be established upon the earth: evil shall hunt the cruel man to destruction.
140.12: I know that the Lord will avenge the afflicted, and judge the poor.
140.13: Surely the righteous shall prayse thy Name, and the just shall dwell in thy presence.

141.1: A Psalm of David. O Lord, I call upon thee: haste thee unto me: hear my voyce, when I cry unto thee.
141.2: Let my prayer be directed in thy sight as incense, and the lifting up of mine hands as an evening sacrifice.
141.3: Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth, and keep the door of my lips.
141.4: Incline not mine heart to evil, that I should commit wicked workes with men that work iniquitie: and let me not eat of their delicates.
141.5: Let the righteous smite me: for that is a benefit: and let him reprooue me, and it shalbe a precious oyle, that shall not break mine head: for within a while I shall even pray in their miseries.
141.6: When their judges shall be cast down in stonie places, they shall hear my wordes, for they are sweet.
141.7: Our bones lye scattered at the graves mouth, as he that heweth wood or diggeth in the earth.
141.8: But mine eyes look unto thee, O Lord God: in thee is my trust: leave not my soul destitute.
141.9: Keep me from the snare, which they have layde for me, and from the grennes of the workers of iniquitie.
141.10: Let the wicked fall into his nettes together, whiles I escape.

142.1: A Psalm of David, to give instruction, and a prayer, when he was in the cave. I cryed unto the Lord with my voyce: with my voyce I prayed unto the Lord.
142.2: I powred out my meditation before him, and declared mine affliction in his presence.
142.3: Though my spirit was in perplexitie in me, yet thou knewest my path: in the way wherein I walked, have they privily layde a snare for me.
142.4: I looked upon my right hand, and beheld, but there was none that would know me: all refuge failed me, and none cared for my soul.
142.5: Then cryed I unto thee, O Lord, and sayde, thou art mine hope, and my portion in the land of the living.
142.6: Hearken unto my cry, for I am brought very low: deliver me from my persecuters, for they are too strong for me.
142.7: Bring my soul out of prison, that I may prayse thy Name: then shall the righteous come about me, when thou art beneficiall unto me.

143.1: A Psalm of David. Hear my prayer, O Lord, and hearken unto my supplication: answer me in thy trueth and in thy righteousnes.
143.2: (And enter not into iudgement with thy servant: for in thy sight shall none that liveth, be justified)
143.3: For the enemie hath persecuted my soul: he hath smitten my life down to the earth: he hath layde me in the darkenes, as they that have been dead long ago:
143.4: And my spirit was in perplexitie in me, and mine heart within me was amased.
143.5: Yet doe I remember the time past: I meditate in all thy workes, yea, I doe meditate in the workes of thine hands.
143.6: I stretch forth mine hands unto thee: my soul desireth after thee, as the thirstie land. Selah.
143.7: Hear me speedily, O Lord, for my spirit fayleth: hide not thy face from me, els I shall be like unto them that go down into the pit.
143.8: Let me hear thy loving kindenes in the morning, for in thee is my trust: shew mee the way, that I should walk in, for I lift up my soul unto thee.
143.9: Deliver me, O Lord, from mine enemies: for I hid me with thee.
143.10: Teach me to doe thy will, for thou art my God: let thy good Spirit lead me unto the land of righteousnes.
143.11: Quicken me, O Lord, for thy Names sake, and for thy righteousness bring my soul out of trouble.
143.12: And for thy mercy slay mine enemies, and destroy all them that oppress my soul: for I am thy servant.

144.1: A Psalm of David. Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth mine hands to fight, and my fingers to battell.
144.2: He is my goodnes and my fortress, my towre and my deliverer, my shield, and in him I trust, which subdueth my people under me.
144.3: Lord, what is man that thou regardest him! or the sonne of man that thou thinkest upon him!
144.4: Man is like to vanitie: his dayes are like a shadow, that vanisheth.
144.5: Bow thine heavens, O Lord, and come down: touch the mountaines and they shall smoke.
144.6: Cast forth the lightning and scatter them: shoot out thine arrowes, and consume them.
144.7: Send thine hand from above: deliver me, and take me out of the great waters, and from the hand of strangers,
144.8: Whose mouth talketh vanitie, and their right hand is a right hand of falsehood.
144.9: I wil sing a new song unto thee, O God, and sing unto thee upon a viol, and an instrument of ten strings.
144.10: It is he that giveth deliverance unto Kings, and rescueth David his servant from the hurtful sword.
144.11: Rescue me, and deliver me from the hand of strangers, whose mouth talketh vanitie, and their right hand is a right hand of falshood:
144.12: That our sonnes may be as the plantes growing up in their youth, and our daughters as the corner stones, graven after the similitude of a palace:
144.13: That our corners may be full, and abounding with divers sorts, and that our sheep may bring forth thousands and ten thousand in our streetes:
144.14: That our oxen may be strong to labour: that there be none invasion, nor going out, nor no crying in our streetes.
144.15: Blessed are the people, that be so, yea, blessed are the people, whose God is the Lord.
