145.1: A Psalm of David of Praise. O my God and King, I will extold thee, and will bless thy Name for ever and ever.
145.2: I will bless thee dayly, and prayse thy Name for ever and ever.
145.3: Great is the Lord, and most worthy to be praysed, and his greatnes is incomprehensible.
145.4: Generation shall praise thy works unto generation, and declare thy power.
145.5: I wil meditate of the beautie of thy glorious maiestie, and thy wonderful workes,
145.6: And they shall speak of the power of thy fearefull actes, and I will declare thy greatnes.
145.7: They shall break out into the mention of thy great goodnes, and shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.
145.8: The Lord is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great mercie.
145.9: The Lord is good to all, and his mercies are over all his workes.
145.10: All thy workes prayse thee, O Lord, and thy Saints bless thee.
145.11: They shew the glory of thy kingdom, and speak of thy power,
145.12: To cause his power to be knowen to the sonnes of men, and the glorious renoume of his kingdom.
145.13: Thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion endureth throughout all ages.
145.14: The Lord upholdeth all that fall, and lifteth up all that are ready to fall.
145.15: The eyes of all wait upon thee, and thou givest them their meat in due season.
145.16: Thou openest thine hand, and fillest all things living of thy good pleasure.
145.17: The Lord is righteous in all his wayes, and holy in all his workes.
145.18: The Lord is neere unto all that call upon him: yea, to all that call upon him in trueth.
145.19: He wil fulfil the desire of them that fear him: he also wil hear their cry, and wil save them.
145.20: The Lord preserveth all them that love him: but he will destroy all the wicked.
145.21: My mouth shall speak the prayse of the Lord, and all flesh shall bless his holy Name for ever and ever.

146.1: Praise ye the Lord. Praise thou the Lord, O my soul.
146.2: I will prayse the Lord during my life: as long as I have any being, I wil sing unto my God.
146.3: Put not your trust in princes, nor in the sonne of man, for there is none help in him.
146.4: His breath departeth, and he returneth to his earth: then his thoughtes perish.
146.5: Blessed is he, that hath the God of Iaakob for his help, whose hope is in the Lord his God.
146.6: Which made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that therein is: which keepeth his fidelitie for ever:
146.7: Which executeth justice for the oppressed: which giveth bread to the hungry: the Lord loseth the prisoners.
146.8: The Lord giveth sight to the blind: the Lord rayseth up the crooked: the Lord loveth the righteous.
146.9: The Lord keepeth the strangers: he relieveth the fatherless and widow: but he overthroweth the way of the wicked.
146.10: The Lord shall reign for ever: O Zion, thy God endureth from generation to generation. Prayse ye the Lord.

147.1: Praise ye the Lord, for it is good to sing unto our God: for it is a pleasant thing, and praise is comely.
147.2: The Lord doth build up Jerusalem, and gather together the dispersed of Israel.
147.3: He healeth those that are broken in heart, and bindeth up their sores.
147.4: He counteth the nomber of the starres, and calleth them all by their names.
147.5: Great is our Lord, and great is his power: his wisdom is infinite.
147.6: The Lord relieveth the meek, and abaseth the wicked to the ground.
147.7: Sing unto the Lord with prayse: sing upon the harp unto our God,
147.8: Which covereth the heaven with cloudes, and prepareth rain for the earth, and maketh the grass to grow upon the mountaines:
147.9: Which giveth to beasts their food, and to the yong ravens that crie.
147.10: He hath not pleasure in the strength of an horse, neither delighteth he in the legs of man.
147.11: But the Lord deliteth in them that fear him, and attend upon his mercie.
147.12: Prayse the Lord, O Jerusalem: prayse thy God, O Zion.
147.13: For he hath made the barres of thy gates strong, and hath blessed thy children within thee.
147.14: He setteth peace in thy borders, and satisfieth thee with the flour of wheat.
147.15: He sendeth foorth his commandement upon earth, and his word runneth very swiftly.
147.16: He giveth snow like wool, and scattereth the hoar frost like ashes.
147.17: He casteth foorth his yce like morsels: who can abide the cold thereof?
147.18: He sendeth his word and melteth them: he causeth his wind to blow, and the waters flow.
147.19: He sheweth his word unto Iaakob, his statutes and his iudgements unto Israel.
147.20: He hath not dealt so with every nation, neither have they knowen his iudgements. Prayse ye the Lord.

148.1: Praise ye the Lord. Praise ye the Lord from the heaven: prayse ye him in the high places.
148.2: Prayse ye him, all ye his Angels: praise him, all his armie.
148.3: Prayse ye him, sunne and moon: prayse ye him all bright starres.
148.4: Prayse ye him, heavens of heavens, and waters, that be above the heavens.
148.5: Let them prayse the Name of the Lord: for he commanded, and they were created.
148.6: And he hath established them for ever and ever: he hath made an ordinance, which shall not pass.
148.7: Prayse ye the Lord from the earth, ye dragons and all depths:
148.8: Fire and hayle, snow and vapours, stormie wind, which execute his word:
148.9: Mountaines and all hils, fruitful trees and all ceders:
148.10: Beasts and all cattell, creeping things and fethered foules:
148.11: Kings of the earth and all people, princes and all judges of the world:
148.12: Yong men and maidens, also old men and children:
148.13: Let them prayse the Name of the Lord: for his Name onely is to be exalted, and his prayse above the earth and the heavens.
148.14: For he hath exalted the horn of his people, which is a prayse for all his Saintes, even for the children of Israel, a people that is neere unto him. Prayse ye the Lord.

149.1: Praise ye the Lord. Sing ye unto the Lord a new song: let his prayse be heard in the Congregation of Saints.
149.2: Let Israel reioyce in him that made him, and let ye children of Zion reioyce in their King.
149.3: Let them prayse his Name with the flute: let them sing prayses unto him with the timbrel and harp.
149.4: For the Lord hath pleasure in his people: he will make the meek glorious by deliverance.
149.5: Let ye Saints be ioyfull with glorie: let them sing loud upon their beddes.
149.6: Let the high Actes of God bee in their mouth, and a two edged sword in their hands,
149.7: To execute vengeance upon the heathen, and corrections among the people:
149.8: To bind their Kings in chaines, and their nobles with fetters of yron,

19:149:7: This is chiefly accomplished in the kingdom of Christ when God’s people for just causes execute God’s judgments against his enemies: and it giveth no liberty to any to revenge their private injuries.
19:149:8: Not only the people, but the kings that were their enemies should be destroyed.
19:149:9: Hereby God bindeth the hands and minds of all his to enterprise no farther than he appointeth.
19:150:1: For his wonderful power appeareth in the firmament, which in Hebrew is called a stretching out, or spreading abroad, wherein the mighty work of God shineth.
19:150:3: Exhorting the people only to rejoice in praising God, he maketh mention of those instruments which by God’s commandment were appointed in the old Law, but under Christ the use thereof is abolished in the Church.
19:150:6: He showeth that all the order of nature is bound to this duty, and much more God’s children, who ought never to cease to praise him, till they be gathered into that kingdom, which he hath prepared for his, where they shall sing everlasting praise.
